cat > white_circle/docs/data-profile.md <<'EOF'
# Data profile: Crunchbase extract (organizations / funding_rounds / contacts)

Profiled 2026-10-29, read-only, DuckDB 1.5.5. Every column is read as `all_varchar` so nothing is silently coerced, then cast with `try_cast`.
Rows: 3,000 organizations, 1,854 funding rounds, 2,763 contacts.

**Headline.** The data is far cleaner than "raw and a little messy" suggests: no duplicate uuids or names, no orphans, no name drift, no unparseable numbers or dates, categorical values are consistent snake_case codes. The mess is elsewhere: sparsity, coded range columns, `;`-delimited multi-value columns, URL and email inconsistencies, role-level contact duplicates, and snapshot semantics that quietly mislead (acquired companies still `active`, `funding_stage` mixing two meanings). The sample is not a random Crunchbase slice: it is AI-heavy by construction (2,023 of 3,000 are AI-tagged), so "AI" is not a discriminating ICP filter on its own.

Setup used throughout (script harness in the scratchpad):
```sql
CREATE VIEW organizations AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('.../organizations.csv', all_varchar=true, header=true, sample_size=-1);
-- same for funding_rounds, contacts
```

## 1. Duplicates

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate org uuid | 0 | Still add `PRIMARY KEY (uuid)` in the staging table so a re-pull fails loudly |
| Duplicate org name (case/space-insensitive) | 0 | None; do not dedupe on name (names are not unique in real Crunchbase) |
| Duplicate website domain (scheme/www/path stripped) | 0 | Build `domain` with `regexp_replace`; use it as the secondary match key |
| Duplicate linkedin_url | 0 | None |
| Duplicate funding rounds (org, type, date, amount) | 0 | None; keep composite key `(org_uuid, investment_type, announced_on)` |
| Same org + same announce date, different rows | 21 (2 types same day, e.g. `debt_financing` + `series_a`) | Legitimate; do not dedupe on (org, date). Break ties by a stable type rank when picking "latest round" |
| Contacts: repeated (org_uuid, person_uuid) | 66 extra rows (13 also repeat title); 11 are exact title repeats with different `started_on` or identical | `QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid, person_uuid ORDER BY started_on DESC NULLS LAST) = 1`. These are multiple roles (Co-Founder then CEO), so keep a `roles` list if titles matter |
| Contacts: person_uuid in more than one org | 4 people (70 dup person_uuid rows = 66 + 4) | Legitimate (serial founders); key a person on `(org_uuid, person_uuid)` |
| Contacts: same linkedin url, different person_uuid | 0 | None |

```sql
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,person_uuid)) FROM contacts;                 -- 66
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,investment_type,announced_on)) FROM funding_rounds; -- 0
```

## 2. Join coverage

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Orgs with >= 1 round | 800 (26.7%) | LEFT JOIN from organizations, never INNER, or 73% of the universe vanishes |
| Orgs with >= 1 contact | 1,047 (34.9%); 1,007 are active | Same; "no contact" is a segment ("needs enrichment"), not an error |
| Orgs with neither rounds nor contacts | 1,697 (56.6%) | Flag `has_contact`, `has_funding` on the org-level model |
| Orgs with 0 contacts / 1 / 8+ | 1,953 / 432 / 86 | 8 looks like a cap on the export per org |
| Orphan rounds / orphan contacts | 0 / 0 | Keep as an assertion test (`NOT EXISTS`) |
| org_name differs from organizations.organization_name for same uuid | 0 / 0 | Drop the denormalised `org_name` from rounds/contacts; join for it |
| `funding_round_count` vs actual round rows | 0 mismatches (null on exactly the 2,200 orgs without rounds) | Recompute from rounds rather than trusting the column |

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM funding_rounds r WHERE r.org_uuid=o.uuid)) AS with_rounds FROM organizations o;
```

## 3. Per-column messiness

### 3a. Null / blank rates (% of rows, `NULL` or `''`)

| Table | Column | % null |
|---|---|---|
| organizations | closed_on 99.1, funding_stage 75.6, funding_total_usd 79.3, last_funding_* 73.3, funding_round_count 73.3, investor_count/names 77.6, article_count 70.9, revenue_range 60.1, contact_email 19.4, employee_count_range 18.1, founded_on 14.0, city/region/country 12.5 (identical rows), linkedin_url 11.3, company_type 2.6, website_url 0.7 | |
| funding_rounds | lead_investor_names 51.1, money_raised_usd 25.6, investor_count 21.0 | |
| contacts | started_on 22.4, person_country 10.0, person_linkedin_url 9.0 | |

Approach: treat null as "unknown", never 0. `NULLIF(trim(col),'')` at staging. Never impute revenue or employees; carry an `is_known` flag. Geography nulls are all-or-nothing (city, region, country null together, 375 rows), so one `has_geo` flag suffices.

### 3b. Categorical columns (all clean, no casing or spelling variants)

| Column | Distinct values and counts | Issue / approach |
|---|---|---|
| operating_status | active 2,928; closed 72 | Clean. Note 46 of 72 closed have no `closed_on` |
| company_type | for_profit 2,904; non_profit 17; null 79 | Map null to `'unknown'` |
| ipo_status | private 2,971; public 29 | Clean |
| employee_count_range | c_00011_00050 1,062; c_00001_00010 912; null 544; c_00051_00100 222; c_00101_00250 138; c_00251_00500 58; c_01001_05000 29; c_00501_01000 25; c_10001_max 7; c_05001_10000 3 | Coded strings; sorts lexically only by luck. Map to `emp_min`, `emp_max`, `emp_bucket_order` via a lookup CTE |
| revenue_range | null 1,803; r_00001000 762; r_00000000 215; r_00010000 151; r_00100000 28; r_00050000 26; r_01000000 7; r_00500000 5; r_10000000 3 | Codes are lower bounds, not labels (r_00001000 = $1M+, per Crunchbase). Treat as an ordinal bound; `r_00000000` is a real band (<$1M), not null. 60% null: do not use as a hard filter |
| funding_stage | null 2,268; seed 456; m_and_a 127; early_stage_venture 90; ipo 26; late_stage_venture 21; private_equity 12 | Mixes two ideas: funding maturity and exit state. 63 non-null stage rows have no rounds. Split into `funding_stage` and `exit_flag` |
| last_funding_type | null 2,200; seed 259; pre_seed 176; series_a 77; series_unknown 65; grant 30; non_equity_assistance 27; angel 23; series_b 19; private_equity 17; convertible_note 16; debt_financing 15; corporate_round 13; equity_crowdfunding 12; series_d 10; series_c 9; post_ipo_debt 9; undisclosed 6; post_ipo_equity 5; secondary_market 4; series_f 3; [REDACTED_SECRET] 1 each | Group into `equity_venture` (pre_seed..series_*), `non_dilutive` (grant, non_equity_assistance), `debt`, `public_market`, `other`. Do not treat `series_unknown` as unfunded |
| investment_type (rounds) | seed 581; pre_seed 348; series_a 172; series_unknown 161; grant 94; series_b 81; angel 69; non_equity_assistance 60; debt_financing 47; series_c 41; convertible_note 33; private_equity 25; post_ipo_equity 21; series_d 21; corporate_round 19; equity_crowdfunding 16; post_ipo_debt 15; secondary_market 12; undisclosed 10; series_e 9; series_f 7; [REDACTED_SECRET] 3 each; series_h 2; product_crowdfunding 1 | Same vocabulary as `last_funding_type` (good); one shared lookup table |
| country | 105 distinct, no case variants; US 949, null 375, UK 327, India 197, Canada 116, Germany 80, France 54, Spain 52, Brazil 46, China 45 | Crunchbase names, not ISO: "The Netherlands", "Russian Federation", "Slovakia (Slovak Republic)". Join to an ISO table with a small alias map. contacts.person_country uses the same style (null 277) |

### 3c. Money columns

| Column | Non-null | Unparseable | Negative | Zero | Min / median / p99 / max | Approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| funding_total_usd | 620 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 / 2.53M / 812M / 4.35B (Accor) | Plain doubles, no currency strings, no `$`/commas. Cast with `try_cast(... AS DOUBLE)` and assert |
| last_funding_total_usd | 559 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 / 1.66M / 285M / 1.0B | Name is misleading: it is the amount of the last round |
| money_raised_usd | 1,380 | 0 | 0 | 1 (Adzact pre_seed) | 0 / 1.84M / 283M / 3.2B | Zero is "undisclosed" not "raised $0": `NULLIF(x,0)` |

Outliers are real and come from public companies (Accor 3.2B `post_ipo_equity`, Sinch 1.13B, Wix 1.0B `post_ipo_debt`): exclude `post_ipo_*` and debt from "venture raised" metrics, and use `log10` or percentile bands for size. No sub-$1,000 amounts, so no unit (thousands vs units) problem was detectable. All amounts are USD by column name; no currency field exists, so currency cannot be verified.

### 3d. Dates

| Column | Non-null | Format | Unparseable | Future (> today) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| founded_on | 2,579 | all ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` | 0 | 0 | 1,371 (53%) are `-01-01`: year-only precision padded to Jan 1. 5 before 1900 (earliest 1833); 193 before 2000 (old incumbents, not startups) |
| closed_on | 26 | ISO | 0 | 0 | 0 closed before founded |
| last_funding_at | 800 | ISO | 0 | 0 | max 2026-06-20 (snapshot ~June 2026; 9 rounds after 2026-06-01) |
| announced_on | 1,854 | ISO | 0 | 0 | 95 are `-01-01` (year-only) |
| contacts.started_on | 2,144 | ISO | 0 | 0 | 588 are `-01-01`; 1,870 are first-of-month (month precision). 78 contacts "started" more than a year before the org was founded |

Other date checks: 11 rounds announced more than a year before the org's `founded_on`; 4 rounds announced after `closed_on`. Approach: add `founded_precision` ('year' when `-01-01`), compute ages in years only; flag impossible rows rather than deleting them.

### 3e. Delimited multi-value columns

`categories`, `category_groups`, `investor_names` are `'; '`-separated (semicolon + space, consistently: 0 rows with a bare `;`, 0 with untrimmed ends). 4 category strings contain commas (inside names such as "Gaming, ..."), so do **not** split on commas. `lead_investor_names` is free text with legal-suffix commas ("Little Bug Ventures, LLC", "..., Co., Ltd."), so it cannot be split safely. 601 distinct category tokens, no case or spelling collisions (601 raw = 601 normalised). 1-21 categories per org (mean 5.25). `investor_count` disagrees with the count of names on 440 of 672 orgs (the name list is truncated to a few names): do not recount from names.

Top 40 category tokens: Software 1,252; Artificial Intelligence (AI) 1,243; Information Technology 656; Generative AI 593; Machine Learning 403; Consulting 379; SaaS 363; Enterprise Software 311; Analytics 258; Health Care 255; Cloud Computing 239; E-Commerce 212; Financial Services 208; Digital Marketing 171; Web Development 169; Agentic AI 155; Marketing 154; Cyber Security 144; Mobile Apps 143; DevOps 134; FinTech 129; Education 123; Business Process Automation (BPA) 123; Internet 122; Advertising 121; Marketing Automation 110; Software Engineering 108; Big Data 101; Electronic Health Record (EHR) 99; Computer Vision 91; Customer Service 89; Chatbot 88; Security 87; Blockchain 86; Data Integration 86; Internet of Things 84; Developer Tools 81; Medical 79; Apps 79; Manufacturing 77.

The "inconsistent categories" are therefore semantic, not typographic: overlap and synonyms (`Cyber Security` 144 vs `Security` 87 vs `Privacy and Security` group; `Chatbot`, `Generative AI`, `Agentic AI`, `Machine Learning` overlap; `FinTech` 129 vs `Financial Services` 208 vs `Payments` 122). Approach: unnest to a bridge table `org_category(uuid, token)` and map tokens to a small curated taxonomy with a lookup table; never string-match the raw column (`LIKE '%AI%'` also hits "Fair", "Retail").

```sql
CREATE TABLE org_category AS
SELECT uuid, trim(unnest(string_split(categories, '; '))) AS category FROM organizations;
```

### 3f. Cross-column consistency

| Check | Result | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| funding_total_usd = SUM(rounds.money_raised_usd) | 620/620 agree exactly; 180 orgs with rounds have null total (all their round amounts are null); 0 disagreements | Safe to trust; for the 180, report `NULL` not 0 |
| last_funding_at = MAX(announced_on) | 800/800 agree | Safe |
| last_funding_type = type of latest round | 4 of 800 disagree (Nagomi Security series_a vs seed; Breaking Change; SumX; LogicMonitor) because two rounds share one date | Recompute from rounds with a deterministic tie-break |
| operating_status vs closed_on | 72 closed, only 26 have `closed_on`; 0 active with closed_on | Do not rely on `closed_on` to find dead companies; use `operating_status` |
| funding_stage = m_and_a but operating_status = active | 106 (plus 21 closed) | Acquired but still listed active: exclude or flag as `acquired`; they are not buyers |
| ipo_status = public but funding_stage not ipo | 3 | Trust `ipo_status` |
| tiny headcount but high revenue (1-10 emp, >= $10M band) | 7 | Low-confidence; ignore for scoring |

```sql
WITH s AS (SELECT org_uuid, sum(try_cast(money_raised_usd AS DOUBLE)) sm, max(announced_on::DATE) mx FROM funding_rounds GROUP BY 1)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE abs(o.funding_total_usd::DOUBLE - sm) >= 1) AS total_disagree,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.last_funding_at::DATE <> mx) AS date_disagree
FROM organizations o JOIN s ON s.org_uuid = o.uuid;   -- 0, 0
```

## 4. ICP-relevant signal coverage (3,000 orgs)

Regex on lower-cased `categories` and `short_description`; counts are orgs, not mentions.

| Signal | in categories | in description | either |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generative AI (`generative ai`, `genai`) | 593 | 80 | 605 |
| AI agent / agentic | 155 | 112 | 236 (pattern includes bare "agent", so an upper bound) |
| Chatbot / conversational AI / virtual assistant | 98 | 76 | 117 |
| LLM / large language model | 0 | 21 | 21 |
| NLP / natural language | 37 | 10 | 43 |
| Copilot | 0 | 7 | 7 |
| Foundation model | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Any of the above (union)** | 820 | 262 | **871 (29%)** |
| Any AI tag (AI in categories or category_groups) | | | 2,023 (67%) |
| Fintech / banking / payments / lending (cat, groups) | 420 | 72 | 429 |
| Neobank / digital bank (strict) | 0 | 6 | 6 |
| Health / medical / biotech / pharma | 363 | 221 | 383 |
| Insurance / insurtech | 47 | 28 | 50 |
| Legal / compliance | 73 | 64 | 95 |
| GenAI-signal AND fintech-signal | | | 46 |
| GenAI-signal AND health-signal | | | 40 |
| Direct guardrail / AI safety / red-team / prompt injection / responsible AI language | | | 3 (RATIONAL AI SRL, HumanLens, AceUp, per a loose match) |

Few firms say "LLM" outright (21); the vocabulary is "Generative AI" and "Agentic AI". LLM is an under-count by text, so tier on category tokens first, description second.

Last funding date by year (800 funded orgs): 2026 77; 2025 138; 2024 117; 2023 111; 2022 76; 2021 66; 2020 54; 2019 34; 2018 33; 2017 24; 2016 25; 2015 19; 2014 and earlier 36. Funded since 2024-01-01: 332; since 2025-01-01: 215; within 12 months of 2026-10-29: 98. Funding recency is coverage-limited (73% have no round at all).

Employee range (all 3,000; active-only differs by < 5%): 1-10 912; 11-50 1,062; 51-100 222; 101-250 138; 251-500 58; 501-1,000 25; 1,001-5,000 29; 5,001-10,000 3; 10,001+ 7; null 544. 66% of orgs are under 50 people, a small-company universe.

Contact titles (2,763 rows; regexes on lower-cased `job_title`, rows can match several):

| Bucket | Rows |
|---|---|
| Any C-level (`chief` or `c?o`) | 1,369 |
| Founder / co-founder / owner | 1,058 |
| CEO | 715 |
| CTO / chief technology | 270 |
| VP / Head / Director of eng, AI, ML, data, product, technology | 139 |
| AI / ML / data specific leaders (head/VP/chief) | 17 |
| Engineers / developers | 97 |
| Product | 75 |
| Sales / growth / marketing / revenue | 131 |
| Compliance / risk / legal / counsel / privacy / DPO | 26 |
| Security / CISO | 7 (orgs: 7) |
| Non-operators (board member/observer, advisor, investor) | 430-515 |

Orgs with a CEO or founder contact: 898; with a CTO or technical head: 399; with any security title: 7. The security and compliance buyer is essentially absent from this extract, so route by founder/CTO. Titles: 1,005 distinct, 947 after case-fold (58 case-only duplicates), so bucket with regex or a lookup, not exact match.

## 5. Surprises and likely traps

| Finding | Count | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Sample is AI-heavy by construction; "AI" tag is not discriminating | 2,023 AI-tagged | Score on specific signals (genai/agentic/chatbot) plus vertical, not "has AI" |
| Wrong-ICP incumbents / public majors in the list | 29 public (Accor 10k+ staff, McKesson, Experian, Dräger, Wix, Sinch, ZipRecruiter, Teledyne FLIR, Freshworks); 39 orgs with 1,000+ staff | Keep but segment as enterprise, or exclude from a startup-led model; their funding is `post_ipo_*` and distorts averages |
| Acquired companies still `operating_status = active` | 106 (127 with `m_and_a`) | Exclude from outreach: `WHERE funding_stage IS DISTINCT FROM 'm_and_a'` |
| Closed companies, some with contacts | 72 closed; 40 have contacts; 46 lack `closed_on` | Exclude by `operating_status`; no closed org has a round after 2024 |
| Non-profits | 17 | Exclude |
| `contact_email` is a generic inbox | 1,657 of 2,420 non-null (info@, hello@, contact@...); 53 freemail | Not a person: never use as a contact; flag `is_generic_inbox`. Email domain differs from the website domain on 333 of 2,415 (e.g. itadviser.dev vs itadviser.org): mismatched, so do not derive the domain from the email |
| Website URLs are inconsistent | 414 `http://`; 984 trailing slash; 46 with a path; 18 with uppercase; 4 social/profile sites; 4 with `utm_source=crunchbase` tracking | Normalise to a bare lower-case registrable domain (strip scheme, `www.`, path, query) before any dedupe or enrichment join. linkedin_url: 70 `http://`, 45 not `/company/` URLs. Contacts: 191 `http://` LinkedIn URLs, many legacy `/pub/` style |
| Truncated descriptions | 214 at 139-140 chars (cap is 140); 515 lack terminal punctuation; 7 contain non-breaking spaces | Regex on text is low-recall; strip `\xa0` and treat description as a hint, not a source |
| Name oddities | 2 with underscores (`open200_software company`, `thewall_`); 305 all-caps; 38 non-ASCII; 84 end in a legal suffix; 78 look like domains | `lower(trim(...))`, strip legal suffixes for fuzzy matching only; do not use names as keys |
| Year-only dates stored as Jan 1 | 1,371 founded_on; 588 contact starts | Add precision flag; do not compute months-since on these |
| Dates relative to snapshot | max date 2026-06-20 vs today 2026-10-29 | Pin an `as_of` constant, do not use `current_date` for recency or the answers drift every day |
| No test/placeholder rows, no injected instructions | 0 test rows ("Playtest" is a real name; two descriptions match "instruction" benignly) | None needed; keep untrusted-text handling for any LLM step that reads descriptions |
| Reference-customer lookalikes | No Lovable, no named neobanks (Revolut, Monzo, N26, Nubank, Chime, Starling all absent) | The extract is a lookalike pool, not a customer list; there is no "customer" flag to train on |

**Deliberate-trap candidates** (inference, not provable): (1) acquired-but-`active` (106) and `funding_stage` doubling as exit state; (2) generic inboxes presented as `contact_email`; (3) NULL-heavy funding/revenue so INNER JOINs silently drop 73% of orgs; (4) role-level contact duplicates (66) that inflate headcount of decision makers; (5) public giants with huge `post_ipo_*` rounds skewing money aggregates; (6) coded `r_`/`c_` ranges that look numeric but are lower bounds. The otherwise-clean keys suggest the messiness was mostly left natural rather than injected.

Profile written to white_circle/docs/data-profile.md. It is the only file written in the repo, and nothing is committed. Scripts are in the scratchpad.

The data is much cleaner than "messy on purpose" implies. There are 0 duplicate uuids, names or domains, 0 duplicate rounds, 0 orphans and 0 org_name drift. Every date is ISO and every money value is a plain double. Categorical values are consistent snake_case codes with no casing variants. funding_total_usd matches the sum of rounds on 620/620 orgs, and last_funding_at matches max(announced_on) on 800/800.

Top issues:
1. Sparsity: only 800 orgs (27%) have rounds and 1,047 (35%) have contacts. 1,697 (57%) have neither. An inner join silently drops about 73% of orgs. revenue_range is 60% null, funding_stage 76%, closed_on 99%.
2. Contacts: 66 repeated (org, person) rows, mostly multiple roles for one person. 430-515 contacts are board members, advisors or investors, not buyers.
3. Acquired companies still `active`: 106 (127 with funding_stage `m_and_a`). 72 are closed, 46 of those with no closed_on. Also 17 non-profits and 29 public companies (Accor, McKesson, Experian, Wix). Their `post_ipo_*` rounds up to $3.2B skew money aggregates.
4. contact_email: 1,657 of about 2,420 are generic inboxes (info@, hello@). 333 of 2,415 have a domain that differs from the website. Website URLs vary: 414 `http://`, 984 trailing slash, 46 with paths, 4 with utm tracking.
5. Descriptions are capped at 140 characters (214 truncated). Categories are `; `-delimited (601 distinct tokens). The inconsistency is semantic overlap (Security vs Cyber Security, FinTech vs Financial Services vs Payments), not typos.
6. Year-only dates are padded to Jan 1: 1,371 founded_on. funding_stage mixes maturity and exit state. Range columns (c_/r_) are coded lower bounds.

Signal coverage (3,000 orgs):
- 2,023 (67%) carry an AI tag, so the sample is AI-heavy by construction and "AI" doesn't discriminate.

# Data profile: Crunchbase extract (organizations / funding_rounds / contacts)

Profiled 2026-10-29, read-only, DuckDB 1.5.5. Every column is read as `all_varchar` so nothing is silently coerced, then cast with `try_cast`.
Rows: 3,000 organizations, 1,854 funding rounds, 2,763 contacts.

**Headline.** The data is far cleaner than "raw and a little messy" suggests: no duplicate uuids or names, no orphans, no name drift, no unparseable numbers or dates, categorical values are consistent snake_case codes. The mess is elsewhere: sparsity, coded range columns, `;`-delimited multi-value columns, URL and email inconsistencies, role-level contact duplicates, and snapshot semantics that quietly mislead (acquired companies still `active`, `funding_stage` mixing two meanings). The sample is not a random Crunchbase slice: it is AI-heavy by construction (2,023 of 3,000 are AI-tagged), so "AI" is not a discriminating ICP filter on its own.

Setup used throughout (script harness in the scratchpad):
```sql
CREATE VIEW organizations AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('.../organizations.csv', all_varchar=true, header=true, sample_size=-1);
-- same for funding_rounds, contacts
```

## 1. Duplicates

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate org uuid | 0 | Still add `PRIMARY KEY (uuid)` in the staging table so a re-pull fails loudly |
| Duplicate org name (case/space-insensitive) | 0 | None; do not dedupe on name (names are not unique in real Crunchbase) |
| Duplicate website domain (scheme/www/path stripped) | 0 | Build `domain` with `regexp_replace`; use it as the secondary match key |
| Duplicate linkedin_url | 0 | None |
| Duplicate funding rounds (org, type, date, amount) | 0 | None; keep composite key `(org_uuid, investment_type, announced_on)` |
| Same org + same announce date, different rows | 21 (2 types same day, e.g. `debt_financing` + `series_a`) | Legitimate; do not dedupe on (org, date). Break ties by a stable type rank when picking "latest round" |
| Contacts: repeated (org_uuid, person_uuid) | 66 extra rows (13 also repeat title); 11 are exact title repeats with different `started_on` or identical | `QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid, person_uuid ORDER BY started_on DESC NULLS LAST) = 1`. These are multiple roles (Co-Founder then CEO), so keep a `roles` list if titles matter |
| Contacts: person_uuid in more than one org | 4 people (70 dup person_uuid rows = 66 + 4) | Legitimate (serial founders); key a person on `(org_uuid, person_uuid)` |
| Contacts: same linkedin url, different person_uuid | 0 | None |

```sql
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,person_uuid)) FROM contacts;                 -- 66
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,investment_type,announced_on)) FROM funding_rounds; -- 0
```

## 2. Join coverage

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Orgs with >= 1 round | 800 (26.7%) | LEFT JOIN from organizations, never INNER, or 73% of the universe vanishes |
| Orgs with >= 1 contact | 1,047 (34.9%); 1,007 are active | Same; "no contact" is a segment ("needs enrichment"), not an error |
| Orgs with neither rounds nor contacts | 1,697 (56.6%) | Flag `has_contact`, `has_funding` on the org-level model |
| Orgs with 0 contacts / 1 / 8+ | 1,953 / 432 / 86 | 8 looks like a cap on the export per org |
| Orphan rounds / orphan contacts | 0 / 0 | Keep as an assertion test (`NOT EXISTS`) |
| org_name differs from organizations.organization_name for same uuid | 0 / 0 | Drop the denormalised `org_name` from rounds/contacts; join for it |
| `funding_round_count` vs actual round rows | 0 mismatches (null on exactly the 2,200 orgs without rounds) | Recompute from rounds rather than trusting the column |

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM funding_rounds r WHERE r.org_uuid=o.uuid)) AS with_rounds FROM organizations o;
```

## 3. Per-column messiness

### 3a. Null / blank rates (% of rows, `NULL` or `''`)

| Table | Column | % null |
|---|---|---|
| organizations | closed_on 99.1, funding_stage 75.6, funding_total_usd 79.3, last_funding_* 73.3, funding_round_count 73.3, investor_count/names 77.6, article_count 70.9, revenue_range 60.1, contact_email 19.4, employee_count_range 18.1, founded_on 14.0, city/region/country 12.5 (identical rows), linkedin_url 11.3, company_type 2.6, website_url 0.7 | |
| funding_rounds | lead_investor_names 51.1, money_raised_usd 25.6, investor_count 21.0 | |
| contacts | started_on 22.4, person_country 10.0, person_linkedin_url 9.0 | |

Approach: treat null as "unknown", never 0. `NULLIF(trim(col),'')` at staging. Never impute revenue or employees; carry an `is_known` flag. Geography nulls are all-or-nothing (city, region, country null together, 375 rows), so one `has_geo` flag suffices.

### 3b. Categorical columns (all clean, no casing or spelling variants)

| Column | Distinct values and counts | Issue / approach |
|---|---|---|
| operating_status | active 2,928; closed 72 | Clean. Note 46 of 72 closed have no `closed

# GTM Engineer — Take-Home Exercise

> Source: https://whitecircle.notion.site/GTM-Engineer-Take-Home-Exercise-38fc3dbe97908031bd22cb2d027b3f23 (copied 2026-10-29)


We’re at a critical juncture - revenue and customers, but no repeatability or playbook. Right now we have customers like Lovable and neobanks. Sales were founder-led till recently. We have started using Attio, Clay and are open to other tools as they become needed (eg. Granola for meetings where Attio cannot record, but don’t fixate on this).

Customer segmentation is not defined and we have SDRs and AEs joining soon. SDRs will be almost solely focused on cold calling, other channels should be automated for them. We want to prevent AEs from having to hunt so they can just focus on closing. Paid ads will be running in a few weeks and RB2B has been installed on our website.


---


#### Part 1 - Segmentation
*(Attachment: gtm-takehome-dataset.zip — the three CSVs in `data/raw/`)*
We've given you a slice of Crunchbase company data. It's raw and a little messy, on purpose.

Load it using the tool/tech of your choice, explore it, and use SQL to answer one question: *which companies should our AEs prioritize, and how would you group them into segments?*

- This is open-ended. You decide what "good fit" means for an AI-safety platform sold to companies deploying LLMs, and you defend it. There is no answer key.
- We want to see your SQL, not just conclusions. Show how you handle data quality issues, inconsistent categories, etc. Derive at least a few meaningful cuts (e.g. by funding stage, size, sector, recency of raise, or a fit score you construct).
- Land on a defensible set of segments (a tiered ICP, priority tiers, or similar) with rough counts for each, straight from the data.
**What to deliver:**

1. Segment the companies and build a scoring model to output a ranked top-50 account list
1. Enrich the top 5 accounts however you like (scraping, LLMs etc - your choice)
1. Write a short memo showcasing your logic for how you went about 1
1. Design the CRM data-model that you will inject those data into
1. We expect all the artifacts you wrote to be included in the submission: code, SQL, schema, notes, and we also expect you to provide your AI traces/logs

---


#### Part 2 - Systems Design
Now build the system that acts on those segments.

Build a system that automates as much of the manual work of the SDRs and AEs as you think sensible, through to close (ignore expansion etc). They qualify using MEDDPICC. Be opinionated and practical, you own this.

**Things to think about**

1. Customer segmentation
1. Enrichment of buyer personas
1. Signals
1. The tools and data sources you would connect, and what would sync back to the CRM
1. What becomes automated vs what stays human-led (and why)
1. How to keep progress transparent (so stakeholders can see what is blocked, what is next, and owners)
**What are we testing?**

- Ability to make messy reality legible, measurable, and action-driven
- Systems thinking across the GTM lifecycle
- A technical, curious mindset: comfort with data flows, automation logic, and edge cases
- Strong judgement about automation vs human decision-making
**What to deliver?**

1. A workflow diagram showing the end-to-end automation: tools, triggers, data flows, and decision points. Format is up to you.
1. A short written note (max 500 words) on what you would build first, what you would leave for later, and why.
If you have any specific questions that would potentially help you deliver a better assignment, don’t hesitate to reach out to [stefan@whitecircle.ai](mailto:stefan@whitecircle.ai).

This should take up to 3 hours.

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA = ROOT / "data"
RAW = DATA / "raw"

cat > obs.py <<'E'
"""Audit trail: every CLI run and every external API call.

Each record goes to two places: a row in DuckDB (ops.run / ops.api_call) and one
JSON line in data/logs/events.jsonl. The JSONL file survives a deleted .duckdb,
which is why both exist. Connections are opened and closed per write so the
DuckDB file is never held locked between steps.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import traceback
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import duckdb

from .paths import DB, EVENTS, ROOT

_DDL = """
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS ops;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ops.run (
  run_id VARCHAR PRIMARY KEY, command VARCHAR, args VARCHAR,
  started_at TIMESTAMP, ended_at TIMESTAMP, status VARCHAR, error VARCHAR,
  rows_written BIGINT, git_sha VARCHAR);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ops.api_call (
  run_id VARCHAR, provider VARCHAR, endpoint VARCHAR, request_summary VARCHAR,
  status_code INTEGER, latency_ms DOUBLE, credits_or_tokens DOUBLE,
  cost_usd DOUBLE, response_ref VARCHAR, called_at TIMESTAMP);
"""


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)


def _git_sha() -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"],
                             capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        return out.stdout.strip() or None
    except Exception:
        return None


def _jsonl(kind: str, rec: dict) -> None:
    EVENTS.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with EVENTS.open("a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps({"event": kind, **rec}, default=str) + "\n")


def _db(sql: str, params: list | None = None) -> None:
    DB.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB))
    try:
        con.execute(_DDL)
        con.execute(sql, params or [])
    finally:
        con.close()


class Run:
    """Handle yielded by track_run; commands add to rows_written."""

    def __init__(self, run_id: str):
        self.run_id = run_id
        self.rows_written = 0

    def add_rows(self, n: int) -> None:
        self.rows_written += int(n)


@contextmanager
def track_run(command: str, args: dict | None = None):
    run = Run(str(uuid.uuid4()))
    started = _now()
    sha = _git_sha()
    args_s = json.dumps(args or {}, default=str)
    status, error = "ok", None
    try:
        yield run
    except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - record then re-raise
        status = "error"
        error = "".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip()
        raise
    finally:
        ended = _now()
        # The DB may have just been rebuilt by the command; write the row after.
        try:
            _db("INSERT INTO ops.run VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                [run.run_id, command, args_s, started, ended, status, error,
                 run.rows_written, sha])
        except Exception as e:  # never mask the command's own outcome
            print(f"[obs] could not write ops.run: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        _jsonl("run", dict(run_id=run.run_id, command=command, args=args or {},
                           started_at=started, ended_at=ended, status=status,
                           error=error, rows_written=run.rows_written, git_sha=sha))


def record_api_call(run_id: str, provider: str, endpoint: str, request_summary: str,
                    status_code: int | None, latency_ms: float | None,
                    credits_or_tokens: float | None = None, cost_usd: float | None = None,
                    response_ref: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Log one external API call (Tavily, Anthropic, ...). Used by later enrichment steps."""
    rec = dict(run_id=run_id, provider=provider, endpoint=endpoint,
               request_summary=request_summary, status_code=status_code,
               latency_ms=latency_ms, credits_or_tokens=credits_or_tokens,
               cost_usd=cost_usd, response_ref=response_ref, called_at=_now())
    _db("INSERT INTO ops.api_call VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", list(rec.values()))
    _jsonl("api_call", rec)
E
cat > cli.py <<'E'
"""whitecircle CLI: load -> build -> dq."""
from __future__ import annotations

import duckdb
import typer
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from .obs import track_run
from .paths import DB, RAW, ROOT, SQL_DIR

[redacted line: outside-scope]
app = typer.Typer(add_completion=False, help="White Circle GTM take-home pipeline.")

# Every column is read as VARCHAR on purpose: raw is a faithful copy and nothing
# is silently coerced. Typing happens in staging with try_cast, where failures
# are visible and counted.
TABLES = ["organizations", "funding_rounds", "contacts"]


@app.command()
def load() -> None:
    """Load data/raw/*.csv into raw.* (all VARCHAR, blanks kept as NULL)."""
    with track_run("load") as run:
        DB.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB))
        try:
            con.execute("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS raw")
            for t in TABLES:
                src = RAW / f"{t}.csv"
                con.execute(
                    f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE raw.{t} AS SELECT * FROM read_csv("
                    f"'{src}', all_varchar=true, header=true, sample_size=-1)")
                n = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM raw.{t}").fetchone()[0]
                run.add_rows(n)
                typer.echo(f"raw.{t}: {n:,} rows")
        finally:
            con.close()


@app.command()
def build() -> None:
    """Run src/white_circle/sql/*.sql in numeric order (stg.*, dq.*)."""
    with track_run("build") as run:
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB))
        try:
            for f in sorted(SQL_DIR.glob("*.sql")):
                con.execute(f.read_text())
                typer.echo(f"ran {f.name}")
            for sch in ("stg", "dq"):
                for (t,) in con.execute(
                        "SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=? "
                        "AND table_type='BASE TABLE' ORDER BY 1", [sch]).fetchall():
                    n = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {sch}.{t}").fetchone()[0]
                    run.add_rows(n)
                    typer.echo(f"  {sch}.{t}: {n:,}")
        finally:
            con.close()


@app.command()
def dq() -> None:
    """Print the data-quality check table (dq.checks)."""
    with track_run("dq"):
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
        try:
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT check_name, rows_affected, action_taken, description "
                "FROM dq.checks ORDER BY ord").fetchall()
        finally:
            con.close()
        w = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
        typer.echo(f"{'check':<{w}}  {'rows':>6}  action / description")
        for name, n, action, desc in rows:
            typer.echo(f"{name:<{w}}  {n:>6,}  {action}")
            typer.echo(f"{'':<{w}}  {'':>6}    ({desc})")

-- 00_schemas.sql
-- Rebuilds the derived schemas from scratch on every `whitecircle build`.
--
--   raw  : untouched copy of the CSVs, every column VARCHAR (made by `whitecircle load`)
--   stg  : cleaned, typed, flagged tables (this folder)
--   dq   : data-quality check log, computed live from raw + stg
--   ops  : audit trail of CLI runs and API calls (NOT dropped here; see obs.py)
--
-- Dropping stg and dq makes the build idempotent: the result depends only on raw
-- and these SQL files, never on what a previous run left behind.
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS stg CASCADE;
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS dq CASCADE;
CREATE SCHEMA stg;
CREATE SCHEMA dq;
E
cat > 10_stg_organizations.sql <<'E'
-- 10_stg_organizations.sql  ->  stg.organizations  (one row per company, 3,000)
--
-- Source: raw.organizations (all VARCHAR). Principle: never delete a row here.
-- Every problem becomes a FLAG, so the scoring step later decides what to exclude
-- and the dq log can count exactly what was flagged and why.
--
-- FIXES (each one maps to a check in 90_dq_checks.sql):
--  1. Blank strings -> NULL (nullif/trim). Unknown is NULL, never 0 or ''.
--  2. domain: websites arrive as http://, https://, www., trailing slash, paths and
--     "?utm_source=crunchbase". We reduce to a bare lower-case host so it can be a
--     join key for enrichment. Four "websites" are social profiles (linkedin.com
--     etc.): that is not the company's domain, so domain is NULL and
--     website_is_social is TRUE.
--  3. Status flags. operating_status only says active/closed, but 127 companies have
--     funding_stage = 'm_and_a' (acquired); 106 of them are still 'active'. An
--     acquired company is not a buyer, so is_acquired uses BOTH columns and
--     acquired_but_active records the trap. ipo_status is trusted over funding_stage
--     for is_public (3 public companies lack funding_stage = 'ipo').
--     is_operating = none of closed / acquired / public / nonprofit.
--  4. funding_stage mixed two ideas (funding maturity AND exit state). We split it:
--     funding_stage_clean keeps only maturity (seed, early, late, PE); exit state
--     lives in is_acquired / is_public.
--  5. founded_on is year-only data padded to Jan 1 for 53% of rows. We expose
--     founded_year (safe) and founded_date_precision ('year' or 'day'); do not
--     compute month-level ages from 'year' rows. A genuine Jan 1 founding would be
--     mislabelled 'year', which is the safe direction.
--  6. employee_count_range / revenue_range are codes (c_00011_00050, r_00001000).
--     Decoded through lookups below into min/max integers and a readable label.
--     NULL stays NULL (never imputed). r_00000000 is a real band (< $1M), not null.
--     Revenue codes are band lower bounds in thousands of USD; the upper bound of
--     each band is the next band's start (Crunchbase convention, our inference).
--  7. contact_email: 'info@', 'hello@' etc. are shared inboxes, not people
--     (contact_email_is_generic); gmail & co. are freemail. The email's domain
--     differs from the website's on ~330 rows, so we never derive a domain from the
--     email; email_domain_matches_website records agreement (NULL if either side is
--     missing).
--  8. company_type NULL -> 'unknown' (79 rows).
--  9. Geography is null in all three of city/region/country together (375 rows):
--     one has_geo flag.
-- 10. short_description is capped at 140 chars by the source and has non-breaking
--     spaces; we replace U+00A0 with a space and flag description_truncated.
-- 11. categories / category_groups kept raw here; see 20_/25_ for the long form.
CREATE TABLE stg.organizations AS
WITH
emp(code, employees_min, employees_max, employees_label, employees_order) AS (VALUES
  ('c_00001_00010',     1,    10, '1-10',          1),
  ('c_00011_00050',    11,    50, '11-50',         2),
  ('c_00051_00100',    51,   100, '51-100',        3),
  ('c_00101_00250',   101,   250, '101-250',       4),
  ('c_00251_00500',   251,   500, '251-500',       5),
  ('c_00501_01000',   501,  1000, '501-1,000',     6),
  ('c_01001_05000',  1001,  5000, '1,001-5,000',   7),
  ('c_05001_10000',  5001, 10000, '5,001-10,000',  8),
  ('c_10001_max',   10001,  NULL, '10,001+',       9)),
rev(code, revenue_min_usd, revenue_max_usd, revenue_label, revenue_order) AS (VALUES
  ('r_00000000',           0,    1000000, 'under $1M',     1),
  ('r_00001000',     1000000,   10000000, '$1M-$10M',      2),
  ('r_00010000',    10000000,   50000000, '$10M-$50M',     3),
  ('r_00050000',    50000000,  100000000, '$50M-$100M',    4),
  ('r_00100000',   100000000,  500000000, '$100M-$500M',   5),
  ('r_00500000',   500000000, 1000000000, '$500M-$1B',     6),
  ('r_01000000',  1000000000,10000000000, '$1B-$10B',      7),
  ('r_10000000', 10000000000,       NULL, '$10B+',         8)),
-- local parts that mean "a shared mailbox", not a person
generic_local(lp) AS (VALUES
  ('info'),('hello'),('hi'),('hey'),('contact'),('contactus'),('support'),('sales'),
  ('team'),('admin'),('office'),('mail'),('enquiries'),('enquiry'),('inquiries'),
  ('inquiry'),('help'),('marketing'),('press'),('media'),('careers'),('jobs'),
  ('hr'),('general'),('service'),('services'),('billing'),('accounts'),('business'),
  ('partners'),('partnerships'),('founders'),('welcome'),('ask'),('connect'),('hola'),
  ('contacto'),('kontakt'),('mailbox'),('reception'),('privacy'),('legal'),('feedback'),
  ('customerservice'),('customersupport'),('bonjour'),('ciao'),('post')),
freemail(d) AS (VALUES
  ('gmail.com'),('googlemail.com'),('yahoo.com'),('hotmail.com'),('outlook.com'),
  ('live.com'),('msn.com'),('icloud.com'),('me.com'),('aol.com'),('proton.me'),
  ('protonmail.com'),('gmx.com'),('gmx.de'),('mail.com'),('yandex.com'),('yandex.ru'),
  ('qq.com'),('163.com'),('126.com'),('yahoo.co.uk'),('hotmail.co.uk'),('web.de')),
social(d) AS (VALUES
  ('linkedin.com'),('facebook.com'),('instagram.com'),('twitter.com'),('x.com'),
  ('youtube.com'),('tiktok.com'),('linktr.ee'),('medium.com'),('github.com'),
  ('crunchbase.com')),
-- step 1: blanks to NULL; step 2: peel the URL one layer at a time
base AS (
  SELECT o.*,
         nullif(trim(website_url), '')                         AS website_raw,
         nullif(trim(contact_email), '')                       AS email_raw
  FROM raw.organizations o),
dom AS (
  SELECT b.*,
    -- lower-case -> drop scheme -> drop www. -> drop path/query/fragment -> drop port
    regexp_replace(
      regexp_replace(
        regexp_replace(
          regexp_replace(lower(website_raw), '^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://', ''),
          '^www[0-9]*\.', ''),
        '[/?#].*$', ''),
      ':[0-9]+$', '')                                          AS host
  FROM base b)
SELECT
  d.uuid,
  d.organization_name,
  d.website_url,
  CASE WHEN d.host IN (SELECT d FROM social) THEN NULL
       ELSE nullif(d.host, '') END                             AS domain,
  coalesce(d.host IN (SELECT d FROM social), FALSE)            AS website_is_social,
  nullif(trim(d.linkedin_url), '')                             AS linkedin_url,
  replace(nullif(trim(d.short_description), ''), chr(160), ' ') AS short_description,
  length(d.short_description) >= 139                           AS description_truncated,
  d.categories,
  d.category_groups,

  -- status flags [REDACTED_SECRET]
  d.operating_status,
  coalesce(nullif(trim(d.company_type), ''), 'unknown')        AS company_type,
  d.ipo_status,
  (d.funding_stage = 'm_and_a' OR d.operating_status = 'acquired')            AS is_acquired,
  (d.funding_stage = 'm_and_a' AND d.operating_status = 'active')             AS acquired_but_active,
  (d.operating_status = 'closed')                              AS is_closed,
  (d.ipo_status = 'public')                                    AS is_public,
  (d.company_type = 'non_profit')                              AS is_nonprofit,
  NOT ( coalesce(d.funding_stage = 'm_and_a' OR d.operating_status = 'acquired', FALSE)
     OR coalesce(d.operating_status = 'closed', FALSE)
     OR coalesce(d.ipo_status = 'public', FALSE)
     OR coalesce(d.company_type = 'non_profit', FALSE) )       AS is_operating,
  -- maturity only; exit states are the flags above
  CASE WHEN d.funding_stage IN ('m_and_a', 'ipo') THEN NULL
       ELSE nullif(trim(d.funding_stage), '') END              AS funding_stage_clean,
  nullif(trim(d.funding_stage), '')                            AS funding_stage_raw,

  -- dates [REDACTED_SECRET]
  try_cast(d.founded_on AS DATE)                               AS founded_on,
  year(try_cast(d.founded_on AS DATE))                         AS founded_year,
  CASE WHEN d.founded_on IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN d.founded_on LIKE '%-01-01' THEN 'year' ELSE 'day' END AS founded_date_precision,
  try_cast(d.closed_on AS DATE)                                AS closed_on,

  -- size and revenue (decoded, never imputed) --------------------------------
  d.employee_count_range,
  e.employees_min, e.employees_max, e.employees_label, e.employees_order,
  d.revenue_range,
  r.revenue_min_usd, r.revenue_max_usd, r.revenue_label, r.revenue_order,

  -- geography [REDACTED_SECRET]
  nullif(trim(d.city), '')    AS city,
  nullif(trim(d.region), '')  AS region,
  nullif(trim(d.country), '') AS country,
  (nullif(trim(d.country), '') IS NOT NULL) AS has_geo,

  -- funding fields as reported by the source (the truth is rebuilt from rounds in
  -- 35_stg_org_funding.sql; these are kept for the reconciliation check) ------
  try_cast(d.funding_total_usd AS DOUBLE)       AS reported_funding_total_usd,
  nullif(trim(d.last_funding_type), '')         AS reported_last_funding_type,
  try_cast(d.last_funding_at AS DATE)           AS reported_last_funding_at,
  try_cast(d.funding_round_count AS INTEGER)    AS reported_funding_round_count,
  try_cast(d.investor_count AS INTEGER)         AS investor_count,
  try_cast(d.crunchbase_rank AS INTEGER)        AS crunchbase_rank,
  try_cast(d.article_count AS INTEGER)          AS article_count,

  -- contact email [REDACTED_SECRET]
  d.email_raw                                   AS contact_email,
  lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 1)) IN (SELECT lp FROM generic_local) AS contact_email_is_generic,
  lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 2)) IN (SELECT d FROM freemail)       AS contact_email_is_freemail,
  lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 2))        AS email_domain,
  CASE WHEN d.email_raw IS NULL OR d.host IS NULL OR d.host = '' THEN NULL
       ELSE lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 2)) = d.host
         OR lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 2)) LIKE '%.' || d.host
         OR d.host LIKE '%.' || lower(split_part(d.email_raw, '@', 2)) END AS email_domain_matches_website
FROM dom d
LEFT JOIN emp e ON e.code = d.employee_count_range
LEFT JOIN rev r ON r.code = d.revenue_range;

-- A re-pull with a duplicate uuid must fail loudly, not silently double-count.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX stg_organizations_uuid ON stg.organizations (uuid);
E

-- 25_stg_org_category.sql  ->  stg.org_category  (long form: one row per org x token)
--
-- `categories` and `category_groups` are '; '-separated strings (never split on
-- commas: four tokens contain commas inside the name). We unnest both columns,
-- trim, lower-case to a canonical form, and de-duplicate, because a token such as
-- "Software" appears in both columns for the same company.
--
-- Each row then picks up its sector and LLM-signal from the maps in 20_. A token
-- missing from the map gets sector 'other' with is_mapped = FALSE, so "mapped to a
-- real sector" and "fell through to the default" stay distinguishable.
CREATE TABLE stg.org_category AS
WITH tokens AS (
  SELECT uuid AS org_uuid,
         lower(trim(unnest(string_split(categories, '; ')))) AS category_token,
         'category' AS src
  FROM raw.organizations WHERE nullif(trim(categories), '') IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT uuid, lower(trim(unnest(string_split(category_groups, '; ')))), 'group'
  FROM raw.organizations WHERE nullif(trim(category_groups), '') IS NOT NULL),
dedup AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, category_token,
         bool_or(src = 'category') AS in_categories,
         bool_or(src = 'group')    AS in_groups
  FROM tokens WHERE category_token <> ''
  GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT d.org_uuid, d.category_token, d.in_categories, d.in_groups,
       coalesce(m.sector, 'other')           AS sector,
       coalesce(m.kind, 'horizontal')        AS sector_kind,
       (m.token IS NOT NULL)                 AS is_mapped,
       l.signal                              AS llm_signal   -- NULL = not an LLM-era tag
FROM dedup d
LEFT JOIN stg.category_map m ON m.[REDACTED_SECRET]
LEFT JOIN stg.llm_signal_token l ON l.[REDACTED_SECRET];
E

-- 30_stg_funding_rounds.sql  ->  stg.funding_rounds  (one row per round, 1,854)
--
-- FIXES:
--  1. Typing: announced_on -> DATE, amounts -> DOUBLE via try_cast; failures would
--     show up as NULLs and be counted in dq.checks (there are none today).
--  2. money_raised_usd = 0 means "amount undisclosed", not "raised $0" (one row,
--     Adzact pre_seed). amount_usd is NULLIF(x, 0); money_raised_raw_usd keeps the
--     source value so the org-level total can still be reconciled exactly.
--  3. is_post_ipo: post_ipo_equity / post_ipo_debt / post_ipo_secondary are public
--     market transactions of listed companies (Accor 3.2B, Wix 1.0B). They are not
--     venture raises and wreck any average, so every venture metric excludes them.
--  4. round_group collapses ~25 investment types into: equity_venture, non_dilutive
--     (grants, assistance), debt, public_market, other. series_unknown is a real
--     venture round of unknown letter, not "unfunded".
--  5. type_rank is a stable ordering by stage. 21 org+date pairs hold two rounds on
--     the same day (e.g. debt_financing + series_a); "latest round" breaks the tie
--     with the higher rank so the answer is deterministic (the source's own
--     last_funding_type disagreed with the latest round in 4 cases for this reason).
--  6. Date plausibility is FLAGGED, not deleted: round_before_founding (> 1 year
--     before founded_on) and round_after_close. announced_date_precision marks
--     Jan-1 padded dates.
--  7. The denormalised org_name is dropped (it never disagrees with organizations);
--     join for the name.
CREATE TABLE stg.funding_rounds AS
WITH typ(investment_type, round_group, type_rank) AS (VALUES
  ('pre_seed',               'equity_venture',  10),
  ('angel',                  'equity_venture',  12),
  ('convertible_note',       'equity_venture',  15),
  ('equity_crowdfunding',    'equity_venture',  18),
  ('seed',                   'equity_venture',  20),
  ('series_unknown',         'equity_venture',  25),
  ('series_a',               'equity_venture',  30),
  ('series_b',               'equity_venture',  40),
  ('series_c',               'equity_venture',  50),
  ('series_d',               'equity_venture',  60),
  ('series_e',               'equity_venture',  70),
  ('series_f',               'equity_venture',  80),
  ('series_g',               'equity_venture',  90),
  ('series_h',               'equity_venture', 100),
  ('grant',                  'non_dilutive',     5),
  ('non_equity_assistance',  'non_dilutive',     6),
  ('debt_financing',         'debt',            26),
  ('post_ipo_debt',          'debt',           210),
  ('corporate_round',        'other',           28),
  ('private_equity',         'other',          110),
  ('secondary_market',       'other',           27),
  ('undisclosed',            'other',            1),
  ('product_crowdfunding',   'other',            2),
  ('initial_coin_offering',  'other',            3),
  ('post_ipo_equity',        'public_market',  200),
  ('post_ipo_secondary',     'public_market',  205))
SELECT
  r.org_uuid,
  r.investment_type,
  coalesce(t.round_group, 'other')                      AS round_group,
  coalesce(t.type_rank, 0)                              AS type_rank,
  (r.investment_type LIKE 'post_ipo%')                  AS is_post_ipo,
  try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE)                      AS announced_on,
  CASE WHEN r.announced_on LIKE '%-01-01' THEN 'year' ELSE 'day' END AS announced_date_precision,
  try_cast(r.money_raised_usd AS DOUBLE)                AS money_raised_raw_usd,
  nullif(try_cast(r.money_raised_usd AS DOUBLE), 0)     AS amount_usd,
  try_cast(r.investor_count AS INTEGER)                 AS investor_count,
  nullif(trim(r.lead_investor_names), '')               AS lead_investor_names,  -- free text, not splittable
  coalesce(try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE) < o.founded_on - INTERVAL 1 YEAR, FALSE) AS round_before_founding,
  coalesce(try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE) > o.closed_on, FALSE)                    AS round_after_close
FROM raw.funding_rounds r
LEFT JOIN typ t ON t.investment_type = r.investment_type
LEFT JOIN stg.organizations o ON o.uuid = r.org_uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX stg_funding_rounds_key
  ON stg.funding_rounds (org_uuid, investment_type, announced_on);
E
cat > 35_stg_org_funding.sql <<'E'
-- 35_stg_org_funding.sql  ->  stg.org_funding  (one row per ORG, all 3,000)
--
-- Per-company funding aggregates rebuilt from the rounds, EXCLUDING post-IPO rounds
-- (public-market transactions are not venture funding, see 30_). We rebuild instead
-- of trusting organizations.funding_* because the source columns are NULL for the
-- 2,200 orgs with no rounds, and last_funding_type is wrong where two rounds share a
-- date.
--
-- Starts from organizations (LEFT JOIN) on purpose: 73% of companies have no round,
-- and an INNER JOIN would silently drop them. "No funding data" is a segment, not an
-- error: has_funding_round = FALSE, counts 0, amounts NULL (never 0).
--
-- total_funding_usd is NULL (not 0) when rounds exist but none disclosed an amount
-- (180 orgs).
--
-- Reconciliation: reported_total_usd comes from the source's funding_total_usd;
-- total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd re-sums ALL rounds with the source's raw amounts. The
-- profile showed these agree exactly for all 620 orgs that have a total, so
-- total_matches_reported = TRUE is expected; any FALSE is a re-pull regression.
CREATE TABLE stg.org_funding AS
WITH venture AS (
  SELECT * FROM stg.funding_rounds WHERE NOT is_post_ipo),
agg AS (
  SELECT org_uuid,
         count(*)                         AS round_count,
         count(amount_usd)                AS rounds_with_amount,
         sum(amount_usd)                  AS total_funding_usd,
         min(announced_on)                AS first_round_date,
         max(announced_on)                AS last_round_date
  FROM venture GROUP BY 1),
last_round AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, investment_type AS last_round_type, round_group AS last_round_group,
         amount_usd AS last_round_amount_usd
  FROM venture
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid
                             ORDER BY announced_on DESC, type_rank DESC) = 1),
post_ipo AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, count(*) AS post_ipo_round_count
  FROM stg.funding_rounds WHERE is_post_ipo GROUP BY 1),
all_raw AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, sum(money_raised_raw_usd) AS total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd,
         count(*) AS round_count_all
  FROM stg.funding_rounds GROUP BY 1)
SELECT
  o.uuid AS org_uuid,
  coalesce(a.round_count, 0)               AS round_count,
  (coalesce(a.round_count, 0) > 0)         AS has_funding_round,
  coalesce(a.rounds_with_amount, 0)        AS rounds_with_amount,
  a.total_funding_usd,
  a.first_round_date,
  a.last_round_date,
  l.last_round_type,
  l.last_round_group,
  l.last_round_amount_usd,
  coalesce(p.post_ipo_round_count, 0)      AS post_ipo_round_count,
  o.reported_funding_total_usd             AS reported_total_usd,
  ar.total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd,
  CASE WHEN o.reported_funding_total_usd IS NULL AND ar.total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd IS NULL THEN NULL
       ELSE abs(coalesce(o.reported_funding_total_usd, 0)
              - coalesce(ar.total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd, 0)) < 1 END AS total_matches_reported
FROM stg.organizations o
LEFT JOIN agg a        ON a.org_uuid  = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN last_round l ON l.org_uuid  = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN post_ipo p   ON p.org_uuid  = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN all_raw ar   ON ar.org_uuid = o.uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX stg_org_funding_org ON stg.org_funding (org_uuid);
E

-- 40_stg_contacts.sql  ->  stg.contacts  (one row per org x person)
--
-- FIXES:
--  1. De-duplication. raw.contacts has 66 extra rows where the same person holds
--     several roles at one org (Co-Founder, then CEO). The key is (org_uuid,
--     person_uuid), NOT person_uuid alone: 4 people legitimately appear at two orgs
--     (serial founders). We keep one row per key; job_title is the most recent role
--     (latest started_on), and `roles` keeps every distinct title joined with ' | '.
--  2. title_bucket. 1,005 distinct titles (947 after case-folding) cannot be matched
--     exactly, so each role is classified by ordered regex rules (first match wins):
--        board_advisor_investor  titles that START with board/advisor/investor/...
--        security                CISO, Chief Security Officer, Head/VP/Director of Security
--        compliance_risk_legal   Chief Compliance/Risk/Legal/Privacy, General Counsel, DPO
--        ceo_founder             CEO, Chief Executive, Founder/Co-founder, Owner
--        cto_eng_leader          CTO, Chief Technology/Technical, VP/Head/Director of Eng
--        ai_ml_leader            Chief/Head/VP/Director/Lead of AI, ML, Data
--        product_leader          CPO, Head/VP/Director of Product
[redacted line: denylist]
--        board_advisor_investor  (again, last) any remaining board/advisor/investor word
--        other                   engineers, sales, individual contributors...
--     Security and compliance rules run BEFORE ceo_founder so "Founder & CISO" is a
--     security contact. The rules favour the strong, unambiguous patterns; a rare
--     misfire (e.g. "Advisor to the CEO") is accepted over a fuzzy model.
--     A person with several roles gets the bucket with the best priority (prio).
--  3. is_buyer_persona = bucket in the six roles that could own an AI-safety
--     purchase. is_non_buyer flags board/advisor/investor people (430-515 rows in
--     the profile): they are on the cap table or in the room but do not sign.
--     other_exec (CFO, COO, sales heads) is neither: not a buyer, not excluded.
--  4. Dates: started_on typed; started_date_precision is 'year' for Jan-1 padding,
--     'month' for first-of-month, else 'day'. started_before_founding flags starts
--     more than a year before the org's founded_on (78 rows): flagged, not deleted.
--  5. LinkedIn URLs: http:// upgraded to https://; legacy /pub/ style flagged.
--  6. org_name / person_country kept as given; org_name is dropped (join for it).
CREATE TABLE stg.contacts AS
WITH roles AS (
  SELECT
    c.org_uuid, c.person_uuid, c.person_name,
    trim(c.job_title) AS job_title,
    try_cast(c.started_on AS DATE) AS started_on,
    c.started_on AS started_raw,
    nullif(trim(c.person_linkedin_url), '') AS li,
    nullif(trim(c.person_country), '') AS person_country,
    lower(trim(c.job_title)) AS t
  FROM raw.contacts c),
classified AS (
  SELECT r.*,
    CASE
      WHEN t ~ '^(board|advis|investor|observer|mentor|angel|venture|limited partner)' THEN 'board_advisor_investor'
[redacted line: denylist]
      WHEN t ~ '\bceo\b|chief executive|founder|\bowner\b' THEN 'ceo_founder'
[redacted line: denylist]
      WHEN t ~ 'board|advis|investor|observer|mentor' THEN 'board_advisor_investor'
      ELSE 'other' END AS role_bucket
  FROM roles r),
ranked AS (
  SELECT k.*,
    -- lower number = more relevant to the AI-safety purchase; used to pick one bucket per person
    CASE role_bucket WHEN 'security' THEN 1 WHEN 'compliance_risk_legal' THEN 2
      WHEN 'ai_ml_leader' THEN 3 WHEN 'cto_eng_leader' THEN 4 WHEN 'ceo_founder' THEN 5
      WHEN 'product_leader' THEN 6 WHEN 'other_exec' THEN 7 WHEN 'other' THEN 8
      ELSE 9 END AS prio,
    row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid, person_uuid
                       ORDER BY started_on DESC NULLS LAST, job_title) AS rn
  FROM classified k),
person AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, person_uuid,
    any_value(person_name)  FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS person_name,
    any_value(job_title)    FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS job_title,
    string_agg(DISTINCT job_title, ' | ' ORDER BY job_title) AS roles,
    count(*)                                      AS role_count,
    any_value(started_on)   FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS started_on,
    any_value(started_raw)  FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS started_raw,
    any_value(li)           FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS li,
    any_value(person_country) FILTER (WHERE rn = 1) AS person_country,
    arg_min(role_bucket, prio)                    AS title_bucket
  FROM ranked GROUP BY 1, 2)
SELECT
  p.org_uuid, p.person_uuid, p.person_name, p.job_title, p.roles, p.role_count,
  p.title_bucket,
  p.title_bucket IN ('ceo_founder','cto_eng_leader','ai_ml_leader','product_leader',
                     'security','compliance_risk_legal')   AS is_buyer_persona,
  (p.title_bucket = 'board_advisor_investor')              AS is_non_buyer,
  p.started_on,
  CASE WHEN p.started_on IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN p.started_raw LIKE '%-01-01' THEN 'year'
       WHEN p.started_raw LIKE '%-01' THEN 'month' ELSE 'day' END AS started_date_precision,
  coalesce(p.started_on < o.founded_on - INTERVAL 1 YEAR, FALSE)  AS started_before_founding,
  regexp_replace(p.li, '^http://', 'https://')             AS person_linkedin_url,
  coalesce(p.li LIKE '%/pub/%', FALSE)                     AS linkedin_is_legacy_pub,
  p.person_country
FROM person p
LEFT JOIN stg.organizations o ON o.uuid = p.org_uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX stg_contacts_key ON stg.contacts (org_uuid, person_uuid);
E

-- 90_dq_checks.sql  ->  dq.checks  (one row per check, computed live)
--
-- The machine-checked data-quality log. Every number is a SELECT over raw.* or
-- stg.*, so it cannot drift from the data. Each row says what was looked at, how
-- many rows are affected, and what the pipeline did about it. Nothing here is
-- hard-coded: if the CSVs change, the counts change on the next `build`.
--
-- Convention: rows_affected = 0 on a "should never happen" check (duplicate keys,
-- orphans, reconciliation breaks) is the PASS state. A non-zero there means a re-pull
-- broke an assumption and the build output should not be trusted until looked at.
--
-- Sections: 1 keys & joins | 2 organizations | 3 funding | 4 contacts | 5 categories
CREATE TABLE dq.checks AS
WITH
o AS (SELECT * FROM stg.organizations),
raw_o AS (SELECT * FROM raw.organizations),
r AS (SELECT * FROM stg.funding_rounds),
f AS (SELECT * FROM stg.org_funding),
c AS (SELECT * FROM stg.contacts),
oc AS (SELECT * FROM stg.org_category),
checks(ord, check_name, description, rows_affected, action_taken) AS (
  -- 1. keys & joins [REDACTED_SECRET]
  SELECT 101, 'org_duplicate_uuid', 'Companies sharing a uuid',
    (SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT uuid) FROM raw_o),
    'None needed (0 = pass). Unique index on stg.organizations(uuid) fails the build if a re-pull duplicates'
  UNION ALL SELECT 102, 'org_duplicate_domain', 'Companies sharing a normalised website domain',
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(n), 0) FROM (SELECT count(*) n FROM o WHERE domain IS NOT NULL GROUP BY domain HAVING count(*) > 1)),
    'None needed (0 = pass). Names are not unique keys in real Crunchbase, so we never dedupe on name'
  UNION ALL SELECT 103, 'orphan_rounds', 'Funding rounds whose org_uuid is not in organizations',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM raw.funding_rounds x WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM raw_o WHERE uuid = x.org_uuid)),
    'None needed (0 = pass); kept as an assertion'
  UNION ALL SELECT 104, 'orphan_contacts', 'Contacts whose org_uuid is not in organizations',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM raw.contacts x WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM raw_o WHERE uuid = x.org_uuid)),
    'None needed (0 = pass); kept as an assertion'
  UNION ALL SELECT 105, 'org_without_funding_round', 'Companies with no funding round (join coverage gap)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM f WHERE NOT has_funding_round),
    'LEFT JOIN from organizations everywhere; "no funding data" is a segment, never dropped'
  UNION ALL SELECT 106, 'org_without_contact', 'Companies with no contact row (join coverage gap)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM c WHERE c.org_uuid = o.uuid)),
    'Kept; becomes the "needs enrichment" segment'
  UNION ALL SELECT 107, 'org_round_count_mismatch', 'Source funding_round_count differs from the actual number of round rows (NULL counted as 0)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o JOIN f ON f.org_uuid = o.uuid
      WHERE coalesce(o.reported_funding_round_count, 0) <> (f.round_count + f.post_ipo_round_count)),
    'Recomputed from rounds; the source column is ignored'

  -- 2. organizations [REDACTED_SECRET]
  UNION ALL SELECT 201, 'org_website_not_clean', 'Raw website_url was not already a bare https://domain (scheme, www, trailing slash, path, query or upper case)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE website_url IS NOT NULL AND domain IS NOT NULL AND website_url <> 'https://' || domain),
    'domain column = lower-case host with scheme, www, path, query and port stripped'
  UNION ALL SELECT 202, 'org_website_tracking_params', 'Website URLs carrying utm_* tracking parameters',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE website_url ILIKE '%utm_%'),
    'Query string stripped when building domain'
  UNION ALL SELECT 203, 'org_website_social_profile', 'Website is a social / free-hosted profile page, not the company domain',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE website_is_social),
    'domain set to NULL, website_is_social = TRUE (so it cannot be used as an enrichment key)'
  UNION ALL SELECT 204, 'org_website_missing', 'No website at all',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM raw_o WHERE nullif(trim(website_url), '') IS NULL),
    'domain NULL; enrichment must fall back to name + linkedin_url'
  UNION ALL SELECT 205, 'org_acquired_but_active', 'funding_stage = m_and_a while operating_status still says active (acquired, not a buyer)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE acquired_but_active),
    'is_acquired = TRUE, so is_operating = FALSE; excluded from outreach'
  UNION ALL SELECT 206, 'org_acquired_total', 'All acquired companies (m_and_a stage)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_acquired),
    'Flagged is_acquired'
  UNION ALL SELECT 207, 'org_closed', 'operating_status = closed',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_closed),
    'is_closed = TRUE, excluded from is_operating'
  UNION ALL SELECT 208, 'org_closed_without_closed_on', 'Closed companies with no closed_on date',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_closed AND closed_on IS NULL),
    'Use operating_status, never closed_on, to find dead companies'
  UNION ALL SELECT 209, 'org_nonprofit', 'company_type = non_profit',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_nonprofit),
    'is_nonprofit = TRUE, excluded from is_operating'
  UNION ALL SELECT 210, 'org_public', 'ipo_status = public (enterprise incumbents, post-IPO rounds)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_public),
    'is_public = TRUE, excluded from is_operating; kept so an enterprise segment is possible'
  UNION ALL SELECT 211, 'org_public_without_ipo_stage', 'ipo_status = public but funding_stage is not ipo',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE is_public AND coalesce(funding_stage_raw, '') <> 'ipo'),
    'Trust ipo_status over funding_stage'
  UNION ALL SELECT 212, 'org_funding_stage_mixed_meaning', 'funding_stage holds an exit state (m_and_a / ipo) instead of a maturity',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE funding_stage_raw IN ('m_and_a', 'ipo')),
    'Split: funding_stage_clean = maturity only; exit state lives in is_acquired / is_public'
  UNION ALL SELECT 213, 'org_funding_stage_without_rounds', 'funding_stage is set but the company has no funding rounds',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o JOIN f ON f.org_uuid = o.uuid
      WHERE o.funding_stage_raw IS NOT NULL AND f.round_count + f.post_ipo_round_count = 0),
    'Kept as reported; stage is not used as proof of funding. Funding facts come from rounds only'
  UNION ALL SELECT 214, 'org_company_type_null', 'company_type is NULL',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM raw_o WHERE nullif(trim(company_type), '') IS NULL),
    'Mapped to the explicit value ''unknown'''
  UNION ALL SELECT 215, 'org_founded_year_only', 'founded_on is Jan 1 (year-only precision padded to a full date)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE founded_date_precision = 'year'),
    'founded_date_precision = ''year''; use founded_year only, no month-level ages'
  UNION ALL SELECT 216, 'org_founded_missing', 'founded_on is NULL',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE founded_on IS NULL),
    'Left NULL; never imputed'
  UNION ALL SELECT 217, 'org_founded_before_1900', 'founded_on before 1900 (old incumbents, not startups)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM o WHERE founded_year < 1900),
    'Kept; age-based scoring must not treat these as startups'
  UNION ALL SELECT 218, 'org_unparseable_dates_or_numbers', 'Non-empty founded_on / closed_on / funding_total_usd values that failed try_cast',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM raw_o WHERE (nullif(trim(founded_on), '') IS NOT NULL AND try_cast(founded_on AS DATE) IS NULL)

Scaffold, raw/staging layer and logging are built in `white_circle`. From scratch (only the .duckdb deleted), `uv sync`, `load`, `build` and `dq` all ran clean. Nothing was committed and nothing outside `white_circle/` was touched.

**Files**
- Root: `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `Makefile`, `.env.example`, `.gitignore`.
- `src/white_circle/`: `cli.py` (`whitecircle` with `load`, `build`, `dq`), `obs.py`, `paths.py`.
- `src/white_circle/sql/`: `00_schemas`, `10_stg_organizations`, `20_stg_category_map`, `25_stg_org_category`, `30_stg_funding_rounds`, `35_stg_org_funding`, `40_stg_contacts`, `90_dq_checks`. Each header explains every fix and why.
- Logging goes to `ops.run`, `ops.api_call` and `data/logs/events.jsonl`. `load`, `build` and `dq` are wired through it. `record_api_call()` is ready for the later Tavily/Anthropic steps and has not been exercised yet.
- `stg` row counts: organizations 3,000; org_funding 3,000; funding_rounds 1,854; contacts 2,697; org_category 27,500; category_map 222 tokens.

**Category map coverage:** 94.2% of org-category rows are in the map (25,905 of 27,500). The 400 unmapped tokens default to `other`.

**dq.checks** has 62 rows. Key counts:
- Passes at 0: duplicate uuid, duplicate domain, orphan rounds, orphan contacts, round-count mismatch, funding-total reconciliation, unparseable values, unknown codes.
- Orgs with no funding round 2,200; with no contact 1,953.
- Acquired but still active 106 (127 acquired in total); closed 72; closed without `closed_on` 46; non-profit 17; public 29.
- Founded date padded to Jan 1: 1,371; revenue range null 1,803; employee range null 544; no geography 375.
- Generic inbox 1,877; email domain differs from website 315; website not clean 2,138; truncated descriptions 214.
- Post-IPO rounds 39; rounds with no disclosed amount 475; orgs with rounds but no disclosed total 181; same-day round pairs 21.
- Contact role duplicates collapsed 66; board/advisor/investor contacts 408; LLM-era category token present on 825 orgs.

**For you to review**
- **Social websites:** only 1 website is detected as social (a sites.google.com page), against 4 in the profile.
- **Generic inboxes:** my local-part list gives 1,877, against 1,657 in the profile. It also counts `founders@`, `connect@`, `contato@` and similar.
- **Domain subdomains:** the email-matches-website flag allows subdomains, so mismatches are 315 against the profile's 333.
- **Taxonomy:** I added `generic_tech` (Software, SaaS, Mobile and similar) and `business_services`, plus a vertical/horizontal flag, because AI is on 67% of rows. `fraud detection` is mapped to fintech and `government` and `public safety` to `legal_compliance`. The LLM-signal set does not include plain "Machine Learning" or "AI".
- **Revenue bands:** upper bounds follow Crunchbase convention, which is my inference.
- **Contact buckets:** the CTO rule runs before CEO, so "Co-Founder & CTO" lands in `cto_eng_leader`. Buyer personas are six buckets; `other_exec` is neither buyer nor non-buyer.
- **Post-IPO funding:** `stg.org_funding` excludes post-IPO rounds, and the reconciliation against the source total uses all rounds.
- **Contacts dedup:** it runs after bucketing, so contact-date flags are slightly below the profile (574 against 588, 63 against 78).
- **Git SHA:** `git_sha` is the parent repo's HEAD, since `white_circle` has no repo of its own.

text:
# GTM Engineer — Take-Home Exercise

> Source: https://whitecircle.notion.site/GTM-Engineer-Take-Home-Exercise-38fc3dbe97908031bd22cb2d027b3f23 (copied 2026-10-29)


We’re at a critical juncture - revenue and customers, but no repeatability or playbook. Right now we have customers like Lovable and neobanks. Sales were founder-led till recently. We have started using Attio, Clay and are open to other tools as they become needed (eg. Granola for meetings where Attio cannot record, but don’t fixate on this).

Customer segmentation is not defined and we have SDRs and AEs joining soon. SDRs will be almost solely focused on cold calling, other channels should be automated for them. We want to prevent AEs from having to hunt so they can just focus on closing. Paid ads will be running in a few weeks and RB2B has been installed on our website.


---


#### Part 1 - Segmentation
*(Attachment: gtm-takehome-dataset.zip — the three CSVs in `data/raw/`)*
We've given you a slice of Crunchbase company data. It's raw and a little messy, on purpose.

Load it using the tool/tech of your choice, explore it, and use SQL to answer one question: *which companies should our AEs prioritize, and how would you group them into segments?*

- This is open-ended. You decide what "good fit" means for an AI-safety platform sold to companies deploying LLMs, and you defend it. There is no answer key.
- We want to see your SQL, not just conclusions. Show how you handle data quality issues, inconsistent categories, etc. Derive at least a few meaningful cuts (e.g. by funding stage, size, sector, recency of raise, or a fit score you construct).
- Land on a defensible set of segments (a tiered ICP, priority tiers, or similar) with rough counts for each, straight from the data.
**What to deliver:**

1. Segment the companies and build a scoring model to output a ranked top-50 account list
1. Enrich the top 5 accounts however you like (scraping, LLMs etc - your choice)
1. Write a short memo showcasing your logic for how you went about 1
1. Design the CRM data-model that you will inject those data into
1. We expect all the artifacts you wrote to be included in the submission: code, SQL, schema, notes, and we also expect you to provide your AI traces/logs

---


#### Part 2 - Systems Design
Now build the system that acts on those segments.

Build a system that automates as much of the manual work of the SDRs and AEs as you think sensible, through to close (ignore expansion etc). They qualify using MEDDPICC. Be opinionated and practical, you own this.

**Things to think about**

1. Customer segmentation
1. Enrichment of buyer personas
1. Signals
1. The tools and data sources you would connect, and what would sync back to the CRM
1. What becomes automated vs what stays human-led (and why)
1. How to keep progress transparent (so stakeholders can see what is blocked, what is next, and owners)
**What are we testing?**

- Ability to make messy reality legible, measurable, and action-driven
- Systems thinking across the GTM lifecycle
- A technical, curious mindset: comfort with data flows, automation logic, and edge cases
- Strong judgement about automation vs human decision-making
**What to deliver?**

1. A workflow diagram showing the end-to-end automation: tools, triggers, data flows, and decision points. Format is up to you.

name: WebFetch
text:
**Deal standard attributes** (writeable, slug in parentheses):

- **Name** (`name`): Text. **Required.**
- **Deal stage** (`stage`): Status. **Required.** Defaults to Lead, In Progress, Won, and Lost, but workspaces can configure these options.
- **Deal owner** (`owner`): Actor reference. **Required.**
- **Deal value** (`value`): Currency. Defaults to USD, which can be changed.
- **Associated people** (`associated_people`): Record reference. A relationship that is the inverse of `Person -> associated_deals`.
- **Associated company** (`associated_company`): Record reference. A relationship that is the inverse of `Company -> associated_deals`.

**Notes on required fields:** Name, Deal stage, and Deal owner must be set. The other attributes are optional.

**Other notes:**
- The Deal object is disabled by default. A workspace admin must enable it in the objects settings.
- Deals have no unique attribute by default. Docs recommend adding one, such as an ID from your own system, to use as the matching attribute. A non-unique matching attribute also works, but a value that matches more than one deal is rejected.

--  2. title_bucket. 1,005 distinct titles (947 after case-folding) cannot be matched
--     exactly, so each role is classified by ordered regex rules (first match wins):
--        board_advisor_investor  titles that START with board/advisor/investor/...
--        security                CISO, Chief Security Officer, Head/VP/Director of Security
--        compliance_risk_legal   Chief Compliance/Risk/Legal/Privacy, General Counsel, DPO

--        other                   engineers, sales, individual contributors...

--     "Co-Founder & CTO" lands on the specialist bucket, not the generic founder one. The rules favour the strong, unambiguous patterns; a rare

--     A person with several roles gets the bucket with the best priority (prio).
--  3. is_buyer_persona = bucket in the six roles that could own an AI-safety

[redacted line: denylist]

[redacted line: denylist]
