Exit code 1
# GTM Engineer — Take-Home Exercise

> Source: https://whitecircle.notion.site/GTM-Engineer-Take-Home-Exercise-38fc3dbe97908031bd22cb2d027b3f23 (copied 2026-10-29)


We’re at a critical juncture - revenue and customers, but no repeatability or playbook. Right now we have customers like Lovable and neobanks. Sales were founder-led till recently. We have started using Attio, Clay and are open to other tools as they become needed (eg. Granola for meetings where Attio cannot record, but don’t fixate on this).

Customer segmentation is not defined and we have SDRs and AEs joining soon. SDRs will be almost solely focused on cold calling, other channels should be automated for them. We want to prevent AEs from having to hunt so they can just focus on closing. Paid ads will be running in a few weeks and RB2B has been installed on our website.


---


#### Part 1 - Segmentation
*(Attachment: gtm-takehome-dataset.zip — the three CSVs in `data/raw/`)*
We've given you a slice of Crunchbase company data. It's raw and a little messy, on purpose.

Load it using the tool/tech of your choice, explore it, and use SQL to answer one question: *which companies should our AEs prioritize, and how would you group them into segments?*

- This is open-ended. You decide what "good fit" means for an AI-safety platform sold to companies deploying LLMs, and you defend it. There is no answer key.
- We want to see your SQL, not just conclusions. Show how you handle data quality issues, inconsistent categories, etc. Derive at least a few meaningful cuts (e.g. by funding stage, size, sector, recency of raise, or a fit score you construct).
- Land on a defensible set of segments (a tiered ICP, priority tiers, or similar) with rough counts for each, straight from the data.
**What to deliver:**

1. Segment the companies and build a scoring model to output a ranked top-50 account list
1. Enrich the top 5 accounts however you like (scraping, LLMs etc - your choice)
1. Write a short memo showcasing your logic for how you went about 1
1. Design the CRM data-model that you will inject those data into
1. We expect all the artifacts you wrote to be included in the submission: code, SQL, schema, notes, and we also expect you to provide your AI traces/logs

---


#### Part 2 - Systems Design
Now build the system that acts on those segments.

Build a system that automates as much of the manual work of the SDRs and AEs as you think sensible, through to close (ignore expansion etc). They qualify using MEDDPICC. Be opinionated and practical, you own this.

**Things to think about**

1. Customer segmentation
1. Enrichment of buyer personas
1. Signals
1. The tools and data sources you would connect, and what would sync back to the CRM
1. What becomes automated vs what stays human-led (and why)
1. How to keep progress transparent (so stakeholders can see what is blocked, what is next, and owners)
**What are we testing?**

- Ability to make messy reality legible, measurable, and action-driven
- Systems thinking across the GTM lifecycle
- A technical, curious mindset: comfort with data flows, automation logic, and edge cases
- Strong judgement about automation vs human decision-making
**What to deliver?**

1. A workflow diagram showing the end-to-end automation: tools, triggers, data flows, and decision points. Format is up to you.
1. A short written note (max 500 words) on what you would build first, what you would leave for later, and why.
If you have any specific questions that would potentially help you deliver a better assignment, don’t hesitate to reach out to [stefan@whitecircle.ai](mailto:stefan@whitecircle.ai).

This should take up to 3 hours.

Files written:
- `white_circle/docs/part2-system-design.md` has the Mermaid flowchart, section (b) and the appendix tables. The appendix covers triggers/SLAs, Attio sync-back fields with overwrite rules, automated vs human with why, edge cases and metrics.
- `white_circle/docs/dashboard/workflow.svg` has six swimlanes, automated steps solid, human steps dashed amber, a legend and a feedback loop. It parses as XML and I checked the render in headless Chrome. It uses currentColor plus one `--wf-human` variable with a fallback, `min-width` 1100px so it scrolls on a phone, and no fonts or scripts.

Section (b) is 370 words by `wc -w` (cap 500). I did not run the Mermaid block through a renderer, so check it once.

Three most opinionated calls:
1. Hot inbound events bypass the nightly scoring run and go straight to the AE (drawn as its own arrow). The ads depend on that 5-minute path, so it ships before the ads launch.
2. MEDDPICC drafts write only to `*_draft` fields, and only AE-confirmed fields count at stage gates. Deal creation stays human to protect the forecast.
3. EU/UK RB2B visitors are company-level signals only. Cold email there needs a documented legitimate-interest assessment and a suppression check, and a call or LinkedIn goes first when unsure.

Gaps in the architecture:
- "Automated background touches" conflicts with "first personal touch on Tier 1 is human". I resolved it by holding Tier 1 sequences until the SDR's first call.
- The architecture never decides on a dialer or on call-consent rules by country. Both matter for a Paris-based company.
- It has no suppression or opt-out list and no data-retention rule.
- There is no rule for what happens to an Nth ad lead from an account that is already in a deal.
- An SLA for an AE who doesn't act on a hot alert was missing. I added reassign to the backup after 15 minutes.
- Scoring SQL can't decay signals on its own, so signal decay needs a runtime that reads the signals table.

-- 70_mart_segments.sql  ->  mart.tier_cutoff, mart.org_segment, mart.top50
--
-- Two separate questions, answered separately:
--   SEGMENT = WHO they are (what kind of buyer, which play to run). Rule-based, so an
--             AE can explain it in one breath. Does not use the score.
--   TIER    = HOW SOON to work them. Cut from fit_score. Only for the core universe.
--
-- Segments (core universe only, first match wins)
--   Regulated GenAI        strong LLM product AND regulated sector. The thesis
--                          account: ships generative output where a bad answer is a
--                          compliance event. Work first.
--   AI-native builders     strong LLM, not regulated. The Lovable lookalikes: the
--                          pain is reputation, jailbreaks and enterprise security
--                          reviews, not a regulator.
--   Regulated AI-adjacent  regulated (the narrow v2 definition), but only NLP / generic
--                          ML. The neobank lookalikes before they ship an LLM feature:
--                          nurture, and re-score when a signal appears. Tier 3 at best.
--   Low fit                everything else with some AI signal: not regulated and no
--                          LLM product.
--   Not deploying AI       v2: llm_level = 'none', whatever the sector. No AI signal
--                          in categories or description, so there is nothing to put a
--                          guardrail on (the owner doubts a traditional bank fits).
--                          Checked first, so it is never folded into Low fit.
-- Everyone else (outside the core universe) gets a named group instead of a segment, so nobody is silently
-- dropped and nobody out-of-universe is mixed in: Enterprise (public companies, a
-- different sales motion), Competitor (guardrail / AI-safety vendors: partner or
-- competitor, not AE targets), Out: closed or acquired, Out: nonprofit. Their tier
-- is NULL.
--
-- Tier = the tier the score earns, then capped by GATES (v2). A gate can only push a
-- company DOWN, never up, and the score itself is untouched:
--   * No AI signal (llm_level = 'none')            -> Nurture, not in the top 50
--   * Services firm (agency / consultancy / dev shop) -> Tier 3 at most, not in the top 50
--   * Regulated AI-adjacent (NLP / ML only)        -> Tier 3 at most
--   * Known headcount 1-10                         -> Tier 2 at most (unknown headcount
--                                                     is NOT gated: missing data = neutral)
-- tier_by_score and tier_cap_reason are kept next to tier so an AE can see why a
-- high score is not Tier 1.
--
-- Tier cutoffs (fit_score of core orgs, 0-100)
--   Tier 1   >= 65   AE works these now
--   Tier 2   52-64   SDR sequence, AE joins on reply
--   Tier 3   42-51   automated nurture, promote on a trigger (new round, hire)
--   Nurture  < 42    watch list; re-score monthly
-- WHY these numbers (v2 re-pick; v1 used 75/60/50 on a different distribution). The
-- scale changed (base 100, regulated points now gated by LLM exposure) and so did the
-- population: the gates remove about a third of the old top band (no-AI orgs, services
-- firms, 1-10 headcount, AI-adjacent), so the cutoff has to sit lower to leave a Tier 1
-- an AE team of ~3 can work in a quarter. The aim was 50-100 Tier 1 accounts.
--   * Score >= 65 holds 53 accounts AFTER the gates (about 115 before them). 70 would
--     leave 36, too few to staff; 62 gives 67 and 60 gives 79, all still fine, but the
--     histogram has no gap to anchor on (the score is a sum of many small pieces), so
--     the choice is "the lowest round number that keeps the AE list worth reading".
--   * Below 42 the count of scoring orgs per 3-point band roughly doubles (166 at 42-44,
--     then 126 at 36-38): that is the large "AI-tagged, unremarkable" bulge. 42 is the
--     last point before it; Tier 3 (42-51) is the companies with some real signal.
--   * 52 splits the 42-64 band so Tier 2 (about 200) is the SDR sequence and Tier 3
--     (about 400) the automated nurture.
-- Cutoffs live in mart.tier_cutoff so they can be moved without editing logic.
-- Counts are checked live in `whitecircle segments`.
--
-- mart.top50: core universe only, v2: no services firms, no 'Not deploying AI', best fit_score first; ties broken by higher
-- data_confidence (we know more, so the score is less of a guess), then the more
-- recent last round, then name so the order is deterministic. It also carries the
-- best buyer contact so the CSV is ready for an SDR.
CREATE TABLE mart.tier_cutoff AS
SELECT * FROM (VALUES
  ('Tier 1', 65, 1), ('Tier 2', 52, 2), ('Tier 3', 42, 3), ('Nurture', 0, 4)
) AS t(tier, min_score, ord);

CREATE TABLE mart.org_segment AS
WITH seg AS (
SELECT f.org_uuid, f.segment_universe, f.llm_level, f.is_regulated, f.is_services_firm, f.size_bucket,
  s.fit_score,
  CASE f.segment_universe
    WHEN 'out_closed_acquired' THEN 'Out: closed or acquired'
    WHEN 'out_nonprofit'       THEN 'Out: nonprofit'
    WHEN 'enterprise'          THEN 'Enterprise'
    WHEN 'competitor'          THEN 'Competitor'
    ELSE CASE WHEN f.llm_level = 'none'                          THEN 'Not deploying AI'
              WHEN f.llm_level = 'strong' AND f.is_regulated     THEN 'Regulated GenAI'
              WHEN f.llm_level = 'strong'                        THEN 'AI-native builders'
              WHEN f.is_regulated                                THEN 'Regulated AI-adjacent'

@app.command()
def build() -> None:
    """Run src/white_circle/sql/*.sql in numeric order (stg.*, mart.*, dq.*)."""
    with track_run("build") as run:
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB))
        try:
            for f in sorted(SQL_DIR.glob("*.sql")):
                con.execute(f.read_text())
                typer.echo(f"ran {f.name}")
            for sch in ("stg", "mart", "dq"):
                for (t,) in con.execute(
                        "SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=? "
                        "AND table_type='BASE TABLE' ORDER BY 1", [sch]).fetchall():
                    n = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {sch}.{t}").fetchone()[0]
                    run.add_rows(n)
                    typer.echo(f"  {sch}.{t}: {n:,}")
        finally:
            con.close()


@app.command()
def dq() -> None:
    """Print the data-quality checks (dq.checks) and the score sanity checks (dq.score_checks)."""
    with track_run("dq"):
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
        try:
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT check_name, rows_affected, action_taken, description FROM ("
                "SELECT * FROM dq.checks UNION ALL SELECT * FROM dq.score_checks) ORDER BY ord").fetchall()
        finally:
            con.close()
        w = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
        typer.echo(f"{'check':<{w}}  {'rows':>6}  action / description")
        for name, n, action, desc in rows:
            typer.echo(f"{name:<{w}}  {n:>6,}  {action}")
            typer.echo(f"{'':<{w}}  {'':>6}    ({desc})")


@app.command()
def segments() -> None:
    """Print the segment x tier count matrix (mart.org_segment)."""
    with track_run("segments"):
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
        try:
            tiers = ["Tier 1", "Tier 2", "Tier 3", "Nurture"]
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT g.segment, coalesce(g.tier, '-') AS tier, count(*) FROM mart.org_segment g "
                "GROUP BY 1, 2").fetchall()
            cuts = con.execute("SELECT tier, min_score FROM mart.tier_cutoff ORDER BY ord").fetchall()
        finally:
            con.close()
        cells = {(s, t): n for s, t, n in rows}
        order = ["Regulated GenAI", "AI-native builders", "Regulated AI-adjacent", "Low fit", "Not deploying AI",
                 "Enterprise", "Competitor", "Out: closed or acquired", "Out: nonprofit"]
        w = max(len(s) for s in order)
        typer.echo("tier cutoffs (fit_score >=): " + ", ".join(f"{t} {m}" for t, m in cuts))
        typer.echo(f"{'segment':<{w}}" + "".join(f"{t:>9}" for t in tiers) + f"{'n/a':>9}{'total':>9}")
        tot = {t: 0 for t in tiers + ["-"]}
        for s in order:
            vals = [cells.get((s, t), 0) for t in tiers + ["-"]]
            for t, v in zip(tiers + ["-"], vals):
                tot[t] += v
            typer.echo(f"{s:<{w}}" + "".join(f"{v:>9,}" for v in vals) + f"{sum(vals):>9,}")
        vals = [tot[t] for t in tiers + ["-"]]
        typer.echo(f"{'TOTAL':<{w}}" + "".join(f"{v:>9,}" for v in vals) + f"{sum(vals):>9,}")


@app.command()
def top50() -> None:
    """Print the ranked top-50 AE list and write docs/deliverables/top50.csv."""
    with track_run("top50") as run:
        con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
        try:
            out = ROOT / "docs" / "deliverables" / "top50.csv"
            out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            con.execute(
                "COPY (SELECT rank, name, domain, country, segment, tier, fit_score, "
                "pts_llm AS llm_product_pts, pts_regulated AS regulated_risk_pts, "
                "pts_bonus AS interaction_bonus_pts, pts_capacity AS buying_capacity_pts, "
                "pts_size AS size_pts, pts_region AS region_pts, pts_reach AS reachability_pts, "
                "round(data_confidence, 2) AS data_confidence, reason_1, reason_2, reason_3, "
                "best_contact_name, best_contact_title FROM mart.top50 ORDER BY rank) "
                f"TO '{out}' (HEADER, DELIMITER ',')")
            rows = con.execute(
                "SELECT rank, name, country, segment, tier, fit_score, reason_1 "
                "FROM mart.top50 ORDER BY rank").fetchall()
        finally:
            con.close()
        run.add_rows(len(rows))
        for r, name, country, seg, tier, score, r1 in rows:
            typer.echo(f"{r:>2}. {name[:34]:<34} {country or '?':<14} {seg:<22} {tier:<7} {score:>3}  {r1}")
        typer.echo(f"wrote {out}")


@app.command("export-traces")
def export_traces(
    session: str = typer.Option(None, help="Claude Code session id (default: the take-home session)."),

-- 55_mart_org_features.sql  ->  mart.org_features  (one row per org, all 3,000)
--
-- Turns the staging tables into the handful of decision-ready attributes the score
-- and the segments use. Nothing is scored here; this file only answers "what do we
-- know about this company". Everything starts FROM stg.organizations with LEFT JOINs:
-- 73% of orgs have no funding round and 65% no contact, and an inner join would
-- silently delete them from the universe.
--
-- llm_level (strong / nlp_only / ml_only / none): how close the product is to LLMs.
--   strong   a category token in stg.llm_signal_token (genai, agentic, chatbot,
--            virtual assistant, foundation model...) OR the description matches the
--            regex below. NOTE: the 'nlp' signal in that table is NOT strong here;
--            plain "Natural Language Processing" is the nlp_only tier (it predates
--            LLMs). Regex uses word boundaries so "gpt" does not hit "egypt" and
--            "agent" alone (real-estate agent, insurance agent) does not count: we
--            require "ai agent" / "agentic".
--   nlp_only NLP / speech / conversational / voice-AI tag or wording, nothing stronger.
--   ml_only  generic AI / ML tag (any 'ai_platform' sector token) or "AI" in text.
-- vertical: the highest-risk sector any category token maps to, in order
--   fintech_banking > insurance > health > legal_compliance > public_sector >
--   education > hr_recruiting > crypto_web3 > finance_ops > security > ecommerce >
--   gaming > creative_tools > consumer_wellness > other (roughly by points, see 50_).
--   A company in several sectors is judged by its riskiest one, because one regulated
--   customer base is enough to need the guardrail. hr_recruiting = the
--   HR / recruiting / staffing tokens (which the shared taxonomy files
--   under business_services).
--   v2: is_regulated is TRUE only for the first four (rank <= 4). Crypto, government,
--   accounting and fitness used to be folded into those and are now separate,
--   non-regulated verticals (see 20_ for why).
-- is_services_firm (v2): agencies, consultancies, dev shops and outsourcers. They
--   build LLM apps FOR clients but do not run them at scale themselves, so they are a
--   weak buyer however AI-heavy their description sounds. 70_ caps them at Tier 3 and
--   keeps them out of the top 50. Matched on the short description (and, for the
--   unambiguous words only, the category tags); the regex was tuned by reading 15
--   flagged and 15 unflagged top candidates, see the comment on the column below.
-- is_competitor: guardrail / AI-safety / red-team / LLM-security vendors. They sell
--   what we sell, so they are partners or competitors, never AE targets.
-- segment_universe: why an org is in or out of the AE list. First match wins:
--   out_closed_acquired > out_nonprofit > enterprise (public) > competitor > core.
--   'enterprise' = publicly listed: a different sales motion, kept visible not deleted.
-- Funding (v2): recency, last round type/date/amount come from EQUITY rounds only
--   (round_group = 'equity_venture' in 30_): pre_seed, angel, convertible_note,
--   equity_crowdfunding, seed, series_unknown, series_a..series_h. NOT counted: grant,
--   non_equity_assistance (non-dilutive), debt_financing, post_ipo_* (public market),
--   private_equity (buyout/growth, not a venture raise), corporate_round, secondary_market
--   (existing shares changing hands), initial_coin_offering, product_crowdfunding,
--   undisclosed (no type, no amount). A company whose only 2025 event was a loan is
--   therefore NOT "recently funded". Same-day ties take the later stage. Stage is the highest equity
--   round ever raised (grants, debt and PE do not make a company "Series B"); where
--   there are no rounds we fall back to the source's funding_stage (63 orgs).
-- region: eu_uk = EU27 + EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) + Switzerland + UK, the
--   places the EU AI Act or UK rules reach; us_ca = US and Canada.
-- best contact: persona buckets from stg.contacts. technical_or_risk_buyer = CTO/eng,
--   AI/ML, security or compliance person; founder_only = only CEO/founder on file.
--   Board members, advisors and investors never count.
-- data_confidence: share of 6 fields known (funding recency, stage, headcount, country,
--   any contact, description). Separate from the score; used only as a tie-break and
--   to tell an AE how much of the picture is guesswork.

## 6. ICP implications for scoring a Crunchbase list

All of this is inferred from sources above. Evidence quality is thin (one named customer, two unnamed bank logos).

1. Companies that do not ship LLM features: do not count in the fit score. The product has nothing to attach to without an LLM or agent in production, and every page frames the trigger as "what AI system do you run". Treat as zero, or keep only as a long-watch nurture tier for companies with strong signs of a first AI launch (new AI hires, AI roadmap posts). [I from S11, S12]
2. Traditional banks and insurers with internal-only AI: low priority, not zero. The regulatory deployer-liability pitch applies to them in principle, and the finance/insurance pages exist, but the proven wins are neobanks/digital banks, not incumbents. Incumbents also mean long procurement and a Founding AE-sized motion. Score only if they have a customer-facing assistant, claims/underwriting AI or agentic workflow, otherwise tier 3. [I from S5, S11, S12]
3. AI-native app builders (Lovable-like) vs fintechs with customer chatbots: both are validated. AI-native builders have the highest pain (agents executing code, millions of sessions, abuse) and the only public logo, so rank them first for the "agentic/vibe-coding/creative tools" wedge. Fintechs/neobanks with customer-facing LLM assistants are the second validated wedge with larger contract potential. [C that both are customers; ranking is I] S3, S5, S6
4. Size: need real LLM traffic and a security/engineering function. Sweet spot is Series A to growth-stage companies with meaningful users plus enterprises' fintech arms; tiny pre-seed teams are likely self-serve only. Funding recency matters because it signals AI roadmap investment and budget. [I]
5. Geography: White Circle has EU and US regions, a Paris/London base, and is hiring AEs in NY/SF/London. Prioritise US and UK/EU first. EU companies carry an extra AI Act/GDPR hook. Other regions low. [I from S2, S6, S14]
6. Signals that show an account is a fit (rank roughly in this order):
   - Ships a customer-facing LLM feature, chatbot or agent (product page, changelog, docs mention of "AI assistant", "copilot", "agent")
   - Agentic action-taking: coding agents, tool use, MCP, browser or workflow agents (higher blast radius)
   - High-volume, consumer or open-signup user base (abuse and jailbreak exposure)
   - Regulated customers or data: fintech/neobank, insurance, health, legal, HR, government/education (PII, advice and bias risk)
   - Hiring for AI/ML engineers, AI security, trust and safety, or "AI governance"; named CISO or head of AI
   - Uses OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini APIs, or other model-provider signals (job posts, tech stack, public integrations)
   - Recent funding round (to fund AI rollout), US/UK/EU base, 20+ employees
   - Public AI incident, jailbreak or safety complaint about their product
   - Counter-signals: AI is only a back-office tool, no end-user exposure, existing vendor like Lakera/Prompt Security already deployed (competitive displacement possible but harder)

-- 52_stg_company_review.sql  ->  stg.company_review  (one row per website-checked org)
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. The Crunchbase tags say what a company SAYS it is; they cannot say
-- whether it actually ships a chatbot or agent to its customers. For the 120 orgs that
-- matter most (the v2 top candidates) an LLM-assisted reviewer opened each company's own
-- website and wrote down what it found, with a quoted sentence and the page it came from.
-- Those labels live in src/white_circle/seeds/company_review.csv (committed, so the
-- evidence travels with the code; `whitecircle merge-reviews` builds it from
-- data/verify/review_part*.csv). This file turns that CSV into a typed staging table.
-- 55_ then lets a confident label override the tag-based guess, and says so in a column.
--
-- Cleaning, in plain words: text is trimmed and the yes/no style fields are lower-cased
-- so 'Yes ' and 'yes' are the same answer; is_agentic / is_regulated become real booleans;
-- blank strings become NULL. If an org appears twice, the most confident row wins
-- (high > medium > low), then the later row.
--
-- The file may legitimately be missing (a fresh clone, or before the review is run).
-- Then this table is created empty and every org simply falls back to its tags: the
-- first statement below always runs, the second only when the seed file exists. The
-- marker line is read by `whitecircle build`; the path placeholder is filled in there.
CREATE TABLE stg.company_review (
  org_uuid VARCHAR, organization_name VARCHAR, url_checked VARCHAR, page_ok BOOLEAN,
  ships_customer_facing_llm VARCHAR, llm_use VARCHAR, is_agentic BOOLEAN,
  true_vertical VARCHAR, is_regulated BOOLEAN, customer_type VARCHAR,
  evidence_quote VARCHAR, source_url VARCHAR, confidence VARCHAR, notes VARCHAR);

-- @requires-seed
INSERT INTO stg.company_review
WITH r AS (
  SELECT * FROM read_csv('{{review_seed}}', all_varchar=true, header=true, quote='"', escape='"')),
c AS (
  SELECT
    nullif(trim(org_uuid), '')                                           AS org_uuid,
    nullif(trim(organization_name), '')                                  AS organization_name,
    nullif(trim(url_checked), '')                                        AS url_checked,
    lower(trim(page_ok)) IN ('true','yes','1','y')                       AS page_ok,
    nullif(lower(trim(ships_customer_facing_llm)), '')                   AS ships_customer_facing_llm,
    nullif(trim(llm_use), '')                                            AS llm_use,
    lower(trim(is_agentic)) IN ('true','yes','1','y')                    AS is_agentic,
    nullif(lower(trim(true_vertical)), '')                               AS true_vertical,
    lower(trim(is_regulated)) IN ('true','yes','1','y')                  AS is_regulated,
    nullif(trim(customer_type), '')                                      AS customer_type,
    nullif(trim(evidence_quote), '')                                     AS evidence_quote,
    nullif(trim(source_url), '')                                         AS source_url,
    nullif(lower(trim(confidence)), '')                                  AS confidence,
    nullif(trim(notes), '')                                              AS notes,
    row_number() OVER () AS file_order
  FROM r)
SELECT org_uuid, organization_name, url_checked, page_ok, ships_customer_facing_llm, llm_use, is_agentic,
       true_vertical, is_regulated, customer_type, evidence_quote, source_url, confidence, notes
FROM c
WHERE org_uuid IS NOT NULL
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid ORDER BY
  CASE confidence WHEN 'high' THEN 3 WHEN 'medium' THEN 2 ELSE 1 END DESC, file_order DESC) = 1;
EOF

@app.command("merge-reviews")
def merge_reviews() -> None:
    """Merge data/verify/review_part*.csv into the committed seed, and load the Tavily call logs into ops.api_call."""
    import csv
    import json
    from datetime import datetime

    import duckdb as _duck

    with track_run("merge-reviews") as run:
        parts = sorted(VERIFY.glob("review_part*.csv"))
        if not parts:
            raise typer.BadParameter(f"no review_part*.csv in {VERIFY}")
        rows: dict[str, dict] = {}
        n_in = 0
        for p in parts:
            with p.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                rd = csv.DictReader(f)
                missing = [c for c in REVIEW_COLS if c not in (rd.fieldnames or [])]
                if missing:
                    raise typer.BadParameter(f"{p.name} is missing columns {missing}")
                for r in rd:
                    n_in += 1
                    rows[r["org_uuid"].strip()] = {c: (r.get(c) or "").strip() for c in REVIEW_COLS}
        REVIEW_SEED.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with REVIEW_SEED.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=REVIEW_COLS, lineterminator="\\n")
            w.writeheader()
            w.writerows(sorted(rows.values(), key=lambda r: (r["organization_name"].lower(), r["org_uuid"])))
        run.add_rows(len(rows))
        typer.echo(f"{len(parts)} parts, {n_in} rows -> {len(rows)} unique orgs -> {REVIEW_SEED}")
        for col, ok in (("ships_customer_facing_llm", {"yes", "no", "unclear"}),
                        ("confidence", {"high", "medium", "low"})):
            bad = sorted({r[col] for r in rows.values() if r[col].lower() not in ok})
            if bad:
                typer.echo(f"WARN {col}: unexpected values {bad}")

        # Tavily call logs -> ops.api_call. Exact duplicate lines (a script re-ran) are dropped.
        seen: set[str] = set()
        dup = already = loaded = 0
        credits = 0.0
        con = _duck.connect(str(DB))
        try:
            con.execute("CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS ops")
            have = {r[0] for r in con.execute(
                "SELECT response_ref FROM ops.api_call WHERE response_ref LIKE 'verify:%'").fetchall()} \\
                if con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='ops' "
                               "AND table_name='api_call'").fetchone()[0] else set()
        finally:
            con.close()
        for p in sorted(VERIFY.glob("tavily_calls_part*.jsonl")):
            for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                if line in seen:
                    dup += 1
                    continue
                seen.add(line)
                c = json.loads(line)
                ref = f"verify:{c.get('batch')}:{c.get('ts')}"
                if ref in have:
                    already += 1
                    continue
                ts = datetime.fromisoformat(c["ts"]).replace(tzinfo=None) if c.get("ts") else None
                summ = (f"{c.get('request_summary')} [{c.get('batch')}; n_results={c.get('n_results')}, "
                        f"n_failed={c.get('n_failed')}; made via the Tavily MCP connector in-session]")
                record_api_call(run.run_id, c.get("provider") or "tavily", c.get("endpoint") or "", summ,
                                200 if c.get("status") == "ok" else None, None,
                                c.get("credits"), None, ref, ts)
                credits += c.get("credits") or 0
                loaded += 1
        typer.echo(f"api calls: loaded {loaded} ({credits:g} credits), dropped {dup} exact duplicate lines, "
                   f"skipped {already} already loaded")
        run.add_rows(loaded)

v3.1 is built from scratch on all 5 review parts (180 orgs), and every dq assertion passes. Nothing is committed, and I touched nothing outside white_circle/.

**Top 15** (all Tier 1, all with a verified ships=yes check):
1. Spellbook 100: AI contract-review and drafting copilot
2. OhMD 97: conversational AI for patient scheduling and triage
3. Sympera AI 97: agentic AI assistant for bank relationship managers
4. Persistence 96: voice agents booking patient appointments
5. Asteroid 93: browser agents operating EHRs and healthcare portals
6. UbiGrowth 86: governed AI platform doing sales, ops and finance tasks
7. Replit 84: AI agent that builds and deploys apps
8. Shapes 81: AI chat and workflows inside an HR platform
9. ReplyCX 80: AI support agents across WhatsApp, SMS and email
10. Enboarder 79: AI assistants and agents guiding employee journeys
11. Botcopy 78: governed contact-center agents
12. AWorld 78: AI-generated courses for bank customers
13. AGENTIC WORKS 78: on-prem agentic AI and local LLM platform
14. Dash0 77: AI trace triage and MCP agent access
15. Regaldi ai 76: AI assistants for pharmacy and 503B workflows

**Segment x tier matrix** (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 / Nurture):
- Regulated GenAI: 13 / 13 / 18 / 0
- AI-native builders: 19 / 142 / 386 / 174
- Regulated AI-adjacent: 0 / 0 / 12 / 304
- Low fit: 0 / 1 / 6 / 915
- Not deploying AI: 0 / 0 / 0 / 769
- Enterprise 26, Competitor 7, Out: closed or acquired 178, Out: nonprofit 17 (no tier)
- Total: 32 / 156 / 422 / 2,162, with 228 untiered

**Seats needing the new batches:** 5 of the 50 top-50 seats come from parts 4 and 5. Parts 1-3 alone already filled all 50, but they included unverified Centrical/MediaGuru-type orgs before the new rules.

**verify_next:** 134 orgs. It is Tier 1/2 by score, not verified, and not a services firm. Columns are queue_rank, org_uuid, name, domain, country, segment, tier_by_score, tier, fit_score, llm_level, llm_level_source, vertical, site_status, review_confidence, reason_1, best_contact_name, best_contact_title. dashboard.py does not read it yet, so adding it needs a new query there. The column names differ from mart.top50 only in that it has queue_rank instead of rank.

**Rules implemented**
- Services firms: flagged from the reviewer's notes or llm_use, using all reviews at any confidence. MediaGuru and Aurionpro are now flagged. I did not check Futura AI separately.
- Competitors: the rule flags 3 orgs, all now in the Competitor segment (7 in total, including tag-flagged Solo.io and 3 others).
  - Guild.ai: agent control plane vendor.
  - TrueFoundry: AI gateway vendor with guardrails.
  - GENUM LTD: reviewer's notes call it an "AI governance vendor; adjacent competitor", so I treated governance as the main product and moved it out of buyers. That was my reading of the notes; the llm_use text alone could be read as an email product with a governance feature.
  - Not flagged: Mavvrik (AI cost governance, FinOps) and Cosmos (corporate governance).
- Credits: merge-reviews now counts a search call with null credits as 1 credit and appends "(credits estimated)" to request_summary. There is no new column. Total is 53 credits over 41 calls: 32 reported plus 21 estimated. One duplicate line was dropped. The dashboard KPI sums both, and I relabelled it "Reported + estimated".

**Still off**
- 30 reviewed sites are dead or unverified and 2 are hijacked. All are capped at Tier 3 and out of the top 50.
- The competitor and services regexes read free text in notes, so a note like "not a consultancy" would false-positive. The current hits looked right on inspection.

Simplify the CRM data model for the White Circle take-home at white_circle. The owner wants it simple: exactly 3 objects (Company, Contact, Deal). Each object lists the basic attributes we collect, and below that, the triggers for when enrichment happens. The current docs/crm-data-model.md (5 objects, 32 MEDDPICC fields, Signal and Enrichment Run custom objects) is too heavy. Read it, plus docs/memo-notes.md (two-stage enrichment: a cheap baseline for everyone, a deep dive for the top 5) and docs/part2-system-design.md (routing and triggers). Keep the Attio facts that file confirmed: domains is the company match key, deals must be enabled, and the upsert is PUT with matching_attribute.

Content (tighten wording, but keep the substance):

COMPANY. Attributes:
- name; domain (the match key); crunchbase_uuid; LinkedIn; HQ country and region
- industry (verified); segment; tier
- fit_score total plus its 5 components (funding recency /40, revenue /25, headcount /15, headcount growth /20, fit bonus /10)
- score_version; scored_at
- ships_ai (verified, with evidence_quote and source_url); is_agentic
- funding stage; last equity round date and amount; total raised
- revenue range; headcount; headcount growth 3m/6m/12m
- data_confidence; last_enriched_at
- owner (AE); lifecycle stage
Enrichment triggers:
- On create, when a new domain comes from any source (Crunchbase import, RB2B visit, ad lead, manual): baseline enrichment (website check, firmographics, headcount), then score.
- On a signal (new funding round alert, Tier 1–2 website visit, AI/security hiring post): re-enrich and rescore.
- On a schedule: monthly rescore and a monthly headcount refresh.
- On reaching the top 5 or AE assignment: deep dive.
- Before outreach, if last_enriched_at is more than 90 days old: refresh.

CONTACT. Attributes:
- name; title; persona (CTO/eng leader, Head of AI/ML, CISO/security, compliance/risk/legal, founder/CEO)
- email; phone; LinkedIn
- company (reference); country; source (crunchbase / rb2b / ad form / clay / web)
- is_buyer_persona; lawful basis (for EU/UK)
- owner; last activity
Enrichment triggers:
- When the company reaches Tier 1–2: find the missing buyer personas (Clay waterfall for email and phone).
- When RB2B identifies a person (US only): create and enrich.
- When an ad form is submitted: enrich and route.
- Before an SDR call: verify the phone number.
- When a job change is detected: update or re-route.

DEAL. Attributes:
- name; company; primary contact; champion
- stage; amount; close date; owner (AE); source (inbound / outbound / signal)
- next step; next step due; blocked_by
- the 8 MEDDPICC elements as ONE text field each, plus meddpicc_confirmed_at
- loss reason
Enrichment triggers:
- When the deal is created (the AE accepts discovery; this stays a human step): attach the company deep dive.
- After each recorded call: AI drafts MEDDPICC updates and the AE confirms them. Only confirmed text counts.
- On stage change: check the required fields.
- Nightly: flag staleness (no next step, no champion, MEDDPICC not updated in 14 days).

# CRM data model (Attio) — Part 1, deliverable 4

Opinion in one line: **Attio holds decisions and conversations; the warehouse holds scores and evidence.** Scores are pushed in as machine-owned, versioned fields. Humans own everything about a deal. A signal never edits a company; it appends a row.

## 0. What I verified in Attio's docs vs. assumed

Checked on docs.attio.com (2026-10-29):

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| People and Companies are on by default; **Deals is an optional standard object** an admin must enable | Confirmed |
| Deal standard attrs: `name` (text), `stage` (status), `owner` (actor ref), `value` (currency), `associated_people`, `associated_company`. Name, stage, owner are required | Confirmed |
| Custom objects can be created (UI or `POST /v2/objects`); lists hold "entries" (one per record) and carry their own attributes | Confirmed |
| 17 attribute types incl. text, number, checkbox, currency, date, timestamp, rating, select, status, record-reference, actor-reference, domain, email, phone, location, personal name, interaction | Confirmed |
| Upsert = `PUT /v2/objects/{object}/records?matching_attribute=...`; update if match, create if none, **error if >1 match**; one matching attribute per call | Confirmed |
| `domains` is the only unique standard company attribute; `email_addresses` the only unique standard people attribute | Confirmed |
| Record-reference can be written by id, by domain/email shortcut, or by `target_record_reference` with `match` / `if_unmatched` / `if_multiple_matches` | Confirmed |
| Status values cannot be created by writing them (unknown title = error) | Confirmed |
| Multiselect matching attribute adds values; other multiselects are overwritten to the supplied list | Confirmed |
| Standard `linkedin` on companies and people exists but is **not** unique | Inferred (only `domains`/`email_addresses` documented unique) |

Assumed, not verified (flagged so nobody trusts them): custom attributes can be created with `is_unique: true` and then used as `matching_attribute` (the docs recommend "an ID from your own system", and the attribute schema has `is_unique`, so likely, but I did not see the create-attribute page); select write shape is the option title string (status confirmed, select not); currency write is `{"currency_value": n}`; Attio rate limits and API plan gating; whether a custom object can be both a list parent and carry record references to deals (should, untested). Everything below that depends on these is marked **(assumed)**.

## 1. Entity diagram

```mermaid

  ENRICHMENT_RUN { text run_id UK

```

Lists (views on records, with their own attributes):
- **SDR Call Queue**: list on Company. Entry attributes: `queue_reason` (text, copied from `reason_1`), `priority` (number), `assigned_sdr` (actor), `attempts` (number), `last_outcome` (select), `next_attempt_at` (timestamp), `cadence_status` (status: Queued / Calling / Nurture / Disqualified / Handed to AE).

- **Top 50**: plain Company list, membership driven by `mart.top50`; the view AEs look at on day one.

Why custom objects for Signal and Enrichment Run (not notes or company fields): they are many-per-company, time-stamped and queryable ("accounts with 2+ signals in 14 days" is a list filter). Notes are unstructured and can't be filtered; company fields would overwrite history. Cost: two more objects. Both are append-only and are never edited by humans.

--
-- RUNS AFTER 70_ (mart.org_score, mart.org_segment, mart.top50 from the scoring
-- step). Those tables may not exist yet; this file must not be run before they do.
-- It creates no tables and writes no data: each view is one row per Attio record,
-- column names are Attio attribute api_slugs, so the exporter does
--   SELECT * FROM crm.company_upsert  ->  PUT /v2/objects/companies/records?matching_attribute=domains
-- Custom attributes (see docs/crm-data-model.md) are prefixed nothing special; slugs
-- are snake_case and must be created in Attio first.
--
-- Companies with no usable domain (website was social/missing) get match_attribute =
-- 'crunchbase_uuid' instead of 'domains'; the exporter groups by match_attribute
-- because Attio takes ONE matching_attribute per request.
-- Only fields the machine owns are exported. Human-owned fields (owner, lifecycle_stage,
-- notes, MEDDPICC) are deliberately absent so an upsert cannot overwrite them.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS crm;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW crm.company_upsert AS
SELECT
  CASE WHEN o.domain IS NOT NULL THEN 'domains' ELSE 'crunchbase_uuid' END AS match_attribute,
  o.domain                                   AS domains,           -- Attio: [{domain}]
  o.uuid                                     AS crunchbase_uuid,   -- custom, unique
  o.organization_name                        AS name,
  o.short_description                        AS description,
  o.linkedin_url                             AS linkedin,
  o.city || ', ' || o.country                AS primary_location_text,
  o.country                                  AS country,

-- 00_schemas.sql
-- Rebuilds the derived schemas from scratch on every `whitecircle build`.
--
--   raw  : untouched copy of the CSVs, every column VARCHAR (made by `whitecircle load`)
--   stg  : cleaned, typed, flagged tables (this folder)
--   dq   : data-quality check log, computed live from raw + stg
--   mart : the answer layer: score weights, org features, fit score, segments, top 50
--   ops  : audit trail of CLI runs and API calls (NOT dropped here; see obs.py)
--
-- Dropping stg, dq and mart makes the build idempotent: the result depends only on raw
-- and these SQL files, never on what a previous run left behind.
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS stg CASCADE;
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS dq CASCADE;
DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS mart CASCADE;
CREATE SCHEMA stg;
CREATE SCHEMA dq;
CREATE SCHEMA mart;
-- 30_stg_funding_rounds.sql  ->  stg.funding_rounds  (one row per round, 1,854)
--
-- FIXES:
--  1. Typing: announced_on -> DATE, amounts -> DOUBLE via try_cast; failures would
--     show up as NULLs and be counted in dq.checks (there are none today).
--  2. money_raised_usd = 0 means "amount undisclosed", not "raised $0" (one row,
--     Adzact pre_seed). amount_usd is NULLIF(x, 0); money_raised_raw_usd keeps the
--     source value so the org-level total can still be reconciled exactly.
--  3. is_post_ipo: post_ipo_equity / post_ipo_debt / post_ipo_secondary are public
--     market transactions of listed companies (Accor 3.2B, Wix 1.0B). They are not
--     venture raises and wreck any average, so every venture metric excludes them.
--  4. round_group collapses ~25 investment types into: equity_venture, non_dilutive
--     (grants, assistance), debt, public_market, other. series_unknown is a real
--     venture round of unknown letter, not "unfunded".
--  5. type_rank is a stable ordering by stage. 21 org+date pairs hold two rounds on
--     the same day (e.g. debt_financing + series_a); "latest round" breaks the tie
--     with the higher rank so the answer is deterministic (the source's own
--     last_funding_type disagreed with the latest round in 4 cases for this reason).
--  6. Date plausibility is FLAGGED, not deleted: round_before_founding (> 1 year
--     before founded_on) and round_after_close. announced_date_precision marks
--     Jan-1 padded dates.
--  7. The denormalised org_name is dropped (it never disagrees with organizations);
--     join for the name.
CREATE TABLE stg.funding_rounds AS
WITH typ(investment_type, round_group, type_rank) AS (VALUES
  ('pre_seed',               'equity_venture',  10),
  ('angel',                  'equity_venture',  12),
  ('convertible_note',       'equity_venture',  15),
  ('equity_crowdfunding',    'equity_venture',  18),
  ('seed',                   'equity_venture',  20),
  ('series_unknown',         'equity_venture',  25),
  ('series_a',               'equity_venture',  30),
  ('series_b',               'equity_venture',  40),
  ('series_c',               'equity_venture',  50),
  ('series_d',               'equity_venture',  60),
  ('series_e',               'equity_venture',  70),
  ('series_f',               'equity_venture',  80),
  ('series_g',               'equity_venture',  90),
  ('series_h',               'equity_venture', 100),
  ('grant',                  'non_dilutive',     5),
  ('non_equity_assistance',  'non_dilutive',     6),
  ('debt_financing',         'debt',            26),
  ('post_ipo_debt',          'debt',           210),
  ('corporate_round',        'other',           28),
  ('private_equity',         'other',          110),
  ('secondary_market',       'other',           27),
  ('undisclosed',            'other',            1),
  ('product_crowdfunding',   'other',            2),
  ('initial_coin_offering',  'other',            3),
  ('post_ipo_equity',        'public_market',  200),
  ('post_ipo_secondary',     'public_market',  205))
SELECT
  r.org_uuid,
  r.investment_type,
  coalesce(t.round_group, 'other')                      AS round_group,
  coalesce(t.type_rank, 0)                              AS type_rank,
  (r.investment_type LIKE 'post_ipo%')                  AS is_post_ipo,
  try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE)                      AS announced_on,
  CASE WHEN r.announced_on LIKE '%-01-01' THEN 'year' ELSE 'day' END AS announced_date_precision,
  try_cast(r.money_raised_usd AS DOUBLE)                AS money_raised_raw_usd,
  nullif(try_cast(r.money_raised_usd AS DOUBLE), 0)     AS amount_usd,
  try_cast(r.investor_count AS INTEGER)                 AS investor_count,
  nullif(trim(r.lead_investor_names), '')               AS lead_investor_names,  -- free text, not splittable
  coalesce(try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE) < o.founded_on - INTERVAL 1 YEAR, FALSE) AS round_before_founding,
  coalesce(try_cast(r.announced_on AS DATE) > o.closed_on, FALSE)                    AS round_after_close
FROM raw.funding_rounds r
LEFT JOIN typ t ON t.investment_type = r.investment_type
LEFT JOIN stg.organizations o ON o.uuid = r.org_uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX stg_funding_rounds_key
  ON stg.funding_rounds (org_uuid, investment_type, announced_on);
-- 35_stg_org_funding.sql  ->  stg.org_funding  (one row per ORG, all 3,000)
--
-- Per-company funding aggregates rebuilt from the rounds, EXCLUDING post-IPO rounds
-- (public-market transactions are not venture funding, see 30_). We rebuild instead
-- of trusting organizations.funding_* because the source columns are NULL for the
-- 2,200 orgs with no rounds, and last_funding_type is wrong where two rounds share a
-- date.
--
-- Starts from organizations (LEFT JOIN) on purpose: 73% of companies have no round,
-- and an INNER JOIN would silently drop them. "No funding data" is a segment, not an
-- error: has_funding_round = FALSE, counts 0, amounts NULL (never 0).
--
-- total_funding_usd is NULL (not 0) when rounds exist but none disclosed an amount
-- (180 orgs).
--
-- Reconciliation: reported_total_usd comes from the source's funding_total_usd;
-- total_incl_post_ipo_raw_usd re-sums A

-- 55_mart_org_features.sql  ->  mart.org_features  (one row per org, all 3,000)
--
-- Turns the staging tables into the handful of decision-ready attributes the score
-- and the segments use. Nothing is scored here; this file only answers "what do we
-- know about this company". Everything starts FROM stg.organizations with LEFT JOINs:
-- 73% of orgs have no funding round and 65% no contact, and an inner join would
-- silently delete them from the universe.
--
-- llm_level (strong / nlp_only / ml_only / none): how close the product is to LLMs.
--   strong   a category token in stg.llm_signal_token (genai, agentic, chatbot,
--            virtual assistant, foundation model...) OR the description matches the
--            regex below. NOTE: the 'nlp' signal in that table is NOT strong here;
--            plain "Natural Language Processing" is the nlp_only tier (it predates
--            LLMs). Regex uses word boundaries so "gpt" does not hit "egypt" and
--            "agent" alone (real-estate agent, insurance agent) does not count: we
--            require "ai agent" / "agentic".
--   nlp_only NLP / speech / conversational / voice-AI tag or wording, nothing stronger.
--   ml_only  generic AI / ML tag (any 'ai_platform' sector token) or "AI" in text.
-- vertical: the highest-risk sector any category token maps to, in order
--   fintech_banking > insurance > health > legal_compliance > public_sector >
--   education > hr_recruiting > crypto_web3 > finance_ops > security > ecommerce >
--   gaming > creative_tools > consumer_wellness > other (roughly by points, see 50_).
--   A company in several sectors is judged by its riskiest one, because one regulated
--   customer base is enough to need the guardrail. hr_recruiting = the
--   HR / recruiting / staffing tokens (which the shared taxonomy files
--   under business_services).
--   v2: is_regulated is TRUE only for the first four (rank <= 4). Crypto, government,
--   accounting and fitness used to be folded into those and are now separate,
--   non-regulated verticals (see 20_ for why).
-- is_services_firm (v2): agencies, consultancies, dev shops and outsourcers. They
--   build LLM apps FOR clients but do not run them at scale themselves, so they are a
--   weak buyer however AI-heavy their description sounds. 70_ caps them at Tier 3 and
--   keeps them out of the top 50. Matched on the short description (and, for the
--   unambiguous words only, the category tags); the regex was tuned by reading 15
--   flagged and 15 unflagged top candidates, see the comment on the column below.
-- is_competitor: guardrail / AI-safety / red-team / LLM-security vendors. They sell
--   what we sell, so they are partners or competitors, never AE targets.
-- segment_universe: why an org is in or out of the AE list. First match wins:
--   out_closed_acquired > out_nonprofit > enterprise (public) > competitor > core.
--   'enterprise' = publicly listed: a different sales motion, kept visible not deleted.
-- v3.1: "verified" means an accepted review: confidence high or medium AND a live (or
--   search-recovered) site. Unclear / low reviews are NOT verified: they change no label.
--   They can still flag a services firm (see is_services_firm in the last SELECT).
-- v3 VERIFIED OVERRIDES. For the orgs whose own website was checked (stg.company_review,
--   52_), a HIGH or MEDIUM confidence label beats the tag-based guess, because a tag says
--   what a company claims and the site says what it ships:
--     llm_level     ships_customer_facing_llm = 'yes' -> 'strong'. = 'no' -> downgraded:
--                   'ml_only' if the reviewer's own text still mentions AI (or gave no text,
--                   so we are unsure), else 'none'. 'unclear' changes nothing.
--     vertical / is_regulated   taken from the reviewer's true_vertical / is_regulated
--                   when true_vertical is a sector we have weights for.
--   The tag-based answers are kept as tags_llm_level / tags_vertical / tags_is_regulated
--   and llm_level_source / vertical_source say which one is in force ('verified' or
--   'tags'), so nothing is overwritten silently. Low-confidence labels are ignored.
--   Labels from a dead or hijacked site (site_status, see 52_) are ignored too; 70_ caps
--   those orgs at Tier 3 and out of the top 50.
--   is_agentic, verified_llm_use and evidence_quote ride along for the score (agentic
--   bonus in 60_) and for the AE-facing CSV.
-- Funding (v2): recency, last round type/date/amount come from EQUITY rounds only
--   (round_group = 'equity_venture' in 30_): pre_seed, angel, convertible_note,
--   equity_crowdfunding, seed, series_unknown, series_a..series_h. NOT counted: grant,
--   non_equity_assistance (non-dilutive), debt_financing, post_ipo_* (public market),
--   private_equity (buyout/growth, not a venture raise), corporate_round, secondary_market
--   (existing shares changing hands), initial_coin_offering, product_crowdfunding,
--   undisclosed (no type, no amount). A company whose only 2025 event was a loan is
--   therefore NOT "recently funded". Same-day ties take the later stage. Stage is the highest equity
--   round ever raised (grants, debt and PE do not make a company "Series B"); where
--   there are no rounds we fall back to the source's funding_stage (63 orgs).
-- region: eu_uk = EU27 + EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) + Switzerland + UK, the
--   places the EU AI Act or UK rules reach; us_ca = US and Canada.
-- best contact: persona buckets from stg.contacts. technical_or_risk_buyer = CTO/eng,
--   AI/ML, security or compliance person; founder_only = only CEO/founder on file.
--   Board members, advisors and investors never count.
-- data_confidence: share of 6 fields known (funding recency, stage, headcount, country,
--   any contact, description). Separate from the score; used only as a tie-break and
--   to tell an AE how much of the picture is guesswork.

-- 60_mart_org_score.sql  ->  mart.org_score  (one row per org, all 3,000)
--
-- Fit score 0-100 = sum of components, each looked up in mart.score_weight (50_),
-- capped at 100. No point value is written in this file. One column per component
-- so a reviewer (or an AE asking "why is this #7?") can see exactly where the points
-- came from:
--   pts_llm        LLM product                       max 35
--   pts_regulated  regulated-sector risk x llm_factor max 25
--   pts_bonus      LLM x regulated interaction       max 10  (strong LLM AND is_regulated)
--   pts_capacity   = pts_recency + pts_stage + pts_round_size   max 10 + 6 + 4 = 20
--   pts_size       headcount                         max 10
--   pts_region     EU/UK > US/CA > other             max 5
--   pts_reach      best buyer persona on file        max 5
--   pts_agentic    v3: +3 when a website check found an action-taking agent AND a
--                  customer-facing LLM ('yes'); 0 for everyone not checked
-- v2: the base maxima add to exactly 100 (35+25+20+10+5+5); with the +10 bonus the
-- raw total can reach 110, so the cap at 100 matters for the very best accounts only.
-- v2 LLM GATE: regulated points are the sector's value (50_) times mart.llm_factor
-- (strong 1.0, nlp_only 0.5, ml_only 0.2, none 0), rounded to a whole point. A bank
-- with no AI product earns nothing for being a bank. The bonus is unchanged.
-- v3: llm_level, vertical and is_regulated come from mart.org_features, where a
-- confident website check (stg.company_review) has already overridden the tag guess;
-- llm_level_source / vertical_source say which one is in force. For a verified org
-- reason_1 is "Ships: <what the site says it ships>", and the generic LLM reason is
-- never shown next to it, so reasons 2 and 3 are the next two best components.
-- score_version is a real column ('v3'), not an alias. Gates that cap the tier
-- (headcount 1-10, services firms, no AI signal) are applied in 70_, not here: the
-- score stays a pure measure of fit.
--
-- Missing data = 0 points for that component and nothing more (see 50_). The
-- score is computed for EVERY org, including ones later excluded from the AE list
-- (enterprise, competitors, closed): the exclusion lives in 70_segments, so a
-- public giant can be inspected with the same score and visibly be a non-target.
--
-- reason_1..3: the three components that added the most points, in plain words, for
-- the AE and the CRM. The bonus is folded into the regulated reason (they are one
-- story: "ships LLMs in a regulated sector"); the three funding sub-scores are one
-- reason ("Raised Series B 5 months ago"). Ties keep a fixed order
-- (LLM, regulated, funding, reach, size, region) so the output is deterministic.
CREATE TABLE mart.org_score AS
WITH
w AS (SELECT component, level, points FROM mart.score_weight),
lv AS (
  SELECT f.*,
    CASE WHEN months_since_last_round IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
         WHEN months_since_last_round <= 12 THEN 'le_12m'
         WHEN months_since_last_round <= 24 THEN '12_24m'
         ELSE 'gt_24m' END AS recency_level,
    CASE WHEN last_round_amount_usd >= 10000000 THEN 'ge_10m'
         WHEN last_round_amount_usd >= 2000000  THEN 'ge_2m'
         ELSE 'lt_2m' END AS round_size_level,
    CASE WHEN llm_level = 'strong' AND is_regulated THEN 'strong_llm_x_regulated' END AS bonus_level,
    CASE WHEN is_agentic AND verified_ships_llm = 'yes' THEN 'verified_agent_ships_llm' END AS agentic_level,

    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='llm_product'       AND level = l.llm_level), 0)      AS pts_llm,
    round(coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='regulated_risk' AND level = l.vertical), 0)
          * coalesce(l.llm_factor, 0))::INT                                                            AS pts_regulated,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='interaction_bonus' AND level = l.bonus_level), 0)    AS pts_bonus,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='agentic_bonus' AND level = l.agentic_level), 0)      AS pts_agentic,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='funding_recency'   AND level = l.recency_level), 0)  AS pts_recency,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='funding_stage'     AND level = l.stage_bucket), 0)   AS pts_stage,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='round_size'        AND level = l.round_size_level), 0) AS pts_round_size,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='size'              AND level = l.size_bucket), 0)    AS pts_size,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='region'            AND level = l.region_bucket), 0)  AS pts_region,

Read-only: one short connection, closed before the page is written. The page is a
single self-contained HTML file with the data embedded as JSON. Columns added later
by the score v3 work (llm_level_source, verified_llm_use, is_agentic, evidence_quote,
vertical_source, evidence source/url) are picked up from whichever mart table holds
them; when absent the page simply hides them.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

from .paths import DB, ROOT

TEMPLATE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "templates" / "dashboard.html"
OUT = ROOT / "docs" / "dashboard" / "index.html"

V3_COLS = ["llm_level_source", "verified_llm_use", "is_agentic", "evidence_quote", "vertical_source",
           "evidence_url", "evidence_source", "source_url", "evidence_source_url"]
TIERS = ["Tier 1", "Tier 2", "Tier 3", "Nurture"]
CORE_SEGMENTS = ["Regulated GenAI", "AI-native builders", "Regulated AI-adjacent", "Low fit", "Not deploying AI"]
OTHER_SEGMENTS = ["Enterprise", "Competitor", "Out: closed or acquired", "Out: nonprofit"]


def _rows(con, sql: str, params: list | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    cur = con.execute(sql, params or [])
    cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]


def _exists(con, table: str) -> bool:
    s, t = table.split(".")
    return con.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema=? AND table_name=?",
                       [s, t]).fetchone()[0] > 0


def _safe(con, sql: str, params: list | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    try:
        return _rows(con, sql, params)
    except Exception:  # a missing table must not break the page
        return []


def _v3_sources(con) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map each v3 column that exists to the mart table that holds it (with org_uuid)."""
    found: dict[str, str] = {}
    rows = con.execute(
        "SELECT table_schema||'.'||table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns "
        "WHERE table_schema IN ('mart','stg','crm') AND column_name = ANY(?)", [V3_COLS]).fetchall()
    has_uuid = {t for (t,) in con.execute(
        "SELECT table_schema||'.'||table_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE column_name='org_uuid'").fetchall()}
    pref = ["mart.org_score", "mart.org_features", "mart.org_segment", "mart.top50"]
    for t, c in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (pref.index(r[0]) if r[0] in pref else 99, r[0])):
        if t in has_uuid and c not in found:
            found[c] = t
    return found


def export(con) -> dict:
    v3 = _v3_sources(con)
    joins = sorted({t for t in v3.values() if t not in ("mart.top50",)})
    alias = {t: f"v{i}" for i, t in enumerate(joins)}
    extra = ", ".join(f"{alias[t] if t in alias else 't'}.{c} AS {c}" for c, t in v3.items())
    jsql = " ".join(f"LEFT JOIN {t} {alias[t]} ON {alias[t]}.org_uuid = t.org_uuid" for t in joins)
    top = _rows(con, f"""
        SELECT t.rank, t.org_uuid, t.name, t.domain, t.country, t.segment, t.tier, t.fit_score,
          t.pts_llm, t.pts_regulated, t.pts_bonus, t.pts_capacity, t.pts_size, t.pts_region, t.pts_reach,
          round(t.data_confidence, 2) AS data_confidence, t.reason_1, t.reason_2, t.reason_3,
          t.best_contact_name, t.best_contact_title,
          f.employees_label, f.region_bucket, f.vertical, f.llm_level, f.short_description
          {', ' + extra if extra else ''}
        FROM mart.top50 t JOIN mart.org_features f USING (org_uuid) {jsql}

    for r in top:

        t = v3["verified_llm_use"]
        verified = con.execute(
            f"SELECT count(*) FROM {t} x JOIN mart.org_segment g USING (org_uuid) "

# White Circle: company research for ICP definition

Researched 2026-10-30 (Tavily worked). Tags: [C] = confirmed on a cited page, [I] = inferred by me.
Sources are numbered, listed at the bottom.

## 1. What the product does

- One line: an "AI control" layer. Customers write plain-language policies, and White Circle's own models check every input, output and tool call against them in real time, then block, rewrite or escalate. [C] S1, S4, S5
- Four modules on the homepage: Test (find failure modes before users do, i.e. red teaming), Control (runtime guardrails across inputs, outputs, tools), Analyze (user and model behaviour over time, monitoring), Improve (tune prompts and models from live signals, labelled-feedback loop). [C] S1
- Also: audit logs and explanations of which policy fired, per-region/jurisdiction policies, user strike/ban system with appeals, user-level risk scoring, human review queue, custom natural-language metrics, Slack and webhook alerts. [C] S1, S2, S3
- Deployment: hosted SaaS API (single event endpoint, EU and US regions, `wceu-`/`wcus-` keys), "5 mins to integrate", 99.99% uptime claim, 150+ languages, text and image checking. Docs show integration guides for an AI support chatbot, a vibe-coding app and a coding assistant. [C] S1, S2, S3
- Self-hosting: the Test product page FAQ says on-prem/VPC is supported for strict-compliance enterprises. [C] S8 (older page, treat as less certain)
- Threats covered: prompt injection, jailbreaks, PII/data leakage, hallucination, harmful/illegal content, tool abuse and destructive agent actions, token drain, abuse/anomalous users, model drift, compliance policy checks. Brand safety and tone are covered on the Test page. [C] S1, S3, S8, S9
- Security attestations: SOC 2 Type I and II, HIPAA. [C] S1, S5
- Own research: CircleGuardBench (moderation benchmark), KillBench (bias study), Halo (open-source training framework); they train their own models for the job. [C] S1, S4

## 2. Who they sell to

Named customers
- Lovable (vibe-coding platform): the only named logo. Full case study plus CISO quote (Igor Andriushchenko). Lovable sends every session event to White Circle; use case is user abuse (phishing sites, malware, explicit content, unsafe commands, multi-step jailbreaks) and agent supervision. [C] S1, S3. Technical partnership announced on LinkedIn. [C] S10
- "Two of the world's largest digital banks" (unnamed) and, per Fortune, "several fintech and legal companies". [C] S5, S6. The company's own job post says "multiple neobanks". [C] S7. None are named anywhere I found. [C]

Industries marketing calls out
- Homepage "one control layer, every industry" tabs: Government, Healthcare, Education. [C] S1
- SEO landing pages exist for finance, insurance, healthcare, government, education, HR, e-commerce, gaming, creative tools, real estate, plus use-case pages (agentic AI security, chatbot guardrails, hallucination detection, content moderation API, data-leak prevention, prompt injection). [C] S11
- Every vertical page is framed as "what AI system do you run" (chatbot, copilot, underwriting AI, claims assistant, fraud assistant). So the trigger is a deployed AI system, not the vertical. [C] S11, S12

Buyer persona
- Only named buyer: a CISO (Lovable). [C] S3
- No persona page exists. Docs and the 5-minute API pitch imply engineers/AI platform teams as users and champions; trust and safety/moderation fits the content-moderation and strike-system features. Compliance/risk is plausible for banks. [I]

Company size and stage of customers
- Lovable is a fast-growing AI-native scale-up; neobanks are large fintechs. Smaller prospects are reachable self-serve ("Get Started" login), larger via "Contact Sales". [I from S1]

Pricing and packaging
- No public pricing found on the site or docs. Self-serve signup plus Contact Sales and Request a Demo. Packaging language: "unlimited custom policies". Usage/cost API exists in docs ("Usage & Cost"), suggesting usage-based billing. [C that no price is public; usage-based is I] S1, S2
- Traction: multi-million-dollar run rate, 100M+ API calls a month (job post) and 1B+ requests cumulative (press). [C] S7, S5

## 3. Regulatory angle

- The philosophy page argues deployers carry the legal responsibility: "A bank is responsible for what its assistant tells a customer about their mortgage... under the EU AI Act, deployers carry their own obligations." That is the only EU AI Act mention I found on their own pages. [C] S13
- Product regulation hooks: per-country/state policies, audit logs "for compliance and incident review", compliance checks in the control flow, EU data region, GDPR mention on the insurance page, HIPAA. [C] S1, S3, S12
- DORA: no mention found anywhere. [C that I did not find it]
- No compliance-reporting module (no EU AI Act dashboard or report) found; compliance is delivered as policies plus audit trail. [I]
- Does it target non-AI/traditional companies? Only as deployers. Every example involves an LLM or agent talking to end users or taking actions (finance chatbot, underwriting AI, claims assistant). Internal-only AI is mentioned in one place: careers says it ships to companies deploying AI "for customers and inside their own systems". [C] S12, S14. The regulatory pitch (deployer liability) would extend to a bank with an internal copilot, but no evidence of such a sale. [I]

- Name: White Circle, PBC (Public Benefit Corporation); also seen as "Pumpkin Intelligence". [C] S4, S15
- HQ: Paris, with London office and a US presence/hiring (NY, SF, LA remote). [C] S4, S14
- Founded: 2025 per Tracxn; CEO's LinkedIn dates the role from Jan 2025. [C] S16, S17
- Founder and CEO: Denis Shilov. Went viral in 2024 with a universal jailbreak (1.4M views), then Anthropic independent safety researcher (Nov 2024 to Jan 2025). # Data profile: Crunchbase extract (organizations / funding_rounds / contacts)

Profiled 2026-10-29, read-only, DuckDB 1.5.5. Every column is read as `all_varchar` so nothing is silently coerced, then cast with `try_cast`.
Rows: 3,000 organizations, 1,854 funding rounds, 2,763 contacts.

**Headline.** The data is far cleaner than "raw and a little messy" suggests: no duplicate uuids or names, no orphans, no name drift, no unparseable numbers or dates, categorical values are consistent snake_case codes. The mess is elsewhere: sparsity, coded range columns, `;`-delimited multi-value columns, URL and email inconsistencies, role-level contact duplicates, and snapshot semantics that quietly mislead (acquired companies still `active`, `funding_stage` mixing two meanings). The sample is not a random Crunchbase slice: it is AI-heavy by construction (2,023 of 3,000 are AI-tagged), so "AI" is not a discriminating ICP filter on its own.

Setup used throughout (script harness in the scratchpad):
```sql
CREATE VIEW organizations AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('.../organizations.csv', all_varchar=true, header=true, sample_size=-1);
-- same for funding_rounds, contacts
```

## 1. Duplicates

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate org uuid | 0 | Still add `PRIMARY KEY (uuid)` in the staging table so a re-pull fails loudly |
| Duplicate org name (case/space-insensitive) | 0 | None; do not dedupe on name (names are not unique in real Crunchbase) |
| Duplicate website domain (scheme/www/path stripped) | 0 | Build `domain` with `regexp_replace`; use it as the secondary match key |
| Duplicate linkedin_url | 0 | None |
| Duplicate funding rounds (org, type, date, amount) | 0 | None; keep composite key `(org_uuid, investment_type, announced_on)` |
| Same org + same announce date, different rows | 21 (2 types same day, e.g. `debt_financing` + `series_a`) | Legitimate; do not dedupe on (org, date). Break ties by a stable type rank when picking "latest round" |
| Contacts: repeated (org_uuid, person_uuid) | 66 extra rows (13 also repeat title); 11 are exact title repeats with different `started_on` or identical | `QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid, person_uuid ORDER BY started_on DESC NULLS LAST) = 1`. These are multiple roles (Co-Founder then CEO), so keep a `roles` list if titles matter |
| Contacts: person_uuid in more than one org | 4 people (70 dup person_uuid rows = 66 + 4) | Legitimate (serial founders); key a person on `(org_uuid, person_uuid)` |
| Contacts: same linkedin url, different person_uuid | 0 | None |

```sql
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,person_uuid)) FROM contacts;                 -- 66
SELECT count(*)-count(DISTINCT (org_uuid,investment_type,announced_on)) FROM funding_rounds; -- 0
```

## 2. Join coverage

| Check | Result | Cleaning approach |
|---|---|---|
| Orgs with >= 1 round | 800 (26.7%) | LEFT JOIN from organizations, never INNER, or 73% of the universe vanishes |
| Orgs with >= 1 contact | 1,047 (34.9%); 1,007 are active | Same; "no contact" is a segment ("needs enrichment"), not an error |
| Orgs with neither rounds nor contacts | 1,697 (56.6%) | Flag `has_contact`, `has_funding` on the org-level model |
| Orgs with 0 contacts / 1 / 8+ | 1,953 / 432 / 86 | 8 looks like a cap on the export per org |
| Orphan rounds / orphan contacts | 0 / 0 | Keep as an assertion test (`NOT EXISTS`) |
| org_name differs from organizations.organization_name for same uuid | 0 / 0 | Drop the denormalised `org_name` from rounds/contacts; join for it |
| `funding_round_count` vs actual round rows | 0 mismatches (null on exactly the 2,200 orgs without rounds) | Recompute from rounds rather than trusting the column |

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM funding_rounds r WHERE r.org_uuid=o.uuid)) AS with_rounds FROM organizations o;
```

## 3. Per-column messiness

### 3a. Null / blank rates (% of rows, `NULL` or `''`)

| Table | Column | % null |

name: WebFetch
text:
## `employee_count`

- **Data Type:** `Integer (>= 0)`
- **Description:** "The current number of employees working at the company based on our number of profiles."
- **Calculation:** Counts profiles whose `experience.company.id` matches the company, with a non-null `job_start_date` and no end date.
- **Example:** `"employee_count": 78`

## `employee_count_by_month`

- **Data Type:** `Object`
- **Keys:** Months in `YYYY-MM` format, with integer values.
- **Description:** "The number of employees at the end of each month."
- **Range:** Starts at the first associated employee's start date or January 1, 2010, whichever is later.
- **Example:**
  ```json
  "employee_count_by_month": {
    "2021-07": 84,
    "2021-08": 86,
    "2021-09": 84
  }
  ```

## `employee_growth_rate`

- **Data Type:** `Object`
- **Keys and types:** `3_month`, `6_month`, `12_month`, `24_month`, each a `Float`.
- **Description:** "The percentage increase in total headcount from N months prior."
- **Calculation:** `(current_employee_count / previous_employee_count) - 1`, rounded to four decimal places. It can be negative, and it is `null` if the company had zero employees or did not exist at the start of the window.
- **Example:**
  ```json
  "employee_growth_rate": {
    "3_month": 0.0595,
    "6_month": 0.0723,
    "12_month": 0.8542,
    "24_month": 1.4722
  }
  ```

## `inferred_revenue`

- **Data Type:** `Enum (String)`
- **Description:** "Company's estimated annual revenue range in US dollars."
- **Source:** A predictive model using insights fields such as `employee_count_by_month_by_role`. Values come from the Canonical Inferred Revenue Ranges.
- **Example:** `"inferred_revenue": "$10M-$25M"`

**Related:** `inferred_revenue_integer` is a beta `Integer` giving a numeric revenue estimate in USD. It is a premium add-on, e.g. `"inferred_revenue_integer": 52000000`.

name: WebFetch
text:
**Endpoint:** `GET https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich`

**Authentication:** Send your API key in the `X-Api-Key` header. The docs say the key "must be included in either the request header or the api_key parameter."

**Parameters**

A request needs at least one of `pdl_id`, `name`, `ticker`, `website`, or `profile`.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `website` | String | The company's website, e.g., `google.com`. |
| `name` | String | The company's name, e.g., `Google, Inc.`. |
| `profile` | String | The company's social profile, e.g., `linkedin.com/company/google`. |
| `ticker` | String | The stock ticker, if publicly traded, e.g., `GOOGL`. |
| `pdl_id` | String | The PDL ID or `linkedin_slug`. If used with other match inputs, only `pdl_id` is used. |
| `min_likelihood` | Integer | Minimum match score, 1-10. Default is `2`. |
| `required` | String | Fields a response must include to count as a match, as a boolean statement, e.g., `location AND (website OR linkedin_url)`. |
| `titlecase` | Boolean | Default `false`. Set to `true` to title-case response text. Otherwise, text is lowercase. |

**Example request (cURL)**

```bash
curl -X GET -G \
  'https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich' \
  -H 'X-[REDACTED_SECRET]' \
  --data-urlencode 'website=google.com' \
  --data-urlencode 'min_likelihood=5'
```
