-- 56_stg_headcount_history.sql  ->  stg.headcount_history  (one row per ENRICHED org)
--
-- Headcount over time is NOT in the Crunchbase extract (only a size band). It comes from
-- People Data Labs via `whitecircle enrich-headcount` (enrich_pdl.py), which writes the
-- committed seed src/white_circle/seeds/headcount_history.csv. This file turns that CSV
-- into a typed table. There is no key yet, so today the seed does not exist: the table
-- is created EMPTY and every org simply has unknown growth (scored 0, never negative).
-- Same pattern as 52_: the first statement always runs, the second only when the seed
-- file exists (the marker line is read by `whitecircle build`).
--
-- Columns: hc_current and hc_Nm_ago are employee counts (current and N months before the
-- fetch month); growth_Nm_pct is the percentage change (25.0 means +25%), as PDL
-- reports it times 100; hc_source names the provider; hc_fetched_at is when it was pulled.
CREATE TABLE stg.headcount_history (
  org_uuid VARCHAR, pdl_id VARCHAR, likelihood INTEGER,
  hc_current INTEGER, hc_3m_ago INTEGER, hc_6m_ago INTEGER, hc_12m_ago INTEGER,
  growth_3m_pct DOUBLE, growth_6m_pct DOUBLE, growth_12m_pct DOUBLE,
  hc_source VARCHAR, hc_fetched_at TIMESTAMP);

-- @requires-hc-seed
INSERT INTO stg.headcount_history
SELECT nullif(trim(org_uuid), ''), nullif(trim(pdl_id), ''), try_cast(likelihood AS INTEGER),
       try_cast(hc_current AS INTEGER), try_cast(hc_3m_ago AS INTEGER), try_cast(hc_6m_ago AS INTEGER),
       try_cast(hc_12m_ago AS INTEGER),
       try_cast(growth_3m_pct AS DOUBLE), try_cast(growth_6m_pct AS DOUBLE), try_cast(growth_12m_pct AS DOUBLE),
       nullif(trim(hc_source), ''), try_cast(hc_fetched_at AS TIMESTAMP)
FROM read_csv('{{hc_seed}}', all_varchar=true, header=true, quote='"', escape='"')
WHERE nullif(trim(org_uuid), '') IS NOT NULL
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY org_uuid ORDER BY hc_fetched_at DESC) = 1;
EOF
cat > 57_mart_org_master.sql <<'EOF'
-- 57_mart_org_master.sql  ->  mart.org_master  (one row per org, all 3,000)
--
-- THE SINGLE SOURCE for the gates (58_) and the rubric (60_). Nothing downstream joins
-- back to stg: if a gate or a point needs a fact, it is a column here. LEFT JOINs only,
-- starting from stg.organizations: 73% of orgs have no funding round and an inner join
-- would silently delete them. A dq check asserts exactly one row per org.
--
-- Column groups
--   * every stg.organizations column (including the decoded revenue_* and employees_*)
--   * funding, joined on org uuid from stg.funding_rounds:
--       rounds                      LIST of STRUCT(announced_on, investment_type, is_equity,
--                                   money_raised_usd, investor_count, lead_investor_names),
--                                   oldest first. money_raised_usd is the source value
--                                   (0 stays 0, "undisclosed"; see 30_).
--       all_rounds_count / _usd     every round incl. debt, grants and post-IPO
--       equity_rounds_count / _usd  venture equity only (round_group = 'equity_venture')
--       first_round_date            earliest round of any kind
--       last_equity_date/type/amount  the latest EQUITY round (same-day ties: later stage)
--       months_since_last_equity    whole months from that date to as_of (2026-10-29)
--     Why equity only for "recency": a loan or grant does not mean the company just
--     raised money to spend on AI rollout (see 55_ for the full list of what is excluded).
--   * the website check (stg.company_review via 55_): llm_level and its source, the
--     tag-based guess it replaced, true_vertical, is_agentic, site_status, evidence quote
--   * vertical: the org's industry for gate 9. It is 55_'s vertical with ONE refinement,
--     'ai_native' (see mart.vertical_gate in 50_): an org that ships an LLM (llm_level
--     'strong') and whose industry is horizontal. Verified orgs: the reviewer's
--     true_vertical was 'generic_tech'. Unverified orgs: tags gave 'other' AND at least
--     one category token is a generic_tech / ai_platform / devtools_infra sector.
--     A verified generic_tech org that does NOT ship an LLM stays 'generic_tech' (fails).
--   * best buyer contact, flags (is_services_firm, is_competitor), region_bucket
--   * headcount growth, LEFT-joined from stg.headcount_history (56_): hc_current,
--     hc_3m_ago, hc_6m_ago, hc_12m_ago, growth_3m_pct, growth_6m_pct, growth_12m_pct,
--     hc_source, hc_fetched_at. NULL for every org until `enrich-headcount` has run.
--     If PDL gave counts but no pct for a window, the pct is computed from the counts.
CREATE TABLE mart.org_master AS
WITH
p AS (SELECT as_of FROM mart.params),
rd AS (
  SELECT org_uuid,
    list(struct_pack(announced_on := announced_on, investment_type := investment_type,
                     is_equity := (round_group = 'equity_venture'),
                     money_raised_usd := money_raised_raw_usd, investor_count := investor_count,
                     lead_investor_names := lead_investor_names)
         ORDER BY announced_on NULLS FIRST, type_rank, investment_type)               AS rounds,
    count(*)                                                                          AS all_rounds_count,
    sum(amount_usd)                                                                   AS all_rounds_usd,
    count(*) FILTER (WHERE round_group = 'equity_venture')                            AS equity_rounds_count,
    sum(amount_usd) FILTER (WHERE round_group = 'equity_venture')                     AS equity_rounds_usd,
    min(announced_on)                                                                 AS first_round_date
  FROM stg.funding_rounds GROUP BY 1),
ainat AS (
  SELECT org_uuid, bool_or(sector IN ('generic_tech', 'ai_platform', 'devtools_infra')) AS has_horizontal_tag
  FROM stg.org_category GROUP BY 1)
SELECT
  o.*,
  coalesce(rd.rounds, [])                                    AS rounds,
  coalesce(rd.all_rounds_count, 0)                           AS all_rounds_count,
  rd.all_rounds_usd,
  coalesce(rd.equity_rounds_count, 0)                        AS equity_rounds_count,
  rd.equity_rounds_usd,
  rd.first_round_date,
  f.last_round_date                                          AS last_equity_date,
  f.last_round_type                                          AS last_equity_type,
  f.last_round_amount_usd                                    AS last_equity_amount_usd,
  f.months_since_last_round                                  AS months_since_last_equity,
  f.llm_level, f.llm_level_source, f.tags_llm_level,
  f.has_verified_review, f.verified_ships_llm, f.verified_llm_use, f.review_confidence,
  rv.true_vertical,
  f.vertical_source, f.is_regulated,
  CASE WHEN f.llm_level = 'strong' AND f.vertical = 'generic_tech'                       THEN 'ai_native'
       WHEN f.llm_level = 'strong' AND f.vertical = 'other' AND f.vertical_source = 'tags'
            AND coalesce(a.has_horizontal_tag, FALSE)                                    THEN 'ai_native'
       ELSE f.vertical END                                   AS vertical,
  f.vertical                                                 AS vertical_v3,
  f.is_agentic, f.evidence_quote, f.site_status,
  f.is_services_firm, f.is_competitor,
  f.region_bucket, f.size_bucket, f.stage_bucket, f.persona_bucket, f.contact_count,
  f.best_contact_name, f.best_contact_title, f.best_contact_bucket,
  f.data_confidence,
  h.hc_current, h.hc_3m_ago, h.hc_6m_ago, h.hc_12m_ago,
  coalesce(h.growth_3m_pct,  CASE WHEN h.hc_3m_ago  > 0 THEN round((h.hc_current::DOUBLE / h.hc_3m_ago  - 1) * 100, 2) END) AS growth_3m_pct,
  coalesce(h.growth_6m_pct,  CASE WHEN h.hc_6m_ago  > 0 THEN round((h.hc_current::DOUBLE / h.hc_6m_ago  - 1) * 100, 2) END) AS growth_6m_pct,
  coalesce(h.growth_12m_pct, CASE WHEN h.hc_12m_ago > 0 THEN round((h.hc_current::DOUBLE / h.hc_12m_ago - 1) * 100, 2) END) AS growth_12m_pct,
  h.hc_source, h.hc_fetched_at
FROM stg.organizations o
CROSS JOIN p
LEFT JOIN rd                          ON rd.org_uuid = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN mart.org_features f         ON f.org_uuid  = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN stg.company_review rv       ON rv.org_uuid = o.uuid AND f.has_verified_review
LEFT JOIN ainat a                     ON a.org_uuid  = o.uuid
LEFT JOIN stg.headcount_history h     ON h.org_uuid  = o.uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX mart_org_master_org ON mart.org_master (uuid);
EOF

-- 58_mart_org_gate.sql  ->  mart.org_gate, mart.gate_funnel
--
-- STAGE 1 OF SCORE v4: exclusion gates. Nine yes/no tests, evaluated IN THIS ORDER. An
-- org is a candidate only if it trips NONE of them. A gate that is TRUE means the org is
-- EXCLUDED by that rule. Every gate is computed for every org (so an org's full record
-- of failures is visible), and first_failed_gate records the first one in the order
-- below, which is the reason shown in the segment "Out: <gate>".
--
--   1 is_closed              Crunchbase says the company shut down. Nobody to sell to.
--   2 is_acquired            Acquired (or funding_stage m_and_a). The buyer is now the
--                            parent company; it is a different account and a different deal.
--   3 is_nonprofit           Non-profits buy on grants and do not match the commercial motion.
--   4 is_public              Publicly listed. NOT discarded as junk: these form the separate
--                            ENTERPRISE segment (long procurement, a different sales motion).
--   5 is_competitor          Sells guardrails / AI-safety / red-teaming / LLM security (tags,
--                            or the website check showed it). Partner or rival, never a lead.
--   6 is_services_firm       Agency, consultancy, dev shop: builds LLM apps FOR clients and
--                            does not run them at scale. A weak buyer however AI-heavy it sounds.
--   7 dead_or_hijacked_site  The website check found the site dead, unverifiable or hijacked.
--                            A June 2026 snapshot cannot show the company shut down or pivoted.
--   8 not_ai                 FAILS unless llm_level is 'strong' or 'nlp_only'. White Circle
--                            guards LLM inputs, outputs and actions, so the company must have
--                            language AI in production. Analytics / classic ML-only AI fails
--                            ('ml_only'), no AI signal fails ('none'), and a website check
--                            that said the company does NOT ship an LLM fails (it is
--                            downgraded to ml_only / none in 55_).
--   9 industry_not_matched   FAILS unless the org's vertical is on the passing list in
--                            mart.vertical_gate (50_ header lists every vertical and which
--                            side it lands on).
--
-- Unknown data never excludes by itself: gates 1-4 read flags that default to FALSE, gate 7
-- fires only on an explicit site_status. Gates 8 and 9 do exclude orgs with no AI signal /
-- no matching industry, which is the point of them.
--
-- mart.gate_funnel: rows remaining after each gate, in order, starting from all orgs.
CREATE TABLE mart.org_gate AS
WITH g AS (
  SELECT m.uuid AS org_uuid, m.organization_name,
    coalesce(m.is_closed, FALSE)                                              AS is_closed,
    coalesce(m.is_acquired, FALSE)                                            AS is_acquired,
    coalesce(m.is_nonprofit, FALSE)                                           AS is_nonprofit,
    coalesce(m.is_public, FALSE)                                              AS is_public,
    coalesce(m.is_competitor, FALSE)                                          AS is_competitor,
    coalesce(m.is_services_firm, FALSE)                                       AS is_services_firm,
    coalesce(m.site_status IN ('dead_or_unverified', 'hijacked'), FALSE)      AS dead_or_hijacked_site,
    coalesce(m.llm_level, 'none') NOT IN ('strong', 'nlp_only')               AS not_ai,
    NOT coalesce((SELECT passes FROM mart.vertical_gate v WHERE v.vertical = m.vertical), FALSE) AS industry_not_matched
  FROM mart.org_master m)
SELECT g.*,
  CASE WHEN is_closed THEN 'is_closed' WHEN is_acquired THEN 'is_acquired'
       WHEN is_nonprofit THEN 'is_nonprofit' WHEN is_public THEN 'is_public'
       WHEN is_competitor THEN 'is_competitor' WHEN is_services_firm THEN 'is_services_firm'
       WHEN dead_or_hijacked_site THEN 'dead_or_hijacked_site' WHEN not_ai THEN 'not_ai'
       WHEN industry_not_matched THEN 'industry_not_matched' END              AS first_failed_gate,
  (NOT (is_closed OR is_acquired OR is_nonprofit OR is_public OR is_competitor OR is_services_firm
        OR dead_or_hijacked_site OR not_ai OR industry_not_matched))           AS passes_all
FROM g;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX mart_org_gate_org ON mart.org_gate (org_uuid);

CREATE TABLE mart.gate_funnel AS
WITH order_(step, gate) AS (VALUES
  (1,'is_closed'), (2,'is_acquired'), (3,'is_nonprofit'), (4,'is_public'), (5,'is_competitor'),
  (6,'is_services_firm'), (7,'dead_or_hijacked_site'), (8,'not_ai'), (9,'industry_not_matched')),
r AS (
  SELECT o.step, o.gate,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_gate g
      WHERE g.first_failed_gate IS NULL
         OR (SELECT step FROM order_ x WHERE x.gate = g.first_failed_gate) > o.step) AS remaining
  FROM order_ o)
SELECT 0 AS step, 'all orgs' AS gate, (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_gate) AS remaining, 0 AS removed_here
UNION ALL
SELECT step, gate, remaining,
       lag(remaining, 1, (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_gate)) OVER (ORDER BY step) - remaining
FROM r
ORDER BY step;
EOF

-- 60_mart_org_score.sql  ->  mart.org_score  (score v4: one row per org that PASSES ALL GATES)
--
-- STAGE 2 OF SCORE v4: a fixed points rubric. Only orgs with mart.org_gate.passes_all are
-- scored; an excluded org has no score at all (it has a reason instead, in org_gate).
-- No point value is written in this file: every number is looked up in mart.score_weight
-- or mart.fit_bonus_rule (50_), which also say WHY. One column per component, so an AE
-- asking "why is this #7?" can read the answer off the row.
--
--   pts_recency    max 40  months since the LAST EQUITY round (as_of 2026-10-29):
--                          <=6 40, <=12 32, <=18 24, <=24 16, <=36 8, older 2, none/unknown 0
--   pts_revenue    max 25  decoded revenue band: <$1M 5, $1-10M 15, $10-50M 25, $50-100M 25,
--                          $100M+ 20 (enterprise procurement drag), unknown 0
--   pts_headcount  max 15  1-10 3, 11-50 8, 51-200 15, 201-500 15, 501-1000 12, 1001+ 8, unknown 0
--   pts_growth     max 20  12-month headcount growth >=50% 12, >=20% 8, >=0% 4, negative 0;
--                          +4 if 6-month growth >=20%; +4 if 3-month growth >=10%; capped at
--                          20. Unknown (not yet enriched by PDL) 0, never negative.
--   pts_bonus      max 10  fit bonus: best matching vertical tier from mart.fit_bonus_rule
--                          (pts_bonus_vertical) + 4 when the website check found an agent that
--                          takes actions (pts_bonus_agentic), capped at 10. Derived only from
--                          docs/whitecircle-research.md; region earns NO points.
--   rubric_total   = recency + revenue + headcount + growth        (out of 100)
--   total          = rubric_total + pts_bonus                       (out of 110)
-- Missing data = 0 points for that component and nothing more. We do not subtract for
-- unknowns, because most orgs have no round, revenue band or growth data: a penalty would
-- just rank by "who has a Crunchbase profile". How much we know is data_confidence, a
-- separate column used as a tie-break.
--
-- ORDER (rank): total desc, then region_priority (eu_uk and us_ca = 1, others = 2; region
-- is a TIE-BREAKER only and earns no points: White Circle sells in Europe and North
-- America), then data_confidence desc, then name. `ord` is that order, 1 = best.
--
-- reason_1..3: the three components that added the most points, in plain words, for the AE
-- and the CRM. For a website-verified org reason_1 stays "Ships: <what the site says it
-- ships>" and reasons 2-3 are the next two best components. Ties keep a fixed order
-- (fit, funding, revenue, headcount, growth) so the output is deterministic.
--
-- scored_at / score_version: when this build scored the org, and 'v4'. Every build is also
-- appended to ops.score_history (61_) so rescoring leaves an audit trail.
CREATE TABLE mart.org_score AS
WITH
w AS (SELECT component, level, points FROM mart.score_weight),
src AS (
  SELECT m.*,
    CASE WHEN m.months_since_last_equity IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
         WHEN m.months_since_last_equity <= 6  THEN 'le_6m'
         WHEN m.months_since_last_equity <= 12 THEN 'le_12m'
         WHEN m.months_since_last_equity <= 18 THEN 'le_18m'
         WHEN m.months_since_last_equity <= 24 THEN 'le_24m'
         WHEN m.months_since_last_equity <= 36 THEN 'le_36m'
         ELSE 'gt_36m' END AS recency_level,
    CASE WHEN m.revenue_min_usd IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
         WHEN m.revenue_min_usd < 1000000   THEN 'lt_1m'
         WHEN m.revenue_min_usd < 10000000  THEN '1m_10m'
         WHEN m.revenue_min_usd < 50000000  THEN '10m_50m'
         WHEN m.revenue_min_usd < 100000000 THEN '50m_100m'
         ELSE 'ge_100m' END AS revenue_level,
    CASE WHEN m.employees_min IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
         WHEN m.employees_min <= 10  THEN '1-10'
         WHEN m.employees_min <= 50  THEN '11-50'
         WHEN m.employees_min <= 200 THEN '51-200'
         WHEN m.employees_min <= 500 THEN '201-500'
         WHEN m.employees_min <= 1000 THEN '501-1000'
         ELSE '1001+' END AS headcount_level,
    CASE WHEN m.growth_12m_pct IS NULL THEN NULL
         WHEN m.growth_12m_pct >= 50 THEN 'ge_50' WHEN m.growth_12m_pct >= 20 THEN '20_50'
         WHEN m.growth_12m_pct >= 0  THEN '0_20' ELSE 'negative' END AS growth12_level,
    CASE WHEN m.growth_6m_pct >= 20 THEN 'ge_20' END AS growth6_level,
    CASE WHEN m.growth_3m_pct >= 10 THEN 'ge_10' END AS growth3_level,
    CASE WHEN m.region_bucket IN ('eu_uk', 'us_ca') THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS region_priority
  FROM mart.org_master m JOIN mart.org_gate g ON g.org_uuid = m.uuid AND g.passes_all),
pts AS (
  SELECT s.*,
    (SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='funding_recency' AND level = s.recency_level)  AS pts_recency,
    (SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='revenue'         AND level = s.revenue_level)  AS pts_revenue,
    (SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='headcount'       AND level = s.headcount_level) AS pts_headcount,
    least((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='growth_total_cap'),
          coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='growth_12m' AND level = s.growth12_level), 0)
        + coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='growth_6m'  AND level = s.growth6_level), 0)
        + coalesce((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='growth_3m'  AND level = s.growth3_level), 0)) AS pts_growth,
    coalesce((SELECT points FROM mart.fit_bonus_rule b WHERE b.kind='vertical' AND b.key = s.vertical), 0) AS pts_bonus_vertical,
    CASE WHEN s.is_agentic AND s.verified_ships_llm = 'yes'
         THEN (SELECT points FROM mart.fit_bonus_rule b WHERE b.kind='feature' AND b.key='verified_agentic') ELSE 0 END AS pts_bonus_agentic,
    (SELECT tier FROM mart.fit_bonus_rule b WHERE b.kind='vertical' AND b.key = s.vertical) AS bonus_tier
  FROM src s),
tot AS (
  SELECT *,
    least((SELECT points FROM w WHERE component='fit_bonus_cap'), pts_bonus_vertical + pts_bonus_agentic) AS pts_bonus,
    pts_recency + pts_revenue + pts_headcount + pts_growth AS rubric_total
  FROM pts),
sc AS (SELECT *, rubric_total + pts_bonus AS total FROM tot),
cand AS (
  SELECT uuid AS org_uuid, 1 AS prio, pts_bonus AS p,
    CASE WHEN pts_bonus_agentic > 0 AND pts_bonus_vertical > 0 THEN 'Fits White Circle messaging (' || replace(vertical, '_', ' ') || ') and ships agents'
         WHEN pts_bonus_agentic > 0 THEN 'Ships agents that take actions'
         ELSE 'Fits White Circle messaging: ' || replace(vertical, '_', ' ') || ' (' || coalesce(bonus_tier, '') || ')' END AS txt FROM sc
  UNION ALL SELECT uuid, 2, pts_recency,
    CASE WHEN last_equity_date IS NULL THEN 'No equity round on file'
         ELSE CASE WHEN last_equity_type = 'series_unknown' THEN 'Raised a round'
                   WHEN last_equity_type LIKE 'series_%' THEN 'Raised Series ' || upper(substr(last_equity_type, 8))
                   WHEN last_equity_type = 'pre_seed' THEN 'Raised a pre-seed'
                   WHEN last_equity_type = 'seed' THEN 'Raised a seed round'
                   WHEN last_equity_type = 'angel' THEN 'Raised an angel round'
                   ELSE 'Last round: ' || replace(last_equity_type, '_', ' ') END
              || ' ' || months_since_last_equity || ' months ago' END FROM sc
  UNION ALL SELECT uuid, 3, pts_revenue, 'Revenue band ' || coalesce(revenue_label, 'unknown') FROM sc
  UNION ALL SELECT uuid, 4, pts_headcount, 'Team size ' || coalesce(employees_label, 'unknown') FROM sc
  UNION ALL SELECT uuid, 5, pts_growth, 'Headcount growth ' || coalesce(round(growth_12m_pct)::INT::VARCHAR || '% over 12 months',

cat > 61_ops_score_history.sql <<'EOF'
-- 61_ops_score_history.sql  ->  ops.score_history (append-only) and view mart.score_history
--
-- WHY. The weights are stated priors to be recalibrated against realized results (see 50_).
-- Recalibrating needs the past: which score did each org have on which date, from which
-- inputs? So every build APPENDS its scores here and never replaces them.
--
-- WHERE. The table lives in schema `ops`, which `00_schemas.sql` does not drop (mart is
-- dropped on every build, which would erase the history). mart.score_history is a plain
-- view over it, so reviewers can find it next to the other score tables.
--
-- DEDUPE KEY. (org_uuid, score_version, input_hash). input_hash is an md5 of everything
-- the score reads: the org's inputs (round dates and types, revenue band, headcount band,
-- growth percentages, vertical, agentic flag, as_of date) PLUS a hash of the weight and
-- bonus tables, so a change to a weight makes new rows even under the same version name.
-- Rebuilding from the same snapshot twice therefore adds ZERO rows; a new data pull, a
-- PDL enrichment or a reweighting adds rows with a new scored_at. A past ranking is
-- reproduced by filtering one scored_at / input_hash and ordering by total.
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS ops;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ops.score_history (
  org_uuid VARCHAR, score_version VARCHAR, input_hash VARCHAR, scored_at TIMESTAMP, as_of DATE,
  pts_recency INTEGER, pts_revenue INTEGER, pts_headcount INTEGER, pts_growth INTEGER,
  pts_bonus INTEGER, rubric_total INTEGER, total INTEGER, region_priority INTEGER,
  data_confidence DOUBLE);

INSERT INTO ops.score_history
WITH wh AS (
  SELECT md5(coalesce((SELECT string_agg(component || '|' || level || '|' || points, ';' ORDER BY component, level) FROM mart.score_weight), '')
          || coalesce((SELECT string_agg(kind || '|' || key || '|' || points, ';' ORDER BY kind, key) FROM mart.fit_bonus_rule), '')) AS h),
x AS (
  SELECT s.*, m.last_equity_date, m.last_equity_type, m.revenue_range, m.employee_count_range,
         m.growth_3m_pct, m.growth_6m_pct, m.growth_12m_pct
  FROM mart.org_score s JOIN mart.org_master m ON m.uuid = s.org_uuid)
SELECT x.org_uuid, x.score_version,
  md5(concat_ws('|', (SELECT as_of FROM mart.params), x.last_equity_date, x.last_equity_type, x.revenue_range,
        x.employee_count_range, x.growth_3m_pct, x.growth_6m_pct, x.growth_12m_pct, x.vertical, x.is_agentic,
        x.verified_ships_llm, x.llm_level, x.region_bucket, (SELECT h FROM wh))) AS input_hash,
  x.scored_at, (SELECT as_of FROM mart.params),
  x.pts_recency, x.pts_revenue, x.pts_headcount, x.pts_growth, x.pts_bonus, x.rubric_total, x.total,
  x.region_priority, x.data_confidence
FROM x
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM ops.score_history h
  WHERE h.org_uuid = x.org_uuid AND h.score_version = x.score_version
    AND h.input_hash = md5(concat_ws('|', (SELECT as_of FROM mart.params), x.last_equity_date, x.last_equity_type, x.revenue_range,
        x.employee_count_range, x.growth_3m_pct, x.growth_6m_pct, x.growth_12m_pct, x.vertical, x.is_agentic,
        x.verified_ships_llm, x.llm_level, x.region_bucket, (SELECT h FROM wh))));

CREATE VIEW mart.score_history AS SELECT * FROM ops.score_history;
EOF

-- 70_mart_segments.sql  ->  mart.tier_cutoff, mart.org_segment, mart.top50, mart.verify_next
--
-- Two separate questions, answered separately:
--   SEGMENT = WHO they are (what kind of buyer, which play to run). Rule-based, so an
--             AE can explain it in one breath. Does not use the score.
--   TIER    = HOW SOON to work them. Cut from the v4 total (out of 110). Gate-passers only.
--
-- Segments
--   Regulated GenAI     passed every gate AND the vertical is the regulated core
--                       (fintech_banking, insurance, health, legal_compliance): ships language
--                       AI where a bad answer is a compliance event. The thesis account.
--   AI-native builders  passed every gate, vertical 'ai_native': the Lovable lookalikes.
--   Marketed verticals  passed every gate, vertical is one White Circle markets to (public
--                       sector, education, HR, e-commerce, gaming, creative tools).
--   Enterprise          failed gate 4: publicly listed. A different sales motion, kept visible.
--   Competitor          failed gate 5: guardrail / AI-safety vendors.
--   Out: <gate>         everything else, named by the FIRST gate it failed (Out: is_closed,
--                       Out: not_ai, Out: industry_not_matched ...). Nobody is dropped
--                       silently; every org has a segment.
-- segment_universe = 'core' for gate-passers, otherwise the first failed gate.
--
-- TIER CUTOFFS (total out of 110, gate-passers only). Re-picked on the v4 distribution.
-- WHY these numbers is documented next to the values below; the counts are checked live
-- in `whitecircle segments`. Cutoffs live in mart.tier_cutoff so they can move without
-- editing logic.
--@@TIER_NOTES@@
--
-- mart.top50: gate-passers only, ranked by TOTAL descending (mart.org_score.ord: total,
-- then region_priority, then data_confidence, then name). Tier is a column, not the sort
-- key. Keeps the v3.1 rule that every top-50 org is VERIFIED: a high/medium-confidence
-- website check that says it ships a customer-facing LLM ('yes'), on a live (or
-- search-recovered) site. Tags alone can fill the tiers, never this list.
--
-- mart.verify_next: the "verify before outreach" queue: gate-passers that are NOT verified
-- (never reviewed, or reviewed unclear/low), best total first. Work it top-down: each org
-- verified moves into the top-50 pool if it ships, or out if it does not.
CREATE TABLE mart.tier_cutoff AS
SELECT * FROM (VALUES
  ('Tier 1', 0, 1), ('Tier 2', 0, 2), ('Tier 3', 0, 3), ('Nurture', 0, 4)
) AS t(tier, min_score, ord);

CREATE TABLE mart.org_segment AS
SELECT g.org_uuid, g.passes_all, g.first_failed_gate,
  CASE WHEN g.passes_all THEN 'core' ELSE g.first_failed_gate END AS segment_universe,
  CASE WHEN g.passes_all THEN
         CASE WHEN s.vertical IN ('fintech_banking', 'insurance', 'health', 'legal_compliance') THEN 'Regulated GenAI'
              WHEN s.vertical = 'ai_native' THEN 'AI-native builders'
              ELSE 'Marketed verticals' END
       WHEN g.first_failed_gate = 'is_public'     THEN 'Enterprise'
       WHEN g.first_failed_gate = 'is_competitor' THEN 'Competitor'
       ELSE 'Out: ' || g.first_failed_gate END AS segment,
  s.total,
  CASE WHEN g.passes_all THEN (SELECT tier FROM mart.tier_cutoff c WHERE s.total >= c.min_score ORDER BY c.ord LIMIT 1) END AS tier
FROM mart.org_gate g
LEFT JOIN mart.org_score s ON s.org_uuid = g.org_uuid;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX mart_org_segment_org ON mart.org_segment (org_uuid);

CREATE TABLE mart.top50 AS
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.ord) AS rank,
  s.org_uuid, m.organization_name AS name, m.domain, m.country, m.short_description,
  g.segment, g.tier, s.total, s.rubric_total,
  s.pts_recency, s.pts_revenue, s.pts_headcount, s.pts_growth, s.pts_bonus,
  s.pts_bonus_vertical, s.pts_bonus_agentic,
  s.region_bucket, s.region_priority, s.data_confidence, s.vertical, s.llm_level,
  m.last_equity_date, m.last_equity_type, m.months_since_last_equity, m.revenue_label, m.employees_label,
  m.growth_3m_pct, m.growth_6m_pct, m.growth_12m_pct,
  s.reason_1, s.reason_2, s.reason_3,
  m.best_contact_name, m.best_contact_title,
  s.llm_level_source, s.verified_ships_llm, s.verified_llm_use, s.is_agentic, s.evidence_quote,
  m.site_status
FROM mart.org_score s
JOIN mart.org_segment g USING (org_uuid)
JOIN mart.org_master m ON m.uuid = s.org_uuid
WHERE g.passes_all
  AND s.llm_level_source = 'verified' AND s.verified_ships_llm = 'yes'
  AND m.site_status IN ('live', 'recovered_via_search')
QUALIFY rank <= 50
ORDER BY rank;

CREATE VIEW mart.verify_next AS
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.ord) AS queue_rank,
  s.org_uuid, m.organization_name AS name, m.domain, m.country, g.segment, g.tier, s.total,
  s.llm_level, s.vertical, m.site_status, m.review_confidence, s.reason_1,
  m.best_contact_name, m.best_contact_title
FROM mart.org_score s
JOIN mart.org_segment g USING (org_uuid)
JOIN mart.org_master m ON m.uuid = s.org_uuid
WHERE g.passes_all AND NOT s.has_verified_review;
EOF

     + (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_gate g WHERE g.passes_all AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mart.org_score s WHERE s.org_uuid = g.org_uuid)), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 921, 'top50_gate_failure', 'ASSERT: every top-50 org passes all gates (top-50 rows that do not)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.top50 t JOIN mart.org_gate g USING (org_uuid) WHERE NOT g.passes_all), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 922, 'score_component_sum_mismatch', 'ASSERT: orgs where component sum differs from total',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score WHERE pts_recency + pts_revenue + pts_headcount + pts_growth + pts_bonus <> total
        OR pts_recency + pts_revenue + pts_headcount + pts_growth <> rubric_total), '0 = pass. total is exactly the sum of the visible columns'
  UNION ALL SELECT 923, 'bonus_over_10', 'ASSERT: orgs with a fit bonus above 10',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score WHERE pts_bonus > 10 OR pts_bonus < 0), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 924, 'rubric_max_not_100', 'ASSERT: sum of the rubric component maxima differs from 100 (40+25+15+20), or a growth/bonus cap differs',
    (SELECT abs((SELECT max(points) FROM mart.score_weight WHERE component = 'funding_recency')
              + (SELECT max(points) FROM mart.score_weight WHERE component = 'revenue')
              + (SELECT max(points) FROM mart.score_weight WHERE component = 'headcount')
              + (SELECT points FROM mart.score_weight WHERE component = 'growth_total_cap') - 100)),
    '0 = pass. Weights 40/25/15/20'
  UNION ALL SELECT 925, 'component_over_max', 'ASSERT: orgs with a component above its maximum (40/25/15/20)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score WHERE pts_recency > 40 OR pts_revenue > 25 OR pts_headcount > 15 OR pts_growth > 20), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 926, 'total_out_of_range', 'Orgs with total outside 0-110',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score WHERE total < 0 OR total > 110), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 927, 'score_level_missing_weight', 'Orgs whose derived level has no row in mart.score_weight (would silently score NULL)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score s
      WHERE s.pts_recency IS NULL OR s.pts_revenue IS NULL OR s.pts_headcount IS NULL), '0 = pass. Catches a typo in a level name in 50_ or 60_'
  UNION ALL SELECT 928, 'bonus_unsupported_by_research', 'Bonus rows whose vertical has no fit_bonus_rule row (silently 0)',
    (SELECT count(DISTINCT vertical) FROM mart.org_score s WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mart.fit_bonus_rule b WHERE b.kind = 'vertical' AND b.key = s.vertical)),
    'INFO: a vertical that passes the industry gate but earns no bonus row is scored 0 for the bonus'
  UNION ALL SELECT 929, 'agentic_bonus_unverified', 'Orgs given the agentic bonus without a verified customer-facing LLM',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_score WHERE pts_bonus_agentic > 0 AND NOT (is_agentic AND verified_ships_llm = 'yes')), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 930, 'score_history_dupes', 'ASSERT: duplicate (org_uuid, score_version, input_hash) rows in ops.score_history',
    (SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT (org_uuid, score_version, input_hash)) FROM ops.score_history), '0 = pass. History is append-only and deduped'
  -- top 50 and queue [REDACTED_SECRET]
  UNION ALL SELECT 940, 'top50_size', 'Top-50 rows short of 50 (50 - rows)',
    (SELECT 50 - count(*) FROM mart.top50), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 941, 'top50_not_verified', 'ASSERT: top-50 rows without a verified (high/medium, live site) ships=yes check',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.top50 WHERE NOT (llm_level_source = 'verified' AND verified_ships_llm = 'yes' AND site_status IN ('live', 'recovered_via_search'))), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 942, 'top50_not_sorted_by_total', 'ASSERT: top-50 rank order violates total desc, then region_priority, data_confidence desc, name',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT total, region_priority, data_confidence, name,

        lag(data_confidence) OVER (ORDER BY rank) pd, lag(name) OVER (ORDER BY rank) pn FROM mart.top50)
      WHERE pt IS NOT NULL AND (total > pt

        OR (total = pt AND region_priority = pr AND data_confidence > pd)
        OR (total = pt AND region_priority = pr AND data_confidence = pd AND name < pn))), '0 = pass'
  UNION ALL SELECT 943, 'verify_next_size', 'INFO: gate-passers not yet verified (mart.verify_next)',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.verify_next), 'Information: work this queue top-down'
  UNION ALL SELECT 944, 'org_without_segment', 'Orgs (any universe) with no segment',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_master m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mart.org_segment g WHERE g.org_uuid = m.uuid AND g.segment IS NOT NULL)), '0 = pass. Nobody silently dropped'
  UNION ALL SELECT 945, 'passer_without_tier', 'Gate-passers with no tier',
    (SELECT count(*) FROM mart.org_segment WHERE passes_all AND tier IS NULL), '0 = pass'

p='70_mart_segments.sql'
s=open(p).read()
notes="""--   Tier 1   >= 40   AE works these now          (47 accounts)
--   Tier 2   25-39    SDR sequence, AE joins on reply (76)
--   Tier 3   14-24    automated nurture, promote on a trigger such as a new round (136)
--   Nurture  < 14     watch list; re-score on new data (349)
-- WHY (the v4 total is 0-110 over the 608 orgs that pass every gate; counts as built):
--   * The top of the distribution is thin: only 3 orgs score 72+, 13 score 52+, and the
--     counts per point are 9 at 49 and 9 at 41. 40 is the first round number below that 41
--     cluster and gives 47 accounts, about the size a 3-person AE team can work in a
--     quarter (the aim was 40-60). 45 would leave 32, 50 would leave 15: too few to staff.
--   * 238 orgs sit at exactly 9 points: nothing known except a headcount band. That is the
--     "no signal" mass, not a lead list. 14 is the first score above it that needs at least
--     one real fact (a round, a revenue band, a growth reading or a fit bonus), so Tier 3
--     starts at 14 and everything below is Nurture.
--   * 25 splits the 14-39 middle so Tier 2 (76) is a size an SDR sequence can cover and
--     Tier 3 (136) is the automated nurture. 25 is also the revenue sweet-spot value, a
--     round number with no gap to anchor on (the score is a sum of small pieces).
--   * The scale changed from v3 (0-100, tag-based points) to v4 (0-110, rubric), and the
--     population changed (gates remove 80%), so v3's 65/52/42 cannot be reused.
--   * Headcount growth is 0 for everyone until PDL enrichment runs (up to +20), so these
--     cutoffs are expected to be RE-PICKED after enrichment; scores will rise for fast
--     growers. History in ops.score_history shows the before and after."""
s=s.replace("--@@TIER_NOTES@@",notes)
s=s.replace("('Tier 1', 0, 1), ('Tier 2', 0, 2), ('Tier 3', 0, 3), ('Nurture', 0, 4)","('Tier 1', 40, 1), ('Tier 2', 25, 2), ('Tier 3', 14, 3), ('Nurture', 0, 4)")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='00_schemas.sql'

open(p,'w').write(s)
E

  -> raw JSON to data/enrich/pdl/<org_uuid>.json -> parsed row appended to
  src/white_circle/seeds/headcount_history.csv (committed provenance, read by 56_).

WHAT THE PDL DOCS CONFIRMED (read 2026-10-30 on docs.peopledatalabs.com):
  * Endpoint: GET https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich, key in header X-Api-Key.
  * Match inputs: at least one of pdl_id, name, ticker, website, profile; website wins for
    us (a clean domain). min_likelihood 1-10 (default 2); we send 5 to avoid wrong-company
    matches. required, titlecase also exist.
  * Response: company fields are TOP LEVEL (not under "data"), plus status and likelihood
    (1-10). Fields without data are null.
  * employee_count (int, current), employee_count_by_month (object, "YYYY-MM" -> int, end of
    month, from the first employee or 2010-01), employee_growth_rate (object with keys
    "3_month", "6_month", "12_month", "24_month"; each a float FRACTION, 0.0595 = +5.95%,
    can be negative, null if the company had zero employees at the window start).
  * Billing is "per match" (a 404 no-match is not a match, so presumably not billed).
  * Free plan: 10 requests per minute (paid 1,000/min); the pricing page says "up to 100
    monthly records" on the free plan.
ASSUMED / NOT CONFIRMED (verify with the first real call before trusting):
  * 1 credit per matched record. The docs pages I could reach do not state the credit
    amount, and the billing page was a 404. --max-credits therefore counts one credit per
    request that returns 200 and refuses to start a request that could exceed the cap.
  * That a 404 is free (inferred from "per match").
  * That the growth keys are present on the free tier and that employee_count_by_month
    reaches back 12 months for small companies.
  * The exact 404 body (not shown in the docs); we only rely on the HTTP status.
  * Parsing from the fixture below is tested; no real response has been seen (no key yet).

Every call is logged with obs.record_api_call. --dry-run (the default) prints the plan and
the request count and calls nothing. Needs env PDL_API_KEY only for a real run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import json
import os
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import typer

from .obs import record_api_call, track_run
from .paths import DB, ENRICH, HC_SEED

URL = "https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich"
MIN_LIKELIHOOD = 5
SEED_COLS = ["org_uuid", "pdl_id", "likelihood", "hc_current", "hc_3m_ago", "hc_6m_ago", "hc_12m_ago",
             "growth_3m_pct", "growth_6m_pct", "growth_12m_pct", "hc_source", "hc_fetched_at"]
FREE_RPM = 10  # free-plan rate limit: 10 requests / minute


def _month_back(ym: str, n: int) -> str:
    y, m = int(ym[:4]), int(ym[5:7])
    t = y * 12 + (m - 1) - n
    return f"{t // 12:04d}-{t % 12 + 1:02d}"


def parse_response(org_uuid: str, body: dict, fetched_at: datetime) -> dict | None:
    """One parsed seed row from a PDL company response, or None if it is not a match."""
    if not body or body.get("status") not in (None, 200) or not body.get("employee_count_by_month") \
            and body.get("employee_count") is None:
        return None
    by_month = body.get("employee_count_by_month") or {}
    cur_month = fetched_at.strftime("%Y-%m")

    def count_ago(n: int):
        v = by_month.get(_month_back(cur_month, n))
        return int(v) if v is not None else None

    cur = body.get("employee_count")
    cur = int(cur) if cur is not None else None
    rate = body.get("employee_growth_rate") or {}

    def pct(key: str):
        v = rate.get(key)
        return round(float(v) * 100, 2) if v is not None else None

    return {
        "org_uuid": org_uuid, "pdl_id": body.get("id"), "likelihood": body.get("likelihood"),
        "hc_current": cur, "hc_3m_ago": count_ago(3), "hc_6m_ago": count_ago(6), "hc_12m_ago": count_ago(12),
        "growth_3m_pct": pct("3_month"), "growth_6m_pct": pct("6_month"), "growth_12m_pct": pct("12_month"),
        "hc_source": "peopledatalabs", "hc_fetched_at": fetched_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    }


def _already_fetched() -> set[str]:
    done = {p.stem for p in ENRICH.glob("*.json")} if ENRICH.exists() else set()
    if HC_SEED.exists():
        with HC_SEED.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            done |= {r["org_uuid"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    return done


def plan_orgs() -> list[dict]:
    """Gate-passers, best PRE-GROWTH score first (growth would otherwise bias the order of a re-run)."""
    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
    try:
        cur = con.execute(
            "SELECT s.org_uuid, m.organization_name, m.domain, s.rubric_total - s.pts_growth + s.pts_bonus AS pre_growth "
            "FROM mart.org_score s JOIN mart.org_master m ON m.uuid = s.org_uuid "
            "ORDER BY pre_growth DESC, s.ord")
        cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
        rows = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]
    finally:
        con.close()
    done = _already_fetched()
    return [r for r in rows if r["org_uuid"] not in done]


def call_pdl(key: str, org: dict) -> tuple[int, dict, float]:
    q = {"min_likelihood": MIN_LIKELIHOOD}
    if org["domain"]:
        q["website"] = org["domain"]
    else:
        q["name"] = org["organization_name"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{URL}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(q)}", headers={"X-Api-Key": key})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode()), (time.time() - t0) * 1000
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        try:
            body = json.loads(e.read().decode())
        except Exception:
            body = {"status": e.code}
        return e.code, body, (time.time() - t0) * 1000


def enrich(limit: int | None = None, max_credits: int = 25, dry_run: bool = True) -> None:
    with track_run("enrich-headcount", {"limit": limit, "max_credits": max_credits, "dry_run": dry_run}) as run:
        todo = plan_orgs()
        n = min(len(todo), max_credits, limit if limit is not None else len(todo))
        batch = todo[:n]
        typer.echo(f"PDL company enrich: {len(todo)} gate-passers not yet fetched; this run would make {n} requests "
                   f"(cap: --max-credits {max_credits}, --limit {limit}); worst case {n} credits (1 per match assumed).")
        typer.echo(f"free plan: ~{FREE_RPM} requests/minute, so about {n / FREE_RPM:.1f} minutes of waiting.")
        for o in batch[:10]:
            typer.echo(f"  {o['pre_growth']:>3}  {o['organization_name'][:36]:<36} {o['domain'] or '(name match)'}")
        if n > 10:
            typer.echo(f"  ... and {n - 10} more")
        if dry_run:
            typer.echo("dry run: no API calls made, nothing written. Re-run with --no-dry-run and PDL_API_KEY set.")
            return
        key = os.environ.get("PDL_API_KEY")
        if not key:
            raise typer.BadParameter("PDL_API_KEY is not set")
        ENRICH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        HC_SEED.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        new = not HC_SEED.exists()
        spent = 0
        with HC_SEED.open("a", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=SEED_COLS, lineterminator="\n")
            if new:
                w.writeheader()
            for i, o in enumerate(batch, 1):
                if spent + 1 > max_credits:  # enforced in code, before the request
                    typer.echo(f"credit cap {max_credits} reached")
                    break
                status, body, ms = call_pdl(key, o)
                fetched = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
                (ENRICH / f"{o['org_uuid']}.json").write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=1))
                credit = 1 if status == 200 else 0
                spent += credit
                record_api_call(run.run_id, "peopledatalabs", "company/enrich",
                                f"{o['domain'] or o['organization_name']} (min_likelihood={MIN_LIKELIHOOD})",
                                status, ms, credit, None, f"pdl:{o['org_uuid']}", fetched)
                row = parse_response(o["org_uuid"], body, fetched) if status == 200 else None
                if row:
                    w.writerow(row)
                    f.flush()
                    run.add_rows(1)
                typer.echo(f"{i}/{len(batch)} {o['organization_name'][:30]:<30} HTTP {status} "
                           f"{'matched' if row else 'no match'}  credits {spent}/{max_credits}")
                time.sleep(60 / FREE_RPM + 0.1)

Feeds the v4 "headcount growth" component (20 points, 0 until this has run). Pipeline:
  gate-passers, best pre-growth score first -> skip orgs already fetched -> one GET each
  -> raw JSON to data/enrich/pdl/<org_uuid>.json -> parsed row appended to
  src/white_circle/seeds/headcount_history.csv (committed provenance, read by 56_).

WHAT THE PDL DOCS CONFIRMED (read 2026-10-30 on docs.peopledatalabs.com):
  * Endpoint: GET https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich, key in header X-Api-Key.
  * Match inputs: at least one of pdl_id, name, ticker, website, profile; website wins for
    us (a clean domain). min_likelihood 1-10 (default 2); we send 5 to avoid wrong-company
    matches. required, titlecase also exist.
  * Response: company fields are TOP LEVEL (not under "data"), plus status and likelihood
    (1-10). Fields without data are null.
  * employee_count (int, current), employee_count_by_month (object, "YYYY-MM" -> int, end of
    month, from the first employee or 2010-01), employee_growth_rate (object with keys
    "3_month", "6_month", "12_month", "24_month"; each a float FRACTION, 0.0595 = +5.95%,
    can be negative, null if the company had zero employees at the window start).
  * Billing is "per match" (a 404 no-match is not a match, so presumably not billed).
  * Free plan: 10 requests per minute (paid 1,000/min); the pricing page says "up to 100
    monthly records" on the free plan.
ASSUMED / NOT CONFIRMED (verify with the first real call before trusting):
  * 1 credit per matched record. The docs pages I could reach do not state the credit
    amount, and the billing page was a 404. --max-credits therefore counts one credit per
    request that returns 200 and refuses to start a request that could exceed the cap.
  * That a 404 is free (inferred from "per match").
  * That the growth keys are present on the free tier and that employee_count_by_month
    reaches back 12 months for small companies.
  * The exact 404 body (not shown in the docs); we only rely on the HTTP status.
  * Parsing from the fixture below is tested; no real response has been seen (no key yet).

Every call is logged with obs.record_api_call. --dry-run (the default) prints the plan and
the request count and calls nothing. Needs env PDL_API_KEY only for a real run.

URL = "https://api.peopledatalabs.com/v5/company/enrich"
MIN_LIKELIHOOD = 5
SEED_COLS = ["org_uuid", "pdl_id", "likelihood", "hc_current", "hc_3m_ago", "hc_6m_ago", "hc_12m_ago",
             "growth_3m_pct", "growth_6m_pct", "growth_12m_pct", "hc_source", "hc_fetched_at"]
FREE_RPM = 10  # free-plan rate limit: 10 requests / minute


def _month_back(ym: str, n: int) -> str:
    y, m = int(ym[:4]), int(ym[5:7])
    t = y * 12 + (m - 1) - n
    return f"{t // 12:04d}-{t % 12 + 1:02d}"


def parse_response(org_uuid: str, body: dict, fetched_at: datetime) -> dict | None:
    """One parsed seed row from a PDL company response, or None if it is not a match."""
    if not body or body.get("status") not in (None, 200) or not body.get("employee_count_by_month") \
            and body.get("employee_count") is None:
        return None
    by_month = body.get("employee_count_by_month") or {}
    cur_month = fetched_at.strftime("%Y-%m")

    def count_ago(n: int):
        v = by_month.get(_month_back(cur_month, n))
        return int(v) if v is not None else None

    cur = body.get("employee_count")
    cur = int(cur) if cur is not None else None
    rate = body.get("employee_growth_rate") or {}

    def pct(key: str):
        v = rate.get(key)
        return round(float(v) * 100, 2) if v is not None else None

    return {
        "org_uuid": org_uuid, "pdl_id": body.get("id"), "likelihood": body.get("likelihood"),
        "hc_current": cur, "hc_3m_ago": count_ago(3), "hc_6m_ago": count_ago(6), "hc_12m_ago": count_ago(12),
        "growth_3m_pct": pct("3_month"), "growth_6m_pct": pct("6_month"), "growth_12m_pct": pct("12_month"),
        "hc_source": "peopledatalabs", "hc_fetched_at": fetched_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    }


def _already_fetched() -> set[str]:
    done = {p.stem for p in ENRICH.glob("*.json")} if ENRICH.exists() else set()
    if HC_SEED.exists():
        with HC_SEED.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            done |= {r["org_uuid"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    return done


def plan_orgs() -> list[dict]:
    """Gate-passers, best PRE-GROWTH score first (growth would otherwise bias the order of a re-run)."""
    con = duckdb.connect(str(DB), read_only=True)
    try:
        cur = con.execute(
            "SELECT s.org_uuid, m.organization_name, m.domain, s.rubric_total - s.pts_growth + s.pts_bonus AS pre_growth "
            "FROM mart.org_score s JOIN mart.org_master m ON m.uuid = s.org_uuid "
            "ORDER BY pre_growth DESC, s.ord")
        cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
        rows = [dict(zip(cols, r)) for r in cur.fetchall()]
    finally:

    done = _already_fetched()
    return [r for r in rows if r["org_uuid"] not in done]

**Organization enrichment** costs **1 credit per organization**. Bulk organization enrichment is also 1 credit per organization.

name: WebFetch
text:
**Endpoint and auth**
- **Method and URL:** `GET https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/organizations/enrich`
- **Auth header:** `x-api-key: <your API key>`. OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens are also accepted for Apollo partners.
- **OAuth scope:** `organizations_enrich`
- **Access:** Works with an API key or Master API key. Free accounts need a work email registration, and paid accounts aren't affected.

**Query parameters** (all optional, but you must supply at least one identifier)
- `domain`: e.g., `apollo.io`. Omit `www.` and `@`.
- `linkedin_url`: e.g., `https://www.linkedin.com/company/apolloio`
- `website`: full URL, e.g., `http://www.apollo.io`
- `name`: improves match accuracy when combined with another identifier. The page conflicts on whether `name` alone is supported. The top-level summary says yes, but the endpoint's parameter description says name alone is not supported. Use another identifier to be safe.

**Headcount growth fields**
- `organization_headcount_six_month_growth`
- `organization_headcount_twelve_month_growth`
- `organization_headcount_twenty_four_month_growth`

These are numbers described as the "percentage change" in total headcount over the prior 6, 12, or 24 months. The example value is `12.3` for six months, which suggests percent rather than fraction, but the page doesn't state the unit explicitly. Each returns `null` when growth data isn't available.

**estimated_num_employees**
- Integer on the organization object (example: `1600`). The page gives no further definition. Each entry in `suborganizations` also has its own `estimated_num_employees`.

**Credit cost:** 1 credit per organization. For up to ten companies in one call, use the bulk organization enrichment endpoint.

**Rate limits:** These depend on your Apollo plan. The sample 429 response cites a limit of 600 calls per hour for this endpoint. Check your current limits with the view API usage stats endpoint.

**Error codes**
- **401:** Invalid API key (plain-text response).
- **403:** `API_INACCESSIBLE` / `AUTH.AUTHORIZATION.ENDPOINT_ACCESS_DENIED`. The key isn't authorized for this endpoint.
- **422:** `ORGANIZATION.VALIDATION.ORGANIZATION_IDENTIFIER_REQUIRED`. No usable identifier was sent.
- **429:** `USAGE.RATE_LIMIT.API_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. Includes a `window` context value and suggests waiting before retrying.

The legacy root-level error fields (`error`, `error_code`, `message`) are removed on 2027-02-16. After that date, parse `error_details.code` instead.

URL = "https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/organizations/enrich"
APOLLO_DIR = DATA / "enrich" / "apollo"
GROWTH_SCALE = 1.0  # see ASSUMED: docs example 12.3 reads as percent
SLEEP_S = 6.1       # 600/hour sample limit -> stay at ~590/hour


def parse_response(org_uuid: str, body: dict, fetched_at: datetime) -> dict | None:
    """One seed row from an Apollo response, or None when there is no usable match."""
    org = (body or {}).get("organization") if isinstance(body, dict) and "organization" in body else body
    if not isinstance(org, dict) or not org:
        return None
    cur = org.get("estimated_num_employees")
    g6 = org.get("organization_headcount_six_month_growth")
    g12 = org.get("organization_headcount_twelve_month_growth")
    if cur is None and g6 is None and g12 is None:
        return None

    def pct(v):
        return round(float(v) * GROWTH_SCALE, 2) if v is not None else None

    return {
        "org_uuid": org_uuid, "pdl_id": None, "likelihood": None,
        "hc_current": int(cur) if cur is not None else None,
        "hc_3m_ago": None, "hc_6m_ago": None, "hc_12m_ago": None,
        "growth_3m_pct": None, "growth_6m_pct": pct(g6), "growth_12m_pct": pct(g12),
        "hc_source": "apollo", "hc_fetched_at": fetched_at.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
    }


def plan_orgs() -> list[dict]:
    """Gate-passers by pre-growth score, minus orgs with a seed row from any source or a saved Apollo response."""
    done = {p.stem for p in APOLLO_DIR.glob("*.json")} if APOLLO_DIR.exists() else set()
    if HC_SEED.exists():
        with HC_SEED.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            done |= {r["org_uuid"] for r in csv.DictReader(f)}
    # enrich_pdl.plan_orgs also drops PDL raw files, which is right: those orgs were fetched elsewhere.
    return [r for r in _plan_all() if r["org_uuid"] not in done]


def call_apollo(key: str, org: dict) -> tuple[int, dict, float]:
    q = {"domain": org["domain"]} if org["domain"] else {"name": org["organization_name"]}
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{URL}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(q)}",
                                 headers={"x-api-key": key, "accept": "application/json",
                                          "Cache-Control": "no-cache"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as r:
            return r.status, json.loads(r.read().decode()), (time.time() - t0) * 1000
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raw = e.read().decode(errors="replace")
        try:
            body = json.loads(raw)
        except Exception:
            body = {"status": e.code, "text": raw[:300]}
        return e.code, body, (time.time() - t0) * 1000


def enrich(limit: int | None = None, max_credits: int = 60, dry_run: bool = True) -> None:
    with track_run("enrich-headcount-apollo", {"limit": limit, "max_credits": max_credits, "dry_run": dry_run}) as run:
        todo = plan_orgs()
        n = min(len(todo), max_credits, limit if limit is not None else len(todo))
        batch = todo[:n]
        typer.echo(f"Apollo org enrich: {len(todo)} gate-passers without headcount data; this run would make {n} "
                   f"requests (cap: --max-credits {max_credits}, --limit {limit}); worst case {n} credits (1 each).")
        typer.echo(f"pacing {SLEEP_S}s/request (600/hour sample limit): about {n * SLEEP_S / 60:.1f} minutes. "
                   "growth_3m_pct stays NULL (Apollo has no 3-month figure).")
        for o in batch[:10]:
            typer.echo(f"  {o['pre_growth']:>3}  {o['organization_name'][:36]:<36} {o['domain'] or '(name only)'}")
        if n > 10:
            typer.echo(f"  ... and {n - 10} more")
        if dry_run:
            typer.echo("dry run: no API calls made, nothing written. Re-run with --no-dry-run and APOLLO_API_KEY set.")
            return

# Memo notes — points the owner wants made

Collected during the build; the memo draft must cover each one.

## Scoring model is a set of stated assumptions, refined by results (owner, 2026-10-30)

> "i think we can call out our assumption but mention we would refine over time with realized
> results. if we are consistently performing better for companies that have recent headcount
> growht despite no new funding, we can rebalance the scoring model. also worth calling out that
> we would rescore companies periodically"

- The 40/25/15/20 weights and the fit bonus are **priors**, chosen up front and stated openly.
- Once we have results, we check each component against what actually happened (meetings booked,
  opportunities, wins). Example: if companies with recent headcount growth but no new round keep
  converting better, growth gets more weight and funding recency gets less.
- **Rescoring runs periodically.** Every company is rescored on a schedule and whenever a new signal
  arrives (new round, headcount change, verification). Each score carries `score_version` and a
  scored-at date, so a past ranking can always be reproduced.

## Two-stage enrichment: baseline for everyone, deep dive for the top 5 (owner, 2026-10-30)

> "i think its worth also calling out that we want to have a baseline enrichment to score
> properly and then do a deep dive - with contact data joined in and a full report on each
> company - for the top 5 (like they ask for in step 2 of part 1)"

- **Baseline enrichment (broad, cheap, feeds the score):** a website check (does the company ship
  customer-facing AI, its real industry, is the site live) and headcount history. These are only
  the fields the gates and rubric need, run on every candidate. Cost per company is cents.
- **Deep dive (narrow, expensive, feeds the AE):** the top 5 only. Contacts are joined in, and each
  company gets a full report the AE can act on. This is Part 1 step 2.
- Why split it: spending deep-research effort on a company before we know it's a fit wastes money
  and pads the CRM with stale detail. The score decides who earns the deep dive.

## Model shape (owner, 2026-10-30)

- Gates first: closed, non-AI, poorly matched industries (plus acquired/nonprofit/public/
  competitor/services/dead site).
- Rubric: recent funding 40, revenue 25, headcount 15, headcount growth 20.
- Fit bonus ≤10, based on what White Circle already signals publicly: "we want to use what they
  have already done as baseline for how we shape our response".
- Region (Europe + North America) is a **tie-breaker only**. Same time zones and selling customs.

Exit code 1
# How the approach changed

Short version: every change to the scoring came from looking at real rows. Either the data showed
a problem, or what White Circle actually sells did.

1. **Profile first.** The data was cleaner than "messy" suggested: no duplicates, no orphan records,
   consistent codes. The real traps were about meaning. 73% of companies have no funding rows,
   106 "active" companies had actually been acquired, 29 were public giants, and two-thirds carry an
   "AI" tag, so the tag tells you almost nothing.

2. **v1: one additive score.** It mixed AI signal, regulated industry, funding, size, region and
   contacts. The top of the list exposed the problems. "Regulated" swept in crypto, fitness and
   government. Dev shops ranked high. Debt rounds counted as fresh funding.

3. **v2: fix the definitions.** Regulated narrowed to banking, insurance, health and legal. Agencies
   were capped. Recency counts equity rounds only. Then an owner challenge: *do traditional
   finance or non-AI companies fit at all?* Research on White Circle's site said no. Every page
   starts from "what AI system do you run". So shipping AI became a requirement, not a bonus.

4. **v3: check the websites.** Crunchbase tags couldn't tell a carbon-reduction startup from a
   fintech. We read the live homepage of the 180 strongest candidates and labelled each one with a
   verbatim quote: does it ship customer-facing AI, what is its real industry. That replaced 29 of
   the top 50: 9 didn't actually ship an LLM, 7 had dead or hijacked sites, and the rest were
   outranked. It also surfaced 3 competitors (agent control planes, AI gateways). Rule from then
   on: **no company enters the top 50 unverified.**

5. **v4: gates, then a fixed rubric.** Exclusions are now pass/fail, applied before any points:
   closed, acquired, non-AI, wrong industry, competitor, services firm, dead site. The survivors
   are scored on a fixed rubric: recent funding 40, revenue 25, headcount 15, headcount growth 20.
   A fit bonus of up to 10 is anchored on the industries and use cases White Circle already
   markets. Region (Europe and North America) breaks ties only. On the real data, 608 of 3,000 companies
   pass all nine gates (no language-AI product removes 1,578 and services firms 494). 10 of the v3.1 top 50
   changed: 3 now fail the industry gate and 7 pass but score too low to stay.

**What stays open.** The weights are starting assumptions. Once meetings and deals come in, each
component gets checked against real outcomes. For example: if headcount growth without a new
round converts better than a fresh raise, the weights shift. Scores are versioned and rescored on
a schedule, so every past ranking can be reproduced.

Enrichment is two-stage: a cheap baseline for every company, a deep dive for the top 5 and for deals.   COMPANY ||--o{ DEAL : has

--       equity_rounds_count / _usd  venture equity only (round_group = 'equity_venture')
--       first_round_date            earliest round of any kind
--       last_equity_date/type/amount  the latest EQUITY round (same-day ties: later stage)
--       months_since_last_equity    whole months from that date to as_of (2026-10-29)

## 58
-- 58_mart_org_gate.sql  ->  mart.org_gate, mart.gate_funnel
--
-- STAGE 1 OF SCORE v4: exclusion gates. Nine yes/no tests, evaluated IN THIS ORDER. An
-- org is a candidate only if it trips NONE of them. A gate that is TRUE means the org is
-- EXCLUDED by that rule. Every gate is computed for every org (so an org's full record
-- of failures is visible), and first_failed_gate records the first one in the order
-- below, which is the reason shown in the segment "Out: <gate>".
--
--   1 is_closed              Crunchbase says the company shut down. Nobody to sell to.
--   2 is_acquired            Acquired (or funding_stage m_and_a). The buyer is now the
--                            parent company; it is a different account and a different deal.
--   3 is_nonprofit           Non-profits buy on grants and do not match the commercial motion.
--   4 is_public              Publicly listed. NOT discarded as junk: these form the separate

--   5 is_competitor          Sells guardrails / AI-safety / red-teaming / LLM security (tags,

--   6 is_services_firm       Agency, consultancy, dev shop: builds LLM apps FOR clients and

# Part 1 memo: who White Circle should call first

Of 3,000 Crunchbase companies, 608 are real candidates and 47 are Tier 1. My top five are Replit, Shapes, Botpress, Dash0 and Kinfolk. Below is how I got there. The full ranking is in [top50.csv](top50.csv) and the [dashboard](../dashboard/index.html).

## 1. What "good fit" means

White Circle sells runtime protection for companies that ship LLMs and agents to their own customers. Its public pages all start from the same question: what AI system do you run? The only named customer is Lovable, which sends every session through White Circle to catch abuse and supervise agents. The company also cites digital banks and neobanks, and its own philosophy page says that under the EU AI Act deployers carry their own obligations.

So a good fit is a company that ships a language-AI product to its own users, ideally one that acts (agents), in a place where a bad answer is expensive. It must also be able to buy: alive, independent, funded and big enough. A company that merely carries an "AI" tag, or one that sells AI services to others, is not a fit. I treat that as a requirement, not a bonus.

## 2. The data and how I handled it

The data was cleaner than "messy" suggested: no duplicates, no orphan records, consistent codes. The traps were about meaning:

- 73% of companies have no funding rows, so every join is a LEFT JOIN.
- 106 "active" companies had been acquired, and 29 were public giants.
- Two-thirds carry an "AI" tag, so the tag says almost nothing.
- Debt and grants are not "fresh funding".

All of it is plain SQL in [src/white_circle/sql](../../src/white_circle/sql/). Files 57 (master table), 58 (gates), 60 (score) and 70 (segments) carry the logic. Each has a header explaining the why, and every point value is looked up in a weights table rather than typed into the query. [approach-evolution.md](approach-evolution.md) shows how the model changed from v1 to v4 after I looked at real rows.

## 3. The model: gates first, then a fixed rubric

Exclusions are pass/fail and come before any points. Nobody is dropped silently; every company keeps a reason.

| Gate (in order) | Removed |
|---|---|
| Closed | 72 |
| Acquired | 106 |
| Non-profit | 17 |
| Public (kept as an Enterprise segment) | 26 |
| Competitor | 7 |
| Services firm | 494 |
| Dead or hijacked site | 28 |
| No language-AI product | 1,578 |
| Industry not matched | 64 |
| **Pass** | **608** |

The survivors get a fixed rubric out of 110:

| Component | Max | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Funding recency (equity only) | 40 | A fresh round means budget and new hires |
| Revenue | 25 | Can afford a contract |
| Headcount | 15 | Enough scale to run agents in production |
| Headcount growth | 20 | Momentum, even without a new round |
| Fit bonus | up to 10 | Taken from White Circle's own landing pages and named customers: the verticals it markets, plus agents that take actions |

Region (Europe plus North America) breaks ties only, because of shared time zones and selling customs. It earns no points.

## 4. Segments and tiers

Segment is who they are, and decides the play. Tier is how soon to work them.

| Segment | Count | Tier | Total /110 | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI-native builders | 472 | Tier 1 | 40 and above | 47 |
| Marketed verticals | 109 | Tier 2 | 25 to 39 | 76 |
| Regulated GenAI | 27 | Tier 3 | 14 to 24 | 136 |
| | | Nurture | below 14 | 349 |

Public companies sit in a separate Enterprise segment because they run a different sales motion.

## 5. Top 50 and top 5

Every company in the top 50 was checked against its live website, with a quote as evidence. In total 186 companies were verified through Tavily. Two high scorers, Centrical and Audion, failed that check and were removed. Account briefs are in [accounts/](accounts/).

- **Replit (77):** a $400M Series D at $9B, and an agent that writes code and touches live infrastructure. The most agentic account here, and a close match to Lovable.
[redacted line: denylist]
- **Botpress (64):** its support agents issue refunds. It is partner-first, since embedding White Circle would cover all its customers, but it already markets guardrails, so competitor risk is real.
- **Dash0 (57):** a $110M Series B and tool-using Agent0 agents. Buyer first, with some competitor risk because it has said it will acquire in AI security.
- **Kinfolk (57):** a seed-stage company whose HR agents write to HRIS records at Deliveroo. It is raising for payroll and IT access, which widens the risk.

## 6. Enrichment

Enrichment runs in two stages. First is a baseline for everyone: a website check (does it ship customer-facing AI, what is its real industry, is the site live) and headcount history. These are only the fields the gates and rubric need, at cents per company. Second is a deep dive for the top 5: contacts joined in and a full report per company that an AE can act on, as step 2 of Part 1 asks. I did not want to spend deep-research effort before knowing a company fits, or to pad the CRM with stale detail. The score decides who earns the deep dive. Total Tavily spend was about 85 credits across verification and the deep dives. The CRM side is in the [CRM model](../part1-crm-model/crm-data-model.md).

## 7. What I'd refine

- **The weights are priors.** 40/25/15/20 and the bonus are my stated assumptions, not findings. Once meetings, opportunities and wins come in, I would test each component against them. Example: if companies with recent headcount growth but no new round keep converting better, growth gets more weight and funding recency gets less.
- **Rescore on a schedule.** Every company is rescored periodically and whenever a new signal arrives (a round, a headcount change, a verification). Each score carries a `score_version` and a scored-at date, so any past ranking can be reproduced.
- **Fill in growth.** It is not populated yet. PDL rejected the signup, and an Apollo lookup is built and waiting for a key (Apollo has no 3-month figure). Until it runs, growth is 0 for everyone, so it shifts nobody's rank.
- **Narrow "AI-native".** At 472 it is too broad to be a single play.
- **Work the verify_next queue.** Only 63 of the 608 are verified so far. The rest of the list leans on tags until that queue is worked.
- The data is a June 2026 snapshot, so every score is as of that date.
EOF

# White Circle GTM take-home

Crunchbase extract in, ranked top-50 account list, Attio CRM data model and a systems-design note out, all reproducible from one DuckDB pipeline.

## View the dashboard

{{ARTIFACT_URL}}

Fallback: download `docs/dashboard/index.html` and open it in a browser. It is one self-contained file and works offline. Tabs: **Accounts** (segments, scoring, top 50, the five enriched dossiers) and **CRM model** (the Attio objects and fields; deep link with `#crm`).

## Where each deliverable is

| Brief item | Where |
|---|---|
| Part 1.1 Segments, scoring model, top 50 | SQL in `src/white_circle/sql/` (`50_`-`70_`), list in `docs/part1-segmentation/top50.csv`, dashboard Accounts tab |
| Part 1.2 Top-5 enrichment | `docs/part1-segmentation/accounts/` (one `.md` and one `.json` dossier per account: Replit, Shapes, Botpress, Dash0, Kinfolk) |
| Part 1.3 Memo | `docs/part1-segmentation/memo.md` |
| Part 1.4 CRM data model | `docs/part1-crm-model/crm-data-model.md`, `crm_model.json`, `attio_upsert_example.json`; export SQL `src/white_circle/sql/80_crm_export.sql` |
| Part 1.5 Code, SQL, schema, notes, AI traces | `src/white_circle/`, `docs/part1-segmentation/data-profile.md` and `approach-evolution.md`, `docs/traces/` |
| Part 2 Workflow diagram and note | `docs/part2-systems-design/system-design.md`, diagram `docs/dashboard/workflow.svg` |
| The brief and our research on White Circle | `docs/context/` |

## How it works

1. DuckDB layers: `raw` (faithful VARCHAR copy of the CSVs) -> `stg` (typed, cleaned) -> `mart` (features, gates, score, segments, top 50) -> `crm` (Attio-shaped export). `dq` holds the checks.
2. Hard gates first (closed, acquired, non-profit, services firm, dead site, not AI, industry not matched), then a points rubric on funding recency, revenue, headcount, growth and fit to White Circle's own positioning.
3. Tavily verification: every gate-passing candidate's website was checked for what the product actually ships; the labels are committed as `src/white_circle/seeds/company_review.csv` and feed the score.
4. Every run and every external API call is logged to `ops.run` and `ops.api_call` (provider, credits, latency).
5. Scores are written to `ops.score_history` on each build so a rubric change is visible as a diff, not a silent overwrite.

## Reproduce it

```
uv sync
[redacted line: outside-scope]
# put organizations.csv, funding_rounds.csv, contacts.csv in data/raw/
make                     # load, merge-reviews, build, dq, top50, dashboard
```

The raw CSVs are not committed: they are the brief's licensed dataset. Verification labels are committed in `src/white_circle/seeds/`, so the build is deterministic without re-scraping. Equivalent commands: `uv run whitecircle load && uv run whitecircle merge-reviews && uv run whitecircle build && uv run whitecircle dq && uv run whitecircle top50 && uv run whitecircle dashboard`. Note: `merge-reviews` needs the review files in `data/verify/`; a reviewer without them can skip it, since the seed is already committed.

-- 50_mart_score_weights.sql  ->  mart.params, mart.vertical_gate, mart.score_weight, mart.fit_bonus_rule
--
-- SCORE v4. THE ONE PLACE the scoring opinion lives. The model has two stages:
--   1. EXCLUSION GATES (58_): yes/no rules. An org that trips ANY gate is out, and the
--      first gate it trips is recorded. Gates never score; they only remove.
--   2. A FIXED POINTS RUBRIC (60_) for the orgs that pass every gate. Every point value
--      is read from this file. No weights are written anywhere else.
-- Re-weighting = edit this file and run `whitecircle build`.
--
-- THE WEIGHTS ARE STATED PRIORS. They encode a hypothesis about who buys an AI-control
-- product, they are NOT fitted to closed-won data (the extract has no customer flag),
-- and they are meant to be RECALIBRATED against realized results.
-- Example of what a recalibration would look like: if companies with strong recent
-- headcount growth but NO new funding round keep converting better than the funding
-- recency weight predicts, move points from "funding recency" to "headcount growth".
-- To make that possible, every scoring run is appended to ops.score_history (61_, shown
-- as mart.score_history) with the exact inputs, the points per component and a
-- timestamp, so a past ranking can be reproduced and compared with what happened.
--
-- RUBRIC (100 points) plus FIT BONUS (up to 10) = 110:
--   Funding recency   40  last EQUITY round: money recently raised means budget now
--   Revenue range     25  can they pay for an enterprise tool
--   Headcount         15  big enough to have a product + security team, small enough to buy quickly
--   Headcount growth  20  a company that is hiring fast is shipping fast (PDL; 0 until enriched)
--   Fit bonus      0-10   White Circle's own landing pages and press, see fit_bonus_rule below
-- REGION earns NO points. White Circle sells in Europe and North America, so region
-- only breaks ties in the ranking (eu_uk and us_ca first, see 60_).
--
-- mart.params: as_of is pinned (not current_date) so the ranking never drifts with the
-- day it is run. The snapshot's latest round is 2026-06-20.
CREATE TABLE mart.params AS
SELECT DATE '2026-10-29' AS as_of, 'v4' AS score_version;

-- mart.vertical_gate: which industries pass gate 9 (industry_not_matched), and why.
-- "Vertical" is the org's industry after the website check (verified) or, if never
-- checked, after the Crunchbase tags (55_). 'ai_native' is not a Crunchbase industry:
-- 57_ assigns it to an org that SHIPS an LLM / agent as its product and sits in a
-- horizontal sector (generic_tech / ai_platform / devtools) instead of an industry,
-- i.e. the Lovable-style builders.
--   regulated core       fintech_banking, insurance, health, legal_compliance
  ('revenue', 'ge_100m',   20, 'Stated prior. $100M and up: can pay, but enterprise procurement drag slows the deal.'),
  ('revenue', 'unknown',    0, 'Revenue band not on file (60% of orgs): unknown, scored 0.'),
  -- Headcount (max 15): employee_count_range decoded (10_) -------------------------------
  ('headcount', '1-10',      3, 'Stated prior. Too small to have a budget line for this.'),
  ('headcount', '11-50',     8, 'Stated prior. Small team; founder-led buying.'),
  ('headcount', '51-200',   15, 'Stated prior. Product team and security review, quick to buy.'),
  ('headcount', '201-500',  15, 'Stated prior. Same. The Crunchbase band 101-250 straddles the 200 line; both sides score 15, so the band edge does not matter.'),
  ('headcount', '501-1000', 12, 'Stated prior. Larger: slower to buy.'),
  ('headcount', '1001+',     8, 'Stated prior. Enterprise-size: long cycles, likely to build in-house.'),
  ('headcount', 'unknown',   0, 'Headcount not on file: unknown, scored 0.'),
  -- Headcount growth (max 20): People Data Labs, see enrich_pdl.py. 0 until enriched. -----
  ('growth_12m', 'ge_50',     12, 'Stated prior. 12-month headcount growth of 50% or more.'),
  ('growth_12m', '20_50',      8, 'Stated prior. 12-month growth 20% to under 50%.'),
  ('growth_12m', '0_20',       4, 'Stated prior. 12-month growth 0% to under 20%.'),
  ('growth_12m', 'negative',   0, 'Shrinking over 12 months.'),
  ('growth_6m',  'ge_20',      4, 'Stated prior. Add-on: 6-month growth of 20% or more (the growth is recent).'),
  ('growth_3m',  'ge_10',      4, 'Stated prior. Add-on: 3-month growth of 10% or more (accelerating now). Cannot be earned while Apollo is the headcount source (no 3-month figure).'),
  ('growth_total_cap', 'cap', 20, 'The three growth parts are capped at 20 together.'),
  -- Fit bonus cap [REDACTED_SECRET]
  ('fit_bonus_cap', 'cap',    10, 'The bonus from fit_bonus_rule is capped at 10.')
) AS w(component, level, points, rationale);

  s.rubric_total, s.score_version, s.scored_at, s.data_confidence,
  s.pts_recency                              AS score_component_funding_recency,
  s.pts_revenue                              AS score_component_revenue,
  s.pts_headcount                            AS score_component_headcount,
  s.pts_growth                               AS score_component_headcount_growth,
